5.1.1: We meditate on Śiva, the Full, who, endowed with the quality of sattva, sustains the worlds; who, resorting to rajas, is the creator; who, joined with tamas, is the destroyer; who abides beyond Māyā, which possesses the guṇas; who is truth and bliss, of infinite awareness, stainless, the ground of names such as Brahmā, eternal, and realised through union with sattva. ॥1॥
5.1.2: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, greatly wise disciple of Vyāsa, salutation to you. You have recited to us the fourth compilation, called the Koṭirudra Saṃhitā. ॥2॥
5.1.3: Now tell us the story of Śambhu, the Supreme Self, together with Ambā, endowed with the various narratives contained within the Umā Saṃhitā. ॥3॥
5.1.4: Sūta said: O great sages headed by Śaunaka, listen with love to the auspicious, divine, supreme story of Śaṅkara, which grants both enjoyment and liberation. ॥4॥
5.1.5: When Vyāsa, the best of sages, had asked Sanatkumāra such a holy question, Sanatkumāra sang the excellent story of Śiva. ॥5॥
5.1.6: Sanatkumāra said: O Vyāsa, I shall now tell that story of the Great Lord which the great sage Upamanyu related to Vāsudeva. ॥6॥
5.1.7: Long ago Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, went to Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṅkara, to perform austerities to Śiva for the sake of a son. ॥7॥
5.1.8: There, seeing Upamanyu performing austerities on the highest peak, he bowed to the sage with devotion and, with joined palms, questioned him. ॥8॥
5.1.9: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Upamanyu, greatly wise, foremost of Śaivas, noble-minded one, I have come here for the sake of a son, to perform austerities to Giriśa. ॥9॥
5.1.10: O sage, tell me the greatness of Śaṅkara, which brings constant bliss, hearing which I may with devotion perform the supreme austerity directed to the Lord. ॥10॥
5.1.11: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the wise Vāsudeva, Upamanyu, serene in mind, replied, remembering Śiva. ॥11॥
5.1.12: Upamanyu said: Listen, O Kṛṣṇa, great Śaiva, to the glory of the Great Lord Śambhu, which I beheld — supreme, and increasing devotion. ॥12॥
5.1.13: While engaged in austerity I beheld Śaṅkara and his weapons, and his entire retinue, the immortals headed by Viṣṇu and others. ॥13॥
5.1.14: I saw his weapon, shining with three parts, of unceasing bliss, imperishable, one-footed, great-tusked, with mouths devouring flames as mouthfuls; ॥14॥
5.1.15: blazing exceedingly with the light of two thousand rays, the foremost of all weapons, irresistible, many-eyed, thousand-footed; ॥15॥
5.1.16: which at the end of the kalpa surely destroys the universe, and for which nothing in the three worlds, moving or unmoving, would be unslayable. ॥16॥
5.1.17: Released from Maheśvara's arm, it burned up swiftly the entire three worlds, moving and unmoving, within half a blink — there is no doubt. ॥17॥
5.1.18: Engaged in austerity, I saw his imperishable, secret, supreme weapon standing at Rudra's side, to which nothing anywhere is equal or superior. ॥18॥
5.1.19: I saw that weapon of the Trident-bearer, famed in all worlds as the Śūla, named Vijaya, exceedingly fierce, destroyer of all weapons and missiles, ॥19॥
5.1.20: which could split the whole earth, which could dry up the great ocean, which could bring down the entire circle of the luminaries — there is no doubt of this; ॥20॥
5.1.21: by which, long ago, Māndhātṛ, son of Yuvanāśva, was slain together with his army — the universal emperor of great splendour, the king who had conquered the three worlds; ॥21॥
5.1.22: and the Haihaya, filled with pride; and the demon Lavaṇa was cast down, having challenged King Śatrughna to battle on every side. ॥22॥
5.1.23: That which, when that demon perished, returned to Rudra's hand — that is the trident, sharp-pointed, great, producing terror, ॥23॥
5.1.24: standing as if threatening, having formed a three-lined frown; like a smokeless fire, like the newly risen morning sun. ॥24॥
5.1.25: I saw the indescribable one with a serpent in hand, like Death with noose in hand; and the sharp-edged axe, adorned with serpents and other things, ॥25॥
5.1.26: resembling the fire at the end of the kalpa and having the form of a person — that axe of Bhārgava Rāma which made an end of the kṣatriyas in battle; ॥26॥
5.1.27: relying on whose power — it having been given by Śiva — the sage Rāma, exultant, long ago burned the kṣatriya race thrice seven times. ॥27॥
5.1.28: Likewise I beheld the discus Sudarśana, mighty, thousand-faced, two-thousand-armed, divine, having the form of a person, ॥28॥
5.1.29: two-thousand-eyed, blazing, crowded with a thousand feet, resplendent like ten million suns, able to burn the three worlds. ॥29॥
5.1.30: I saw the thunderbolt, greatly blazing, sharp, hundred-jointed, unsurpassed; and the great bow Pināka with its quiver, of great brilliance; ॥30॥
5.1.31: I saw the spear, the sword, and the noose, greatly blazing, together with the goad; and the great divine mace, and other weapons. ॥31॥
5.1.32: And likewise whatever weapons belong to the guardians of the worlds — all of them I beheld beside the blessed Rudra. ॥32॥
5.1.33: On the god's right side stood Brahmā, grandsire of the worlds, mounted on a divine aerial chariot yoked with swans and swift as thought. ॥33॥
5.1.34: And on his left side stood Nārāyaṇa, bearer of conch, discus and mace, likewise mounted on Vainateya (Garuḍa). ॥34॥
5.1.35: The Manus headed by Svāyambhuva, the sages headed by Bhṛgu, and the gods headed by Śakra — all came together. ॥35॥
5.1.36: Skanda, holding his spear, seated on a peacock and bearing a bell, stood near the Goddess like a second fire. ॥36॥
5.1.37: Nandī, holding a trident, stood before Bhava; and all the hosts of beings and the various Mothers were stationed there. ॥37॥
5.1.38: Then those gods, having saluted Maheśāna and surrounded him on all sides, praised Mahādeva with various hymns. ॥38॥
5.1.39: Whatever is seen or heard in this world — beholding all of it beside the Lord, I was utterly amazed; ॥39॥
5.1.40: then, summoning very great composure, with joined palms praising him with various hymns, I became immersed in supreme bliss in that worship, O Kṛṣṇa. ॥40॥
5.1.41: Seeing Śaṅkara before me, I, filled with faith, worshipped him properly according to rule, with a voice choked with tears. ॥41॥
5.1.42: Then the Lord Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, greatly pleased, spoke to me affectionately in a sweet voice, as if smiling. ॥42॥
5.1.43: O brahmin, you could not be shaken by me, though tested again and again. Good fortune to you. You are firm and endowed with devotion. ॥43॥
5.1.44: Therefore I am fully pleased with you; choose a boon, O you of good vows. Even what is hard to obtain among all the gods—nothing is withheld from you. ॥44॥
5.1.45: Hearing those words of Śambhu, full of true love, I, with joined palms, spoke to that god who is compassionate to his devotees. ॥45॥
5.1.46: Upamanyu said: O Lord, if you are pleased, if my devotion is steady, then by that truth may I have knowledge encompassing the three times. ॥46॥
5.1.47: Grant me abundant, unwavering devotion to you; and may there always be plenty of milk and rice for me together with my lineage. ॥47॥
5.1.48: May your presence always be in my hermitage, O all-pervading one; may there be friendship with your devotees, and may it always be mutual. ॥48॥
5.1.49: Thus addressed by me, Śambhu, the Supreme Lord, laughing, looked at me at once with a compassionate glance and spoke, O best of the Yadus. ॥49॥
5.1.50: Śrī Śiva said: O Upamanyu, O sage, dear child, you will be free from the defects born of old age and death; be endowed with all desires. ॥50॥
5.1.51: You will be worthy of worship by sages, endowed with fame and wealth; by my grace you will have virtue, beauty, good qualities and lordship at every step. ॥51॥
5.1.52: The presence of the Ocean of Milk itself, the treasury of waters, will always be with you wherever you wish, O sage. ॥52॥
5.1.53: That milk will be of the nature of nectar; as long as it is sustained, you will thereby behold this Vaivasvata kalpa together with your kinsmen. ॥53॥
5.1.54: And may your lineage be imperishable forever by my grace; I will make my presence in your hermitage, O great sage. ॥54॥
5.1.55: May your devotion to me be very steady; I will always grant you my sight when remembered by you, dear child. You are in every way dear to me. ॥55॥
5.1.56: Dwell in happiness as you desire; you should not feel anxious longing. May all that you have thought of come to complete fulfilment—there is no doubt of this. ॥56॥
5.1.57: Upamanyu said: Having spoken thus and granted the boons, the Lord Maheśāna, radiant like ten million suns, vanished right there. ॥57॥
5.1.58: Thus, O Kṛṣṇa, was Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, giver of enjoyment and liberation, seen by me together with his retinue. ॥58॥
5.1.59: Whatever was spoken by that wise Śambhu, the Supreme Lord, all of it I have attained through meditative absorption, O god of gods. ॥59॥
5.1.60: See before your very eyes the Gandharvas and Apsarases who have appeared, and likewise the sages, Vidyādharas and Siddhas stationed here. ॥60॥
5.1.61: See the delightful trees, with glossy leaves and sweet fragrance, laden with the flowers of all seasons, ever bearing blossoms and fruits. ॥61॥
5.1.62: All this, O mighty-armed one, the whole world filled with its being, exists by the grace of the great-souled Śaṅkara, the god of gods. ॥62॥
5.1.63: By the grace of the trident-bearer I possess all knowledge; I truly know everything—past, present and future. ॥63॥
5.1.64: I have seen that god whom even the gods, lords of the celestials, do not see without worshipping him. Who else is more blessed than I? ॥64॥
5.1.65: The supreme, eternal principle known as the twenty-sixth—thus do the wise meditate on the great, supreme, imperishable one. ॥65॥
5.1.66: He who knows the whole ordering of the principles, who beholds the meaning of all principles—he alone is the blessed god, the Lord of Pradhāna and Puruṣa. ॥66॥
5.1.67: It is the Lord who from his own right side created Brahmā, the cause of the worlds, and from his left side created Viṣṇu for the protection of the worlds. ॥67॥
5.1.68: And when the end of the kalpa arrived, the Lord created Rudra from his heart; then he withdrew the whole world, moving and unmoving. ॥68॥
5.1.69: At the end of the age, Mahādeva, having become Time, remains devouring all beings like the Saṃvartaka fire. ॥69॥
5.1.70: The all-knowing god, the Self of all beings, the source of the origin of all beings, abides all-pervading, to be seen by all the deities. ॥70॥
5.1.71: Therefore, worship Śaṅkara well for the sake of obtaining a son; Śiva, who loves his devotees, will quickly become gracious to you. ॥71॥
5.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The description of his own attainment, in the dialogue of Kṛṣṇa and Upamanyu, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
5.2.1: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of the great-souled sage Upamanyu, Kṛṣṇa, in whom devotion to Mahādeva had arisen, spoke to that sage. ॥1॥
5.2.2: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Upamanyu, O sage, dear one, show me your kindness: tell me of those who, having worshipped Śiva, obtained their desires. ॥2॥
5.2.3: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard this, the sage Upamanyu, great and foremost among Śaivas, a treasury of compassion, highly praised Kṛṣṇa's words and replied. ॥3॥
5.2.4: Upamanyu said: I shall tell you of those devotees by whom, through the worship of Bhava, the heart's desire was indeed obtained; listen, O best of the Yadus. ॥4॥
5.2.5: Long ago Hiraṇyakaśipu obtained from Śarva, the moon-crested one, lordship over all the immortals for ten lakhs of years. ॥5॥
5.2.6: Then his foremost son, renowned by the name Nandana, by a boon of Śarva fought Indra for ten thousand years. ॥6॥
5.2.7: And Viṣṇu's terrible discus and the thunderbolt of Ākhaṇḍala (Indra) were shattered against his limbs in that great battle long ago, O Kṛṣṇa. ॥7॥
5.2.8: Owing to his merit, no weapons—not even the discus, thunderbolt and the rest—made any impression on the body of that wise and exceedingly mighty seizer (graha) in battle. ॥8॥
5.2.9: The gods, oppressed by that very powerful seizer, later, having received boons from the God, struck down the lords of the asuras fiercely. ॥9॥
5.2.10: Pleased, Bhava, lord of all worlds, granted to Vidyutprabha too lordship over the three worlds for a hundred thousand years. ॥10॥
5.2.11: Likewise Śiva gave him ten thousand thousands of sons, and said: you shall always be my attendant. ॥11॥
5.2.12: The blessed Bhava, Śaṅkara, with delighted mind, lovingly gave him an auspicious kingdom in Kuśadvīpa, O Vāsudeva. ॥12॥
5.2.13: Long ago the daitya Śatamakha, created by Dhātṛ, performed austerities for a hundred years and obtained a thousand sons from Bhava. ॥13॥
5.2.14: The sage famed as Yājñavalkya, celebrated in the Vedas, obtained supreme knowledge by worshipping Mahādeva. ॥14॥
5.2.15: He who by name is Vedavyāsa and gained incomparable fame—he too, by worshipping Śaṅkara, obtained knowledge of the three times. ॥15॥
5.2.16: Those Vālakhilyas, humiliated by Indra, obtained from Śaṅkara Garuḍa, the stealer of Soma, invincible to all. ॥16॥
5.2.17: All the waters had vanished through the former wrath of Kapardin; the gods, having worshipped Śarva with the samakapāla offering, set them flowing again. ॥17॥
5.2.18: And Anasūyā, wife of Atri, fasting for three hundred years and lying upon pestles, then obtained sons from Śarva— ॥18॥
5.2.19: —she obtained the sage Dattātreya, Candra and likewise Durvāsas; and that devoted wife brought the Gaṅgā to flow at Citrakūṭa. ॥19॥
5.2.20: Vikarṇa too, having propitiated Mahādeva, the bringer of happiness to devotees, attained great perfection, O Madhusūdana. ॥20॥
5.2.21: King Citrasena, firm in devotion, having propitiated Śambhu, obtained fearlessness from the dread of all kings, and incomparable happiness. ॥21॥
5.2.22: Śrīkara, son of a cowherd woman, devotion to Mahādeva having arisen in him from watching a king's worship, attained the highest perfection. ॥22॥
5.2.23: Citrāṅgada, a king's son and husband of Sīmantinī, though submerged in the Yamunā, did not die, through Śiva's grace, O Hari. ॥23॥
5.2.24: And he, of good vows, went to the abode of Takṣaka, gained his friendship, and returned happily to his own home, endowed with manifold riches. ॥24॥
5.2.25: Sīmantinī, his beloved, devoted to the Monday vow, obtained supreme marital fortune through Śiva's grace, O Kṛṣṇa. ॥25॥
5.2.26: By the power of that vow, long ago a certain brahmin's son, who out of greed had deceitfully assumed the guise of a wife, actually became a woman. ॥26॥
5.2.27: Cañcukā, a wicked unchaste woman, long ago at Gokarṇa heard from a brahmin the sacred story of Śambhu and with devotion attained the highest state. ॥27॥
5.2.28: The sinner Binduga, Cañcukā's husband, through the grace of his own wife heard the Śiva Purāṇa and attained the good state belonging to Śaṅkara. ॥28॥
5.2.29: The famed courtesan Piṅgalā and the vile brahmin named Madara, having worshipped the Śaiva Ṛṣabha, both obtained a good state. ॥29॥
5.2.30: A certain courtesan named Mahānandā, devoted to Śiva's feet, having fully propitiated Śiva through her firm pledge, obtained a good state. ॥30॥
5.2.31: Kaikeyī, a brahmin girl also called Sādarā, devoted to Śiva's vow, attained supreme happiness by observing the vow of Śiva the Lord. ॥31॥
5.2.32: King Vimarṣaṇa too, having practised devotion to Śiva, attained the highest state long ago through Śiva's grace, O Kṛṣṇa. ॥32॥
5.2.33: King Durjana, a sinful villain lusting after many women, reached Śiva through devotion to Śiva, untainted in all his actions. ॥33॥
5.2.34: One named Śambara, together with his wife, a votary of Śiva's vow and devoted to Śaṅkara, delighting in pyre-ash, through devotion obtained his supreme state. ॥34॥
5.2.35: A cāṇḍāla woman named Saumini, having worshipped Śiva even unknowingly, obtained the Śaiva state through the supreme grace of Śaṅkara, O Kṛṣṇa. ॥35॥
5.2.36: A hunter named Mahākāla, a Kirāta who harmed others, having worshipped Śiva with devotion, obtained the supreme good state. ॥36॥
5.2.37: Durvāsas, tiger among sages, through Śiva's grace long ago spread in the world his own doctrine—devotion to Śiva, the giver of liberation. ॥37॥
5.2.38: And Kauśika, a kṣatriya, having worshipped Śaṅkara, benefactor of the world, became a brahmin, like a second lotus-born (Brahmā). ॥38॥
5.2.39: Having worshipped Śiva with true devotion, Virañci (Brahmā), best of Śaivas, became the creator and grandsire of all worlds, O Kṛṣṇa. ॥39॥
5.2.40: Mārkaṇḍeya, best of sages, glorious, foremost among Śiva's devotees, became long-lived and a great master through Śiva's grace, O Hari. ॥40॥
5.2.41: Indeed, O Kṛṣṇa, the king of the gods, a great devotee of Śiva, once enjoyed rule over the three worlds through Śiva's grace, as the mighty overlord of all the gods. ॥41॥
5.2.42: Bāṇa, the son of Bali, a great devotee of Śiva and self-controlled, through Śiva's grace became ruler of the cosmic egg and lord of all. ॥42॥
5.2.43: Hari, Śakti and Dadhīca, through true devotion and Śiva's grace, became great lords; likewise Rāma too was a devotee of Śaṅkara. ॥43॥
5.2.44: Kaṇāda, Bhārgava, the preceptor Bṛhaspati and Gautama too — through devotion to Śiva they became lords of great power. ॥44॥
5.2.45: Śākalya, of disciplined mind, worshipped Bhava with a mental sacrifice for as long as nine hundred years, O Mādhava. ॥45॥
5.2.46: The Lord was pleased and said: you will be an author of treatises; dear child, your fame will be undying and will prevail in the three worlds. ॥46॥
5.2.47: May your lineage be imperishable, adorned with great sages. O best of sages, you will be a composer of sūtras, and thereafter so will your son. ॥47॥
5.2.48: In this way that best of sages obtained a boon from Śaṅkara, and he became renowned throughout the three worlds and worthy of worship, O delight of the Yadus. ॥48॥
5.2.49: There was a sage renowned as Sāvarṇi in the Kṛta age; here he performed austerities for six thousand years. ॥49॥
5.2.50: Lord Rudra, appearing in person, said to him: I am pleased with you, O sinless one. You will be an author of treatises, renowned in the world, free from old age and death. ॥50॥
5.2.51: Such is Mahādeva; worshipped by those rich in prior merit, he then grants auspicious desires just as they wish. ॥51॥
5.2.52: With only one mouth I cannot tell the qualities of the Lord that exist, not even in hundreds of years. ॥52॥
5.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The instruction of Upamanyu, in the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and Vyāsa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
5.3.1: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard these words of his, he (Kṛṣṇa), struck with the greatest wonder, spoke to that great sage Upamanyu, whose mind was at peace. ॥1॥
5.3.2: Vāsudeva said: You are blessed, O best of brāhmaṇas! What accomplished person is able to praise you, in whose hermitage the God of the first gods himself makes his presence felt? ॥2॥
5.3.3: O tiger among sages, may that blessed Śiva grant me his sight; may he likewise bestow his grace upon me too. ॥3॥
5.3.4: Upamanyu said: In a very short time, without doubt, you will surely see Mahādeva by his grace alone, O Puruṣottama. ॥4॥
5.3.5: In the sixteenth month you will obtain excellent boons from Maheśvara. How would the god, together with his consort, not grant you boons, O Hari? ॥5॥
5.3.6: You are worthy of worship by all the deities and ever praiseworthy for your virtues. I shall tell you, who have faith, the mantra to be repeated, O Acyuta. ॥6॥
5.3.7: By the power of that repetition you will truly see Śaṅkara, and from Maheśvara you will obtain a son equal to yourself in strength. ॥7॥
5.3.8: The repetition is namaḥ śivāya — this king of mantras, O Hari, divine, granting all desires and bestowing both enjoyment and liberation. ॥8॥
5.3.9: Sanatkumāra said: While he was thus narrating stories concerning Mahādeva, eight days passed like a single moment, O ascetic. ॥9॥
5.3.10: When the ninth day arrived, he was initiated by the sage and taught the great Śaiva mantra of the Atharvaśiras. ॥10॥
5.3.11: At once he became a staff-bearer with shaven head, well concentrated, and he performed austerities, his body raised on the tip of his big toe and his arms held aloft. ॥11॥
5.3.12: When the sixteenth month arrived, the Supreme Lord Śambhu, pleased, together with Pārvatī, granted Kṛṣṇa his sight. ॥12॥
5.3.13: He saw the god accompanied by Pārvatī, three-eyed, moon-crested, being praised by Brahmā and others and worshipped by millions of siddhas; ॥13॥
5.3.14: wearing divine garlands and garments, especially bowed to by gods and demons humble with devotion, adorned with various ornaments; ॥14॥
5.3.15: full of every wonder, lovely, the great Lord, unborn and imperishable, attended by various gaṇas, pleased, the Master accompanied by his two sons. ॥15॥
5.3.16: Seeing Śaṅkara thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, his eyes wide with wonder, with joined palms, delighted and full of great joy, bowed down. ॥16॥
5.3.17: Then he worshipped him with words, with many kinds of hymns, and with bowed neck he praised the Lord of gods with the Thousand Names. ॥17॥
5.3.18: Then the gods, with the gandharvas, vidyādharas and great serpents, released a shower of flowers and words of applause pleasing to the mind. ॥18॥
5.3.19: And looking at Pārvatī's face, the blessed Lord, loving to his devotees, Rudra the great Lord, pleased, then spoke to Keśava. ॥19॥
5.3.20: Śrī Mahādeva said: Kṛṣṇa, I know you to be my devotee, ever firm in your vow towards me. Choose from me holy boons, hard to obtain in the three worlds. ॥20॥
5.3.21: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of his, Kṛṣṇa, with joined palms and reverence, bowing again and again, spoke to Śambhu, Lord of all. ॥21॥
5.3.22: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, I indeed ask of you excellent boons, eight in number, O Lord, as offered by you, O Maheśvara. ॥22॥
5.3.23: May my mind ever be in your dharma; may I have great and unshakable fame, nearness to you, and steady devotion to you always — thus I ask. ॥23॥
5.3.24: O Śambhu, may my wives indeed have sons, ten and more each; and may all enemies proud of their strength be slain in battle. ॥24॥
5.3.25: May I never suffer humiliation anywhere from an enemy, O Lord; and may I be exceedingly dear even to all yogins. ॥25॥
5.3.26: Grant these eight excellent boons, O God of gods; salutation to you. You alone are Lord of all, and especially my own Lord. ॥26॥
5.3.27: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of his, the blessed Bhava said to him, all this shall be; then the trident-bearer spoke to him again. ॥27॥
5.3.28: A mighty son named Sāmba, of great valour, will be born to you. The terrible Saṃvartaka Āditya was cursed by the sages, ॥28॥
5.3.29: You shall become a human — he will be your son. And whatever you have asked for, obtain all of it. ॥29॥
5.3.30: Sanatkumāra said: Having thus obtained all the boons from the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa gratified him with many hymns of various kinds. ॥30॥
5.3.31: Then Śivā Pārvatī, pleased and loving to her devotees, spoke to the great-souled Vāsudeva, the ascetic devoted to Śambhu. ॥31॥
5.3.32: Pārvatī said: O Vāsudeva of great intellect, O sinless Kṛṣṇa, I am pleased with you. Accept from me too boons that are delightful and rare on earth. ॥32॥
5.3.33: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of Pārvatī, that scion of the Yadus, his heart deeply gladdened, spoke with a mind full of devotion. ॥33॥
5.3.34: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Goddess, if you are fully pleased and are giving me boons, then by this true austerity may there never arise towards brāhmaṇas ॥34॥
5.3.35: hatred at any time; rather, may I always honour the twice-born. And may my mother and father be ever pleased with me. ॥35॥
5.3.36: Wherever I go, may I enjoy goodwill among all beings; and by your sight, may I have fitting offspring in my family. ॥36॥
5.3.37: May I gratify the gods, Indra and the rest, with a hundred sacrifices; and may I always feed thousands of ascetics and guests— ॥37॥
5.3.38: may I always feed them in my home with food purified by faith. And may there be constant affection with my kinsmen, and perfect contentment. ॥38॥
5.3.39: O Goddess, may I be dear as life to thousands of wives, and by your grace, O consort of Śaṅkara, may my desirability to them never wane. ॥39॥
5.3.40: And may their fathers in the world be truthful. Let these and other excellent boons be granted through your grace, O Pārvatī. ॥40॥
5.3.41: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing those words of his, the goddess, astonished, said to him: so be it; blessings to you—she, the eternal one, the giver of all desires. ॥41॥
5.3.42: Having given those boons to him, Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord, having bestowed true grace on Kṛṣṇa, vanished right there. ॥42॥
5.3.43: Kṛṣṇa considered himself fulfilled, O lord of sages. He quickly reached the incomparable hermitage of the sage Upamanyu. ॥43॥
5.3.44: Then the slayer of Keśin, having bowed his head there to that sage, related to Upamanyu all that had happened. ॥44॥
5.3.45: And he said to him: who else could there be, other than the god Śarva, O Janārdana, who is the lord of great gifts in the world, or so exceedingly unbearable in anger, ॥45॥
5.3.46: or in knowledge, in austerity, in valour, in steadfastness, or in rank? Listen, O Govinda, O illustrious one, to the divine sovereignty of Śambhu. ॥46॥
5.3.47: Hearing that, he became filled with faith and devoted to Śambhu; he asked about Śiva's greatness, and the lord of sages spoke to him. ॥47॥
5.3.48: Upamanyu said: Formerly, in the world of Brahmā, the blessed Śaṅkara was praised with a thousand names by the great-souled Taṇḍi, a yogin of Brahman. ॥48॥
5.3.49: The Sāṅkhyas recite that hymn, extensive like a lexicon. That hymn is hard for humans to understand, yet it grants all desires. ॥49॥
5.3.50: Remembering Śaṅkara constantly, go home happy, O Kṛṣṇa. You will always be, dear one, the foremost among the hosts of Śiva's devotees. ॥50॥
5.3.51: Thus addressed, Vāsudeva bowed to the lord of sages, and Keśava, recollecting Śambhu in his mind, went to Dvārakā. ॥51॥
5.3.52: Sanatkumāra said: Thus Kṛṣṇa, having worshipped Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world, became fulfilled, O best of sages, and likewise became invincible to all. ॥52॥
5.3.53: Likewise Rāma, son of Daśaratha, having worshipped Śiva with devotion, became fulfilled, O best of sages, and was victorious everywhere. ॥53॥
5.3.54: Formerly, O sage, Rāma, having performed extremely vast austerity on a mountain, obtained from Śiva a bow, arrows, a further bow, and indeed supreme, excellent knowledge. ॥54॥
5.3.55: Having slain Rāvaṇa with his hosts, having built a bridge over the ocean, and having regained Sītā, he went home and enjoyed rule over the entire earth. ॥55॥
5.3.56: Likewise Rāma the Bhārgava, grieved on seeing his father killed by kṣatriyas, worshipped the all-pervading Lord with austerity, and from Śarva— ॥56॥
5.3.57: —from the pleased Supreme Lord he obtained a sharp axe, and with it he burned up those kṣatriyas thrice seven times. ॥57॥
5.3.58: Invincible and immortal, that treasury of austerities, ever devoted to the worship of the liṅga, is seen even today by Siddhas and Cāraṇas. ॥58॥
5.3.59: Rāma, dwelling on Mount Mahendra, remains in austerity; at the end of the kalpa he will again attain the station of a ṛṣi. ॥59॥
5.3.60: Formerly the younger brother of Asita, the ascetic named Devala, in affliction performed austerity, holding fast to the root of the universe Śiva. ॥60॥
5.3.61: That ascetic, who had been cursed by Purandara, by worshipping the wish-granting liṅga firmly obtained a dharma untouched by adharma. ॥61॥
5.3.62: Gṛtsamada, son of Cākṣuṣa Manu, became a deer in a desert region through Vasiṣṭha's curse; alone in the Daṇḍaka forest, ॥62॥
5.3.63: remembering with devotion in his heart Śiva united with the praṇava, he thereby became a deer-faced gaṇa, having the appearance of the mouth of death. ॥63॥
5.3.64: Having crossed beyond the curse, he was again brought to freedom from old age and death, and out of affection Śaṅkara made him a permanent follower of Lambodara. ॥64॥
5.3.65: Śarva granted Gārgya liberation, rare on earth, the power of moving at will, a great domain, and knowledge of time endowed with great prosperity, ॥65॥
5.3.66: and eternal mastery of the four-footed Sarasvatī speech; and Śiva gave him a thousand unequalled sons. ॥66॥
5.3.67: The wielder of Pināka, pleased, gave to Parāśara a son, Vedavyāsa, lord of yogins, free from old age and death. ॥67॥
5.3.68: Māṇḍavya, taken down from the point of the stake after ten hundred thousand years, was released by Śaṅkara himself, who gave him life. ॥68॥
5.3.69: A certain poor brahmin, who had formerly been a householder, placed his son Gālava in his teacher's house. ॥69॥
5.3.70: Hiding in the sages' hall, he said to his wife—since he was utterly penniless—whatever mendicant comes to this house, ॥70॥
5.3.71: he should be told by you, ॥71॥
5.3.72: Once a certain guest, emaciated and parched with hunger and thirst, said to her, where has your husband gone? And she to him ॥72॥
5.3.73: said, my husband is not to be seen at present. That seer, knowing the truth by his divine sight, said this to her: ॥73॥
5.3.74: Thus cursed, that brahmin, staying hidden in the house, died right there. Then his son Gālava, permitted by Viśvāmitra, ॥74॥
5.3.75: came home and, hearing from his mother of the most dreadful curse, worshipped the god Śaṅkara, performing the worship of Śambhu. ॥75॥
5.3.76: He the father came forth from the house, remembering Śaṅkara in his heart. Then, seeing his son, the father, with joined palms, said to him: ॥76॥
5.3.77: By Mahādeva's grace, through your deed I am fulfilled; I am wealthy and blessed with a son; I was dead and am alive again. ॥77॥
5.3.78: Thus I have told you everything; I am not able to describe Śambhu's virtues either briefly or in detail—even Śeṣa would not have enough mouths. ॥78॥
5.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The description of the glory of Śiva in uplifting Kṛṣṇa and other devotees of Śiva, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
5.4.1: The sages said: Dear sir, dear sir, O greatly fortunate one, you are truly blessed, O wise one! This wondrous story of Śambhu, which bestows supreme devotion, has been narrated to us. ॥1॥
5.4.2: Tell again the story of Śambhu, following the questions of Vyāsa. You are all-knowing, the disciple of Vyāsa, skilled in the truth of Śiva. ॥2॥
5.4.3: Sūta said: In just this way my teacher Vyāsa questioned Sanatkumāra, born of the Unborn Brahmā, the all-knowing devotee of Śiva, lord among sages. ॥3॥
5.4.4: Vyāsa said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, this auspicious story of Śaṅkara, the great Lord who sports in various divine plays, has been narrated to me. ॥4॥
5.4.5: Tell again, in particular, of the greatness of Mahādeva; for, dear sir, my great eagerness to hear keeps growing. ॥5॥
5.4.6: Tell by what greatness of Śambhu, who sports in various plays, all those in the world were deluded, he having taken away their knowledge through his māyā. ॥6॥
5.4.7: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great intellect, to the delightful story of Śaṅkara, by the mere hearing of which devotion to Śiva arises. ॥7॥
5.4.8: Śiva is the god, lord of all, the Self of all, the all-seeing; by his greatness this whole entire world is pervaded. ॥8॥
5.4.9: The supreme form of Śiva alone is made up of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Īśvara; it is called the self of all beings, and has the form of the three liṅgas and of the liṅga-less. ॥9॥
5.4.10: There are eight orders of birth of the gods, the human one which is the ninth, and five orders of animals; thus there are fourteen. ॥10॥
5.4.11: Whether past, present or future, all beings everywhere come forth from Śiva, and, having reached their growth, dissolve into him. ॥11॥
5.4.12: Of Brahmā, Indra, Upendra and Candra, of gods, Dānavas and serpents, of Gandharvas, of humans, and of all others as well — ॥12॥
5.4.13: — Śiva is regarded as kinsman, friend, preceptor, protector, leader, benefactor, teacher, wish-fulfilling tree, or brother, father and mother. ॥13॥
5.4.14: Śiva, who comprises everything, is to be known by men through himself; he is higher than the highest; he cannot be described, and he is that which is both the higher and the lower. ॥14॥
5.4.15: His supreme divine māyā pervades everywhere, O sage; the whole world, with gods, asuras and humans, is subject to it. ॥15॥
5.4.16: By Kāma, its own helper, the mighty Mind-born one, every hero has been overpowered — even the mighty ones beginning with Viṣṇu. ॥16॥
5.4.17: Through the power of Śiva's māyā, Hari became infatuated by desire and violated others' wives many times, O lord of sages. ॥17॥
5.4.18: Indra, though lord of the gods, became infatuated with Gautama's wife; the wicked one committed sin and then received the sage's curse. ॥18॥
5.4.19: Even Fire, the foremost in the world, deluded by Śiva's māyā, was made subject to desire because of his pride; and afterwards he was rescued by that very Śiva. ॥19॥
5.4.20: Even the Wind, the life-breath of the world, deluded through pride by Śiva's māyā and conquered by desire, O Vyāsa, once took pleasure with another's wife. ॥20॥
5.4.21: The fierce-rayed Sun, Mārtaṇḍa, deluded by Śiva's māyā, quickly became overwhelmed with desire on seeing a mare, and assumed the form of a horse. ॥21॥
5.4.22: And the Moon, deluded by Śambhu's māyā and filled with desire, carried off his teacher's wife; then, united with her, he was rescued by that very Śiva. ॥22॥
5.4.23: Long ago Mitra and Varuṇa were engaged in severe austerity; yet even those two sages were deluded, bewildered by Śiva's māyā. ॥23॥
5.4.24: Seeing the young Urvaśī, both became lustful; Mitra discharged his semen into a jar, and Varuṇa likewise into water. ॥24॥
5.4.25: Then from the jar arose Vasiṣṭha, born of Mitra; and from Varuṇa was born Agastya, radiant like the submarine fire. ॥25॥
5.4.26: And Dakṣa, the son of Brahmā, deluded by Śambhu's māyā, once together with his brothers desired to enjoy their sister. ॥26॥
5.4.27: And Brahmā too, deluded many times by Śiva's māyā, became desirous of enjoying his own daughter and other women. ॥27॥
5.4.28: Even Cyavana, the great yogin, deluded by Śiva's māyā, sported with Sukanyā; he became attached to desire. ॥28॥
5.4.29: Kaśyapa, deluded through Śiva's māyā and filled with desire, once out of infatuation begged King Dhanvan for his daughter. ॥29॥
5.4.30: Garuḍa, utterly infatuated, wished to carry off the maiden Śāṇḍilī; but being found out by her, he at once had his wings burnt. ॥30॥
5.4.31: The sage Vibhāṇḍaka, on seeing a woman, fell under the sway of desire; his son Ṛṣyaśṛṅga was born of a doe by Śiva's command. ॥31॥
5.4.32: And the sage Gautama, his mind deluded by Śambhu's māyā, seeing Śāradvatī naked, was agitated by her and took pleasure. ॥32॥
5.4.33: That ascetic held his own spilled semen in a wooden vessel; and from that pot was born Droṇa, the best of weapon-bearers. ॥33॥
5.4.34: Parāśara, the great yogin, deluded by Śiva's māyā, sported with the maiden Matsyodarī, the fisherman's daughter. ॥34॥
5.4.35: Then Viśvāmitra, deluded by Śiva's māyā and fallen under the sway of desire, O Vyāsa, took pleasure with Menakā in the forest. ॥35॥
5.4.36: Bereft of sense, he entered into hostility with Vasiṣṭha; yet by Śiva's grace that same man again became a brāhmaṇa. ॥36॥
5.4.37: Rāvaṇa, son of Viśravas, became lustful through Śiva's māyā; the evil-minded one, deluded, carried off Sītā and met his death. ॥37॥
5.4.38: Bṛhaspati, best of sages, though self-controlled, deluded by Śiva's māyā, took pleasure with his brother's wife; from that Bharadvāja was born. ॥38॥
5.4.39: Thus, O Vyāsa, I have described to you the power of the māyā of the great-souled Śaṅkara. What else do you wish to hear? ॥39॥
5.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The description of the power of Śiva's māyā, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
5.5.1: Vyāsa said: O Lord, describe to me those beings who are given to sin and who are the causes of falling into great hells. O son of Brahmā, salutations to you. ॥1॥
5.5.2: Sanatkumāra said: Those beings who are given to sin and who are the causes of falling into great hells are described here in brief; listen attentively. ॥2॥
5.5.3: Setting one's intent on another's wife or wealth, thinking of harm in the mind, and obsession with what ought not to be done: mental action of sin is of four kinds. ॥3॥
5.5.4: Incoherent babbling, whatever is untrue and unpleasant, and slander behind a person's back: verbal action of sin is of four kinds. ॥4॥
5.5.5: Eating what should not be eaten, violence, engaging in false deeds, and taking the property of others: bodily action of sin is of four kinds. ॥5॥
5.5.6: Thus this twelvefold action, performed through three means, has been declared. Now I shall further tell its subdivisions, whose fruit is endless. ॥6॥
5.5.7: Those who hate Mahādeva, who ferries beings across the ocean of saṃsāra, commit a very great sin; they go into the ocean of hell. ॥7॥
5.5.8: Those deluded ones who revile one who expounds the knowledge of Śiva, an ascetic, gurus, and fathers go to the ocean of hell. ॥8॥
5.5.9: Reviling Śiva, reviling the guru, defaming the knowledge of Śiva, stealing the property of the gods, destroying the property of brahmins, ॥9॥
5.5.10: and the act of those deluded ones who steal a book of Śiva-knowledge: these six they call great sins, yielding endless evil fruit. ॥10॥
5.5.11: Those who, seeing worship of Śiva being performed, do not rejoice in it; who, seeing a worshipped Śiva-liṅga, do not bow and do not praise it; ॥11॥
5.5.12: who, acting as they please and without fear, stand about and amuse themselves before Śiva and in the presence of the guru, devoid of proper courtesies; ॥12॥
5.5.13: those who, though established in the path of ritual action, do not on festival days perform consecration of the sacred place and worship, or honour the gurus according to rule; ॥13॥
5.5.14: those who abandon Śaiva conduct and hate Śiva's devotees; those who, without first worshipping the Śiva-knowledge scripture, study and copy it; ॥14॥
5.5.15: who impart it, hear it, and recite it improperly; who trade in it out of greed and according to the rules of false knowledge; ॥15॥
5.5.16: and who lay it down as they please in unconsecrated places; he who, interrupting a discourse on Śiva-knowledge, speaks of something else; ॥16॥
5.5.17: he who does not speak the truth and does not give gifts; he who, being impure or in an impure place, expounds or listens to it; ॥17॥
5.5.18: he who wishes to hear scripture without first worshipping the guru, and who does not render service or obey his command with devotion; ॥18॥
5.5.19: who does not welcome his words but answers back, and who neglects whatever in the guru's work is hard to accomplish; ॥19॥
5.5.20: the evildoer who abandons his guru when he is afflicted, powerless, setting out for a foreign land, or humiliated by enemies; ॥20॥
5.5.21: and he who shows contempt toward his wife, sons, and friends — and likewise toward those of a good expounder who reveals dharma, even though he be not one's own guru: ॥21॥
5.5.22: All these deeds, O best of sages, they declare to be very great sins, equal to reviling Śiva. ॥22॥
5.5.23: The slayer of a brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and the violator of the guru's bed — these are the great sinners, and the fifth is one who associates with them. ॥23॥
5.5.24: He who, out of anger, greed, fear, or hatred, aiming at a brahmin's ruin, alleges a grave fault that cuts to the quick, becomes a brahmin-slayer. ॥24॥
5.5.25: He who invites a brahmin and then gives nothing, he who having given takes back, and he who defames a faultless one — that man becomes a brahmin-slayer. ॥25॥
5.5.26: He who, out of pride in his learning, puts to shame a good brahmin who is indifferent to dispute in the midst of an assembly is declared a brahmin-slayer. ॥26॥
5.5.27: He who by false merits forcibly raises himself to eminence, setting aside others' true merits, he too becomes a brahmin-slayer. ॥27॥
5.5.28: He who creates obstruction for cows being covered by bulls, and for brahmins, gurus foremost — him they call a brahmin-slayer. ॥28॥
5.5.29: He who seizes land given to gods, brahmins, or cows, even if it has been lost to them over time — him they call a brahmin-slayer. ॥29॥
5.5.30: The seizing of the property of gods and brahmins, and whatever is acquired unjustly, should be known as a sin equal to killing a brahmin; there is no doubt about this. ॥30॥
5.5.31: If a twice-born, having studied the Veda and the knowledge of Brahman that is of the nature of Śiva, foolishly abandons it, that is equal to drinking liquor. ॥31॥
5.5.32: Having undertaken any vow, observance, or sacrifice and then abandoning it, and the abandonment of the five daily sacrifices — that is equal to drinking liquor. ॥32॥
5.5.33: Forsaking father and mother, false witness, lying to brahmins, meat -eating by Śiva's devotees, and eating what is forbidden; ॥33॥
5.5.34: and killing innocent creatures in the forest; and when what a good man would set aside for brahmins one does not apply to a righteous purpose; ॥34॥
5.5.35: and the deed of those who set fire on the paths of cows, in forests, or in villages — these are terrible sins, equal to killing a brahmin. ॥35॥
5.5.36: Seizing all that a poor man owns; the sale of men, women, elephants, horses, cows, land, silver, garments, medicinal herbs, and juices, ॥36॥
5.5.37: of sandal, aloe-wood, camphor, musk, and silk garments — the sale of these made knowingly by twice-born men when not in distress, ॥37॥
5.5.38: and misappropriating a deposit placed in one's hands — these are held equal to stealing gold. Not giving marriageable daughters to a suitable bridegroom, ॥38॥
5.5.39: going to the wives of one's son or friend, and to sisters; the terrible violation of a maiden; consorting with the wife of a drunkard; ॥39॥
5.5.40: and going to a woman of one's own class — these are held equal to violating the guru's wife. The great sins have been told; now hear about the minor sins. ॥40॥
5.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The description of the great sins, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
5.6.1: Sanatkumāra said: Stealing the property of brahmins, and also violating the rules of inheritance, excessive pride and excessive anger, hypocrisy, ingratitude, ॥1॥
5.6.2: excessive attachment to sense-objects, miserliness, envy of the good, going to others' wives, defiling the daughters of good people, ॥2॥
5.6.3: the elder brother who stays unmarried while his younger brother marries (parivitti), the younger who marries first (parivettā), and the girl by whom he is so married; giving a girl in marriage to those two, and officiating at sacrifices for those very two, ॥3॥
5.6.4: destroying the trees of Śiva's hermitages and flower-gardens; and he who inflicts even slight pain on those dwelling in hermitages, ॥4॥
5.6.5: harming one with his servants and household, his cattle, grain and wealth; theft of base metals, grain and cattle, and likewise polluting waters, ॥5॥
5.6.6: selling sacrifices, gardens and ponds, or one's wife and children; selling the merit of pilgrimages and fasts, of vows and the rites of upanayana, ॥6॥
5.6.7: those who, utterly conquered by women, live on women's wealth; failing to protect women, and enjoying women by deceit, ॥7॥
5.6.8: not giving what has fallen due in time, living on interest from grain, accepting wealth from a censured person, living by fraud in merchandise, ॥8॥
5.6.9: the use of poisons and killing-spells, constantly yoking bulls, rites of expulsion (uccāṭana) and black magic (abhicāra), taking grain, and practising medicine, ॥9॥
5.6.10: he whose undertaking of good deeds is for the enjoyment of palate and lust; one who always teaches for a fee, and whatever Vedic knowledge and the like is sold, ॥10॥
5.6.11: abandoning the vows of brahmacarya and the like, following the conduct of others, studying false scriptures, relying on dry logic, ॥11॥
5.6.12: the reviling of gods, fire, gurus and holy men, and of a brahmin, whether to their face or behind their back, and also of kings and regional rulers, ॥12॥
5.6.13: those who have abandoned worship of ancestors and gods, who forsake their own duties, the ill-behaved, unbelievers, sinners, and those who always speak untruth, ॥13॥
5.6.14: he who has intercourse on a festival day (parvan), by day, or in water, in an unnatural orifice, with animals, or with a menstruating woman, ॥14॥
5.6.15: those who cut off the hopes of wife, son or friend when they approach, speakers of unpleasant things to people, the cruel, and breakers of agreements, ॥15॥
5.6.16: one who breaches ponds and wells, sellers of liquids, and he who makes distinction in the food served to those seated in the same row, ॥16॥
5.6.17: Women and men guilty of these sins are declared to be committers of minor sins (upapātaka). Others too are tainted with these; listen, I shall tell you of them. ॥17॥
5.6.18: Those men who ruin the affairs of cows, brahmins and maidens, of masters, friends and ascetics, are declared destined for hell. ॥18॥
5.6.19: Those who burn with longing for another's wife, who point out others' wealth to thieves, who constantly steal others' wealth, and who follow false weights, ॥19॥
5.6.20: those who cause suffering to brahmins, who raise a blow against them, twice-born men who consort with a śūdra woman, and those who prepare liquor at will, ॥20॥
5.6.21: cruel men devoted to sin, men fond of violence, and those who perform acts like giving and sacrifice for the sake of a livelihood, ॥21॥
5.6.22: those who discharge excrement and the like in cowpens, fire, water and streets, in the shade of trees and on hills, and in gardens and temples, ॥22॥
5.6.23: those addicted to drinking liquor in places of modesty, hermitages and temples, lechers given to dalliance, and those intent on seeking out others' weak points, ॥23॥
5.6.24: those who obstruct the road with bamboo, bricks, stones, wood, horns and stakes, and those who seize another's boundary, ॥24॥
5.6.25: makers of forged edicts, those devoted to fraudulent deeds, those who deal fraudulently in cooked food, grain and cloth, ॥25॥
5.6.26: he who makes bows, weapons and arrows and buys and sells them, he who is extremely merciless toward servants, and he who harshly tames animals, ॥26॥
5.6.27: he who quietly listens to the words of one speaking falsely, the betrayer of master, friend and guru, the deceitful, the fickle, the rogue, ॥27॥
5.6.28: those who eat while neglecting their hungry wife, sons and friends, children, the old, the weak and the sick, servants, guests and relatives, ॥28॥
5.6.29: He who himself eats sweet food and does not give to brahmins should be known as a futile cook, censured among the expounders of the Veda. ॥29॥
5.6.30: those of uncontrolled senses who, having themselves taken up observances, abandon them; those who falsely wear the garb of renunciation; and those who deface the image of Hara, ॥30॥
5.6.31: those cruel ones who beat a cow and subdue it again and again, who do not nourish weak ones and constantly abandon them, ॥31॥
5.6.32: who torment them with excessive loads and make one that cannot bear it carry them, who yoke them when they have not eaten and do not release them when tied, ॥32॥
5.6.33: Those who do not carefully tend cows and bulls afflicted by loads, wounds and disease, or tormented by hunger, are cow-killers, declared destined for hell. ॥33॥
5.6.34: Those most sinful ones who castrate bulls, and who make a barren cow carry loads, are men destined for great hell. ॥34॥
5.6.35: Those who have arrived with hope, emaciated by hunger, thirst and toil — guests, the helpless, and independent wanderers who have come to the house — ॥35॥
5.6.36: those longing for food, or the wretched, children, the old, the weak and the sick — the fools who show them no compassion go to the ocean of hell. ॥36॥
5.6.37: Wealth turns back at the house, relatives at the cremation ground; only good and evil deeds follow the one who departs. ॥37॥
5.6.38: A base brahmin who lives by goats and sheep, by buffaloes, by sea-trade, who is husband of a śūdra woman, or who lives like a śūdra or by a kṣatriya's livelihood, becomes hell-bound. ॥38॥
5.6.39: Craftsmen, artisans, physicians, goldsmiths, royal standard-bearers and hired servants — all of them, when given to fraud, are declared hell-bound. ॥39॥
5.6.40: He who, transgressing what is proper, levies tax merely at his own whim, is roasted in hell; so too the man who delights in punishment. ॥40॥
5.6.41: The king whose subjects in his kingdom are oppressed by bribe-takers, by officials bought at will, and by thieves, is cooked in the hells. ॥41॥
5.6.42: Those brahmins who accept gifts from a king who acts unjustly go to terrible hells; there is no doubt. ॥42॥
5.6.43: He who, having unjustly taken wealth from the subjects, gives it to brahmins, he too is cooked in the hells, just like the king. ॥43॥
5.6.44: The sin that belongs to adulterers, thieves and violent men, and also to one attached to others' wives, always accrues to the king who does not restrain them. ॥44॥
5.6.45: A king who, without investigation, regards a non-thief as a thief or a thief as a non-thief, and therefore has him killed, goes to hell. ॥45॥
5.6.46: Ghee, oil, food and drinks, honey, meat, liquor and spirits, jaggery, sugarcane, vegetables and milk, curd, roots and fruits, ॥46॥
5.6.47: grass, wood, leaves and flowers, medicine and one's own food, sandals, umbrella, cart, seat and water-pot, ॥47॥
5.6.48: copper, lead and tin, weapons, conch and other water-born things, musical instruments, bamboo articles and other household goods, ॥48॥
5.6.49: and garments, coarse and fine, made of wool, cotton, silk and fine thread — those who out of greed steal these, ॥49॥
5.6.50: — having stolen these and other various goods, even small ones, they surely go to the hells. ॥50॥
5.6.51: Having stolen another's property, whatever it may be, even as little as a mustard seed, men go to hell; there is no doubt about this. ॥51॥
5.6.52: Through such sins, a man, immediately after departing from life, obtains a body of complete form for the sake of bodily torment. ॥52॥
5.6.53: By Yama's command these go with that body to Yama's world, being led by Yama's very terrible messengers, sorely afflicted. ॥53॥
5.6.54: For gods, animals and humans whose minds are devoted to unrighteousness, Dharmarāja is known as the chastiser, with very terrible and various punishments. ॥54॥
5.6.55: For those who observe rules and right conduct but have slipped through carelessness, the guru is the chastiser, through expiations; Yama is not accepted as their punisher by the wise. ॥55॥
5.6.56: For adulterers, thieves and those who deal unjustly, the king is declared the chastiser; for those whose sins are hidden, it is Dharmarāja. ॥56॥
5.6.57: Therefore one should perform expiation for a sin committed; otherwise there is no destruction of a sin not experienced in its fruit, even in hundreds of crores of kalpas. ॥57॥
5.6.58: He who himself does a deed, causes it to be done, or approves of it, by body, mind or speech — for him the fruit is the course leading to sin's consequences. ॥58॥
5.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The description of the kinds of sin, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
5.7.1: Sanatkumāra said: Now, because of sins of four kinds, men go to the world of Yama, which is dreadful and causes terror; all embodied beings go there helplessly. ॥1॥
5.7.2: It must be understood to apply to all creatures: to beings in the womb, to those being born, to children, to the young and the middle-aged, and to women, men and neuters. ॥2॥
5.7.3: And here the fruit of the good and evil deeds of embodied beings is examined by Citragupta and all the others, and likewise by those headed by Vasiṣṭha. ॥3॥
5.7.4: There are no living beings who do not go to the abode of Yama. For a deed that has been done must surely be experienced; let this be pondered. ॥4॥
5.7.5: Of these, the men whose deeds are good, whose minds are gentle and who are full of compassion go to Yama's dwelling by the pleasant eastern path. ॥5॥
5.7.6: But those who do sinful deeds, the wicked who are devoid of giving, go to Yama's abode by the dreadful southern path. ॥6॥
5.7.7: Having passed beyond eighty-six thousand yojanas, that city of Vaivasvata Yama is to be known, situated there in manifold forms. ॥7॥
5.7.8: To men of meritorious deeds it appears as though near at hand; to sinners, who go by the terrible path, it is very far away. ॥8॥
5.7.9: They go by a path beset with sharp thorns, strewn with gravel, and laid with sharp stones like razor edges; ॥9॥
5.7.10: in places by a path with deep mud and swarming with leeches, in places furnished with darbha grass like iron needles; ॥10॥
5.7.11: by mountains mostly of steep precipices, very rugged and thick with trees, and by a road covered with glowing coals, they go in misery. ॥11॥
5.7.12: In places with uneven pits, in places with clods very hard to cross, with burning-hot sand and likewise with sharp stakes; ॥12॥
5.7.13: in places overrun with bamboo thickets spreading with many branches; somewhere by a painful path in darkness without any support; ॥13॥
5.7.14: in places with sharp iron caltrops, again with forest fire, in places with heated rocks, and in places covered with snow; ॥14॥
5.7.15: in places covered with sand into which one sinks up to the throat, in places with foul water, and in places with dung-fire; ॥15॥
5.7.16: in places with lions, wolves, tigers and very fierce mosquitoes, in places with huge leeches, and in places likewise with pythons; ॥16॥
5.7.17: with fierce flies, in places with serpents of virulent poison, and with herds of rutting elephants, mad with strength and crushing; ॥17॥
5.7.18: with sharp-tusked boars furrowing the path, with sharp-horned buffaloes, and with beasts of prey of every kind; ॥18॥
5.7.19: tormented by fierce ḍākinīs, by hideous rākṣasas and by most dreadful diseases, they indeed proceed. ॥19॥
5.7.20: Struck by a very violent wind mixed with thick dust and by a shower of huge stones, they go without refuge. ॥20॥
5.7.21: In places they go on being burnt by falling lightning, and pierced on all sides by a great shower of arrows. ॥21॥
5.7.22: They are indeed burnt by falling thunderbolts, by dreadful falls of meteors, and by a shower of blazing coals. ॥22॥
5.7.23: Filled up by a great shower of dust they weep, and again and again they are terrified by the dreadful roars of great clouds. ॥23॥
5.7.24: Cut on all sides by a shower of sharp weapons and drenched by torrents of very caustic water, they go on. ॥24॥
5.7.25: Afflicted on every side by an extremely cold, dry and harsh wind, they wither and shrivel up. ॥25॥
5.7.26: Thus, by a terrible road, without provisions for the journey, without support, hard to pass, waterless all around, ॥26॥
5.7.27: very rugged and long, without people or shelter, of the form of darkness, painful, and the haunt of every evil thing, ॥27॥
5.7.28: all embodied beings who are deluded and do sinful deeds are led by force by the most dreadful messengers of Yama, who carry out his command. ॥28॥
5.7.29: Alone, in the power of others, deprived of friends and kin, lamenting their own deeds and weeping again and again, ॥29॥
5.7.30: having become pretas, naked, with throats, lips and palates parched, ghastly, stricken with fear, burning and tormented by hunger, ॥30॥
5.7.31: some men, bound with chains, lying on their backs and held by the feet, are dragged; and as they are dragged they are beaten by Yama's messengers of fierce strength. ॥31॥
5.7.32: Others, face down, scraped along on their chests, in great misery, are dragged with a rope tied to their tufts of hair. ॥32॥
5.7.33: Other embodied beings, pierced in the forehead with a goad, suffer; some are dragged on their backs along a thorny path, in places along a road of burning coals. ॥33॥
5.7.34: With arms bound behind them, squeezed at the belly, loaded with chains and with their hands firmly nailed, ॥34॥
5.7.35: some are dragged by a noose on the neck; others go on in great misery; they are dragged by a rope with a hook driven into the tongue. ॥35॥
5.7.36: Likewise others are dragged by a rope through a pierced nose; others, pierced in the cheeks and likewise in the lips, are dragged by a rope. ॥36॥
5.7.37: With the tips of their feet and hands cut off, with ears, lips and noses cut off, with penis and testicles severed, their limbs and joints cut and split, ॥37॥
5.7.38: being pierced through with lances and pierced with arrows, running hither and thither, crying out, without refuge, ॥38॥
5.7.39: struck again and again with mallets and iron rods, and with various dreadful thorns shining like fire and the sun, ॥39॥
5.7.40: they are pierced with bhindipāla darts, streaming pus and blood; smeared with excrement and worms, the helpless men are led on. ॥40॥
5.7.41: Begging for water, or for food when hungry, pleading for shade, and again for fire when afflicted by cold, ॥41॥
5.7.42: thus men devoid of charity go along, longing for comfort. Those who have taken gifts given in life as their provisions for the journey go happily to Yama's abode. ॥42॥
5.7.43: When, in this manner and with hardship, they have reached the city of the departed, they are announced by the messengers and then placed before Yama. ॥43॥
5.7.44: There, those who have done good deeds Yama honours with words of welcome, the offering of a seat, water for the feet and arghya, and kind speech. ॥44॥
5.7.45: Blessed are you, great souls, doers of what the Vedas enjoin, by whom merit has been performed for the sake of heavenly happiness. ॥45॥
5.7.46: Mounting a celestial chariot adorned with celestial women and enjoyments, go to spotless heaven, furnished with all desires. ॥46॥
5.7.47: Having enjoyed great pleasures there, at the end, upon the exhaustion of your merit, whatever small evil remains, that you will again experience here. ॥47॥
5.7.48: Righteous men, who are like friends to themselves, behold a gentle face and the King of Dharma himself. ॥48॥
5.7.49: But those of cruel deeds see him terrifying, his face dreadful with fangs, his eyes crooked with knitted brows, ॥49॥
5.7.50: with hair standing up, a great beard, lips quivering upward, eighteen-armed, angry, resembling a heap of blue collyrium, ॥50॥
5.7.51: his hands raising all weapons, threatening with the rod of all punishment, mounted on a great buffalo, with eyes like blazing fire, ॥51॥
5.7.52: wearing red garlands and garments, towering like great Meru, roaring like the clouds of dissolution, as if drinking up the great ocean, ॥52॥
5.7.53: as if swallowing the king of mountains, as if vomiting fire. And Death stands near, with a radiance like the fire of time's end; ॥53॥
5.7.54: and Kāla, resembling collyrium, and terrifying Kṛtānta, Mārī, the fierce Mahāmārī, and dreadful Kālarātri; ॥54॥
5.7.55: various diseases, leprosies, of many forms, fearsome, bearing spears, tridents and goads, with nooses, discuses and swords in their hands, ॥55॥
5.7.56: bearing thunderbolt-like beaks, fierce, carrying razors, quivers and bows, all bearing various weapons, great heroes, terrifying; ॥56॥
5.7.57: countless great heroes, with a radiance like black collyrium, their hands raised with all weapons—the terrifying messengers of Yama. ॥57॥
5.7.58: The most sinful behold that Yama, terrible to look upon, surrounded by this retinue, and the fearsome Citragupta. ॥58॥
5.7.59: Yama severely rebukes those evil-doers, and the venerable Citragupta instructs them with words of dharma. ॥59॥
5.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The description of the road to the world of hell and of the form of Yama's messengers, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
5.8.1: Citragupta said: O you whose deeds are wicked, stealers of others' wealth, proud of your beauty and strength, violators of others' wives. ॥1॥
5.8.2: The deed that one does oneself is the very thing one experiences as its result in turn. Why then did you commit evil, only to bring about your own ruin? ॥2॥
5.8.3: Why do you lament now, tormented by your own deeds? Let your own deeds be experienced; the fault indeed lies with no one else. ॥3॥
5.8.4: Sanatkumāra said: In the same way those kings, arrogant with the power of their misdeeds, arrived before him on account of their own terrible deeds. ॥4॥
5.8.5: Them too Citragupta, the great lord, knower of dharma, filled with anger, admonishes according to the instruction of King Yama. ॥5॥
5.8.6: Citragupta said: O kings of wicked conduct, destroyers of your subjects, why did you commit evil for the sake of a kingdom that lasts but a short time? ॥6॥
5.8.7: Since, out of delusion from the enjoyment of kingship, you punished your subjects by force and unjustly, let the fruit of that be experienced now, O kings. ॥7॥
5.8.8: Where now is that kingdom and wife for whose sake evil was done? Abandoning all that, you stand here alone. ॥8॥
5.8.9: I see that the strength by which the subjects were crushed is gone. Now, as you are being dealt with by Yama's messengers, what will your state be like? ॥9॥
5.8.10: Sanatkumāra said: Thus reproached by Yama with many kinds of words, those kings grieve over their own deeds and stand in silence. ॥10॥
5.8.11: Having thus pointed out the deeds of the kings, Yama, the king of dharma, speaks these words to his messengers for cleansing the mire of their sins. ॥11॥
5.8.12: Yama said: O Caṇḍa, O Mahācaṇḍa, seize these kings by force and purify them in due order, according to rule, in the fires of hell. ॥12॥
5.8.13: Sanatkumāra said: Then, quickly taking hold of the kings, seizing them by the feet, whirling them around with force, tossing them up and catching them again, ॥13॥
5.8.14: with all their great might they dash them violently on an exceedingly heated rock surface, like great trees struck by a thunderbolt. ॥14॥
5.8.15: Then, shattered, he streams blood from his ears; that embodied being then becomes senseless and motionless. ॥15॥
5.8.16: Then, touched by the wind, he is revived again by them; and then, for the purification of his sins, they cast him into the ocean of hell. ॥16॥
5.8.17: Beneath the earth are the divisions (koṭi) of hell, seven groups, twenty-eight in number, situated at the end of the seventh nether level in dreadful darkness. ॥17॥
5.8.18: The first division is called Ghorā; Sughorā lies below it; then Atighorā, Mahāghorā, and the fifth, Ghorarūpā; ॥18॥
5.8.19: the sixth is called Talātalā, the seventh Bhayānakā, the eighth Kālarātri, and the ninth Bhayotkaṭā; ॥19॥
5.8.20: the tenth, below that, is Caṇḍā; further below is Mahācaṇḍā; then another, Caṇḍakolāhalā; Pracaṇḍā; Caṇḍanāyikā; ॥20॥
5.8.21: Padmā, Padmāvatī, Bhītā, Bhīmā, Bhīṣaṇanāyikā, Karālā, Vikarālā, and Vajrā, which is known as the twentieth; ॥21॥
5.8.22: Trikoṇā, Pañcakoṇā, Sudīrghā, Akhilārtidā, Samā, Bhīmabalā, Abhogrā, and Dīptaprāyā, which is the twenty-eighth. ॥22॥
5.8.23: Thus these dreadful divisions of hell have been told to you by name; they are exactly twenty-eight, consisting of torments for sinners. ॥23॥
5.8.24: For each of these divisions, in order, five chief hells are to be known; learn them by name. ॥24॥
5.8.25: The first of them is Raurava, where embodied beings weep; and through the torments of Mahāraurava even the great weep. ॥25॥
5.8.26: Then Śīta and also Uṣṇa: these five are known as the first chief hells. Sughora, Sumahātīkṣṇa, and likewise Sañjīvana are known next. ॥26॥
5.8.27: Mahātama, Viloma, Vilopa, and also Kaṇṭaka, Tīvravega, Karāla, Vikarāla, Prakampana, ॥27॥
5.8.28: Mahāvakra, Kāla, Kālasūtra, Pragarjana, Sūcīmukha, Suneti, Khādaka, Suprapīḍana, ॥28॥
5.8.29: Kumbhīpāka and Supāka, the extremely cruel Krakaca, Aṅgārarāśibhavana, and then Medo'sṛkprahita, ॥29॥
5.8.30: Tīkṣṇatuṇḍa, Śakuni, Mahāsaṃvartaka, Kratu, Taptajantu, Paṅkalepa, Pratimāṃsa, Trapūdbhava, ॥30॥
5.8.31: Ucchvāsa, Sunirucchvāsa, Sudīrgha, Kūṭaśālmali, Duriṣṭa, Sumahāvāda, Pravāha, Supratāpana, ॥31॥
5.8.32: then Megha, Vṛṣa, Śālma; those with the faces of lions, tigers, and elephants; those with the faces of dogs, boars, goats, buffaloes, owls, ruddy geese, and wolves; ॥32॥
5.8.33: those named Grāha, Kumbhīna, and Nakra; Sarpa, Kūrma, and Vāyasa; those named Gṛdhra, Ulūka, and Halauka; Śārdūla, Kratha, and Karkaṭa; ॥33॥
5.8.34: Maṇḍūka, the Pūtivaktras, Raktākṣa, the Pūtimṛttikās, Kaṇadhūmra, likewise Agni, and likewise Kṛmigandhivapus, ॥34॥
5.8.35: Agnīdhra, Apratiṣṭha, Rudhirābha, Śvabhojana, Lālābhakṣa and Antrabhakṣa, and the very cruel Sarvabhakṣa, ॥35॥
5.8.36: Kaṇṭaka, Suviśāla, Vikaṭa, Kaṭapūtana, Ambarīṣa, Kaṭāha, and the painful river Vaitaraṇī, ॥36॥
5.8.37: Sutaptalohaśayana (the bed of red-hot iron), Ekapāda, Prapūraṇa, the dreadful Asitālavana (forest of sword-palms), Asthibhaṅga, Supūraṇa, ॥37॥
5.8.38: Vilātasa, also Asuyantra, Kūṭapāśa, Pramardana, Mahācūrṇa, also Asucūrṇa, and likewise the mountain made of heated iron, ॥38॥
5.8.39: the Mountain, Kṣuradhārā (razor's edge), likewise Yamalaparvata (twin mountains), the well of urine, excrement, and tears, and the cold well of caustic brine, ॥39॥
5.8.40: the device of pestle and mortar, the stone-cart and plough, the thicket of palm-leaf swords, and the pavilion of the great cart. ॥40॥
5.8.41: Then come Sammoha, Asthibhaṅga, Tapta, Cala, Ayoguḍa, Bahuduḥkha, Mahākleśa, Kaśmala, Samala and Mala. ॥41॥
5.8.42: Hālāhala, Virūpa, Svarūpa, Yamānuga, Ekapāda, Tripāda, Tīvra, Acīvara and Tamas. ॥42॥
5.8.43: These, in order, are the twenty-eight hells; they are arranged in groups of five by five, and in due sequence there are five by five crores of hells under them, with their chiefs. ॥43॥
5.8.44: They are made known as belonging to Raurava; the hells are traditionally counted as a hundred and forty — this is declared to be the great circle of hells. ॥44॥
5.8.45: Thus, O Vyāsa, I have fully described to you the arrangement of hell; from such enumeration arises dispassion. Now hear also that course of sinners. ॥45॥
5.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The description of the world of hell, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
5.9.1: Sanatkumāra said: In these hells the sinners are cooked and parched in the fires of hell, intensely, by various torments, until their own karma is exhausted. ॥1॥
5.9.2: Just as metals are smelted in fire through the removal of their own impurities, so there sinful men are purified through the destruction of sin, in accordance with their deeds. ॥2॥
5.9.3: Then, having bound them very tightly by the hands with a chain, Yama's servants hang the men from the topmost branches of great trees. ॥3॥
5.9.4: Then, flung with all force by the servants, they swing; and swinging with tremendous speed, they lose consciousness and are carried a yojana away. ॥4॥
5.9.5: And again, to the feet of those hanging in mid-air, a hundred loads of iron are tied by Yama's mighty messengers. ॥5॥
5.9.6: Severely afflicted by that great weight, the men brood on their own deeds and remain silent and motionless. ॥6॥
5.9.7: Then the evil-doers are struck on all sides by the terrible servants with fire-coloured goads and dreadful iron rods. ॥7॥
5.9.8: Then they are smeared all over, again and again, with burning, fierce caustic, more scorching even than fire. ॥8॥
5.9.9: Thoroughly smeared with the molten substance, their limbs cut, they are battered to pieces; and again, their limbs being torn open in order, beginning from the head, ॥9॥
5.9.10: they are cooked like eggplants in heated iron cauldrons; likewise they are thrown into a well full of excrement, and again into a mass of worms, ॥10॥
5.9.11: and again they are thrown into a pond full of fat, blood and pus; they are devoured by sharp-toothed worms and by iron-beaked crows, ॥11॥
5.9.12: by dogs, gadflies, wolves, tigers and fierce beasts with hideous faces; and they are also roasted like fish on heaps of blazing coals. ॥12॥
5.9.13: Pierced by very sharp spikes on account of their sinful deeds, men, trampled in oil-presses because of their own terrible actions, ॥13॥
5.9.14: are crushed like sesame seeds in the hell called Cakra, reduced to lumps of human flesh; and they are fried in many ways in the heat, in heated iron vessels. ॥14॥
5.9.15: In well-heated cauldrons full of oil, again and again, in many ways; and the tongue is cooked after the body is pressed down at the chest and feet. ॥15॥
5.9.16: Here great torments are inflicted on the body, exceedingly and on every side; in this way men pass in succession through all the hells. ॥16॥
5.9.17: In all the hells, O Vyāsa, various torments of Yama, causing intense pain, are inflicted on every limb by Yama's attendants. ॥17॥
5.9.18: Taking a burning coal and filling his mouth with it, the sinner is beaten; then again and again the mouth is filled with burning caustic and molten copper, ॥18॥
5.9.19: and then with extremely hot ghee and oil; his mouth being pried open this way and that and forcibly filled, he is beaten. ॥19॥
5.9.20: Being filled here and there with excrement and worms, they are made to embrace the very fierce, blazing iron śālmali tree. ॥20॥
5.9.21: And they are struck on the back again with blazing great hammers, and cut with a powerful, toothed and very blunt saw. ॥21॥
5.9.22: Beginning from the head they are tormented because of the terrible deeds born of themselves; they are made to eat their own flesh, and their own blood is drunk. ॥22॥
5.9.23: Those who, always nourishing only themselves, never gave food or drink are crushed like sugarcane after being battered with clubs. ॥23॥
5.9.24: Then in the terrible Asitāla forest they are cut to pieces; with all their limbs pierced by needles, impaled on the points of heated stakes, ॥24॥
5.9.25: shaken about many times, they suffer yet do not die; for their bodies are such as to endure pleasure and pain. ॥25॥
5.9.26: Their flesh is torn from the body, and they are smashed with clubs by Yama's terrible messengers of jagged-toothed form and overpowering strength. ॥26॥
5.9.27: In the hell Nirucchvāsa they remain breathless for a long time; likewise in Ucchvāsa, the abode of sand, men are beaten and tossed up. ॥27॥
5.9.28: In Raurava, weeping, they are tormented with various kinds of blows; and through the torments of Mahāraurava even the mighty weep. ॥28॥
5.9.29: On the feet, mouth, anus, head, eyes and crown they are struck with hammers and with sharp, red-hot iron spikes. ॥29॥
5.9.30: They are placed again and again on scorching sand; thrown into a fiercely heated mire of creatures, they wail discordantly. ॥30॥
5.9.31: O sage, sinners of cruel deeds are cooked again in the Kumbhīpāka hells, in heated oils, utterly unbearable. ॥31॥
5.9.32: Those sinners are cast into the painful Lālābhakṣa hells, and likewise into hells in various places, again and again. ॥32॥
5.9.33: A sinful man devoid of merit is cast into the hell Sūcīmukha of great affliction and is beaten by Yama's servants. ॥33॥
5.9.34: Thrown into an iron pot, breathing ever more faintly, men are cooked by a great fire because of their own sins alone. ॥34॥
5.9.35: Bound tightly with ropes and the like, they are crushed on rocks, thrown into blind wells, and stung severely by bees. ॥35॥
5.9.36: With all their limbs pierced by worms and shattered a hundredfold, they are thereafter thrown into wells of very sharp caustic. ॥36॥
5.9.37: Here in the hell Mahājvāla the sinners cry out in misery; burned by its flames they run hither and thither. ॥37॥
5.9.38: Bringing their limbs round to the back, with the two ends joined and fastened at the shoulders, and drawing them tightly through the middle by the back of the arms, ॥38॥
5.9.39: all are bound very tightly to one another with noose-ropes; bound into bundles, they are seen undergoing torments in Mahājvāla. ॥39॥
5.9.40: Wrapped in ropes and smeared with mud, they are cooked in a fire of dung and chaff, yet they do not die. ॥40॥
5.9.41: Those sinners of very cruel conduct, having been dashed hundreds of times against rough rocks, are then cooked like grass. ॥41॥
5.9.42: Men are fiercely devoured by numerous sharp-mouthed worms that have entered inside their bodies, until their own bodies are wasted away. ॥42॥
5.9.43: Thrown into a mass of worms, into heaps of pus, flesh and bones, they remain with terrified hearts, crushed between two mountains. ॥43॥
5.9.44: The body is smeared with heated adamantine plaster, and, head down and feet up, they are scorched again and again by fire. ॥44॥
5.9.45: Helpless under another's control, they chew a red-hot iron club thrust inside their mouths, and they are beaten by them with hammers. ॥45॥
5.9.46: Thus, O Vyāsa, evil-doers are indeed tormented in the hells. Now I shall describe, for the sake of truth, the wretched disfigurement of those doers. ॥46॥
5.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The general description of the passage to hell, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
5.10.1: Sanatkumāra said: One who engages in false teaching goes to the hell called Dvijihva; there he is tormented by sharp ploughs half a krośa wide drawn across his tongue. ॥1॥
5.10.2: The cruel one who reviles his mother, father or teacher is beaten, his mouth filled with excrement mixed with worms. ॥2॥
5.10.3: Those men who damage Śiva's temples, gardens, step-wells, wells and ponds, and the dwelling of brahmins, and who amuse themselves there, ॥3॥
5.10.4: and, intoxicated with pride, practise there for pleasure rubbing with unguents, oil-massage, bathing, drinking water, eating, sport, sexual intercourse and gambling, ॥4॥
5.10.5: they are tormented by various terrible crushings, such as in sugarcane presses, and are cooked in the fires of hell until the dissolution of beings. ॥5॥
5.10.6: Adulterers are beaten in that very form in which they sinned; they are made to tightly embrace a red-hot woman made of iron. ॥6॥
5.10.7: And men in the shape of her former lovers, blazing on all sides, tightly embrace the unchaste woman, and they weep. ॥7॥
5.10.8: Those who listen to slander of the good have their ears stuffed with fire-coloured, heated iron nails, and ones made of copper and the like, ॥8॥
5.10.9: with molten tin, lead and brass, with boiling milk again and again, with very hot pungent oil, or again with adamantine cement. ॥9॥
5.10.10: Having filled the ears in succession, these torments take place in all the hells, one after another, on every side. ॥10॥
5.10.11: In the same way, for all the senses, terrible torments come in turn for each, according to the sin, and for what was done with the body. ॥11॥
5.10.12: Those deluded ones who, through the fault of touch, touch another man's wife have their hands violently filled with fire-coloured dust. ॥12॥
5.10.13: Their body is smeared all over with caustics and the like, and in all the hells there are torments of great pain. ॥13॥
5.10.14: Men who frown at their parents and make angry gestures with hands and eyes have their faces, inside and out, firmly studded with spikes. ॥14॥
5.10.15: With whatever senses men misbehave towards another's wife, those very senses of theirs are likewise mutilated by Yama's servants. ॥15॥
5.10.16: The lustful who stare at others' wives with fixed gaze have their eyes filled with fire-coloured needles, ॥16॥
5.10.17: and then with caustics and the like; all these torments of Yama take place right here in succession, O tiger among sages — truly, truly, without doubt. ॥17॥
5.10.18: Those who eat without first offering to the gods, fire, teachers and brahmins have their tongue and mouth filled with hundreds of heated iron nails. ॥18॥
5.10.19: Men who out of greed pluck by hand the flowers of the gods' gardens, smell them, and moreover wear them on their heads, ॥19॥
5.10.20: have their heads filled with heated iron spikes, and then their noses intensely with very abundant caustics and the like. ॥20॥
5.10.21: Those who revile the great-souled reciter, the teacher of dharma, devotees of the gods, fire and teachers, and the eternal dharma-śāstra — ॥21॥
5.10.22: in their chest and throat, tongue, the joints of the teeth, palate and lip, nose, head, and all the joints of the limbs, ॥22॥
5.10.23: fire-coloured, heated, three-pronged iron spikes are driven in many times with hammers at these places. ॥23॥
5.10.24: Then the body is filled all over with burning caustic, and great torments indeed befall the body on every side. ॥24॥
5.10.25: They pass again in succession through all the hells. Those who seize others' property and touch a brahmin with their feet, ॥25॥
5.10.26: or touch with the feet the implements of Śiva's worship, a cow, or whatever is written containing knowledge and the like — their hands, feet and so on are filled with torments all over. ॥26॥
5.10.27: And in all the hells there arise many strange and very painful torments, again and again, arising in the hands and feet. ॥27॥
5.10.28: Sinners who discharge excrement and urine within the precincts of Śiva's temple or anywhere in the gods' gardens — ॥28॥
5.10.29: their penis with the testicles is crushed with iron hammers, and likewise filled again with fire-coloured needles. ॥29॥
5.10.30: Then the embodied being's anus and penis are tightly filled again and again with a great quantity of sharp molten caustic. ॥30॥
5.10.31: Next, the sin from which suffering arises for the mind and all the senses: those who, out of craving, do not give gifts even though they have wealth, ॥31॥
5.10.32: and who disregard a guest arriving at the proper time while in the householder's stage — having incurred sin from that, they go to an impure hell. ॥32॥
5.10.33: Those who eat without giving food to dogs together with crows have their mouths forced open, pinned by a pair of pegs, ॥33॥
5.10.34: and they are tormented within by worms, fierce creatures, iron-beaked crows, and many kinds of fierce afflictions. ॥34॥
5.10.35: The offering formula: Śyāma and Śabala, the two who guard the path of Yama — to them I give this; may those two accept this offering. ॥35॥
5.10.36: And the crows of the west, north-west, south and south-west — crows of meritorious deeds — may they accept my offering. ॥36॥
5.10.37: Those who carefully worship Śivā, offer oblations into the fire according to rule, and give the bali-offering with Śaiva mantras do not see Yama; ॥37॥
5.10.38: they do not see him; they go to heaven. Therefore one should give the offering day after day. Having made a square maṇḍala scented with perfumes and the like, ॥38॥
5.10.39: one should place an offering for Dhanvantari in the north-east, for Indra in the east, for Yama in the south, for Varuṇa in the west, and for Soma (?) on the right side. ॥39॥
5.10.40: Having placed an offering for the Pitṛs, one should then place one for Aryaman in the east, and for Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ at the doorway. ॥40॥
5.10.41: He should scatter food on the ground for dogs, for dog-keepers and for birds. By gods, ancestors and humans, by pretas and bhūtas together with guhyakas, ॥41॥
5.10.42: by birds, worms and insects — the householder is relied upon for sustenance. The svāhā-call, the svadhā-call, the vaṣaṭ-call as the third, ॥42॥
5.10.43: and likewise the hanta-call as the other — these are the four teats of the cow. The gods drink from the svāhā teat, and likewise the ancestors from the svadhā, ॥43॥
5.10.44: likewise other gods and the lords of beings drink from the vaṣaṭ teat, and humans constantly drink from the hanta teat. ॥44॥
5.10.45: The man who, with faith and in proper order, constantly tends this cow at the right time, becomes fit for the status of one who keeps the sacred fire. ॥45॥
