5.10.46: But he who abandons it, or is negligent, sinks into Tāmisra hell. Therefore, having offered the bali to them, he should wait a moment standing at the door, reflecting. ॥46॥
5.10.47: A guest afflicted by hunger, even one living in the same village, he should duly feed with good food, according to his means, from his own meal. ॥47॥
5.10.48: He whose guest turns back from his house with hopes broken — that guest goes away, giving him his own sins and taking his merit. ॥48॥
5.10.49: Then the man who eats only the food he likes without sharing is again bound in chains; pierced here through the urge of his tongue, he remains for a long time. ॥49॥
5.10.50: For his flesh is cut out in pieces the size of a sesame seed and given to them to eat, and having pierced him, his blood too. ॥50॥
5.10.51: He is tormented again and again, thoroughly, with whips in succession, suffering great pain from hunger and likewise from extreme thirst. ॥51॥
5.10.52: Such and other extremely dreadful torments belong to those who do sinful deeds. What is attained at the end, hear that in brief. ॥52॥
5.10.53: He who commits a great sin and practises only a little dharma, or one whose dharma is weightier — hear the condition of these two. ॥53॥
5.10.54: The fruit of good deeds is not spoken of, owing to the force of the heavy sin; there, though endowed with many enjoyments, he does not obtain happiness. ॥54॥
5.10.55: So, anxious and greatly tormented, he finds no pleasure in foods, because of the lack of anything further before him, every morning, day after day. ॥55॥
5.10.56: The man of weighty dharma, even when fasting, like a wealthy householder, firm in his observances, does not feel distress. ॥56॥
5.10.57: There are those terrible sins by which a man on earth is split a hundredfold, like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt. ॥57॥
5.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The description of the passage to hell and of what is undergone there, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
5.11.1: Vyāsa said: Men who have committed sins travel the road of Yama burdened with great suffering. O lord, tell me the righteous deeds (dharmas) by which men travel that road in comfort. ॥1॥
5.11.2: Sanatkumāra said: A deed once done, good or bad, must certainly be experienced; there is no question about it. Now I shall tell you those righteous deeds that bring happiness. ॥2॥
5.11.3: Those men who here in this world do good deeds, who are gentle-minded and compassionate, travel happily along Yama's fearsome road. ॥3॥
5.11.4: The man who gives shoes and wooden sandals to eminent brahmins goes comfortably to Yama's abode on a great horse. ॥4॥
5.11.5: By giving an umbrella, embodied beings go along that road as if sheltered by an umbrella; by giving a palanquin one travels comfortably in such a vehicle. ॥5॥
5.11.6: By giving a bed and a seat one goes comfortably, well rested. Those who create shady groves or plant trees along the road go to Yama's world free of fatigue even in the scorching heat. ॥6॥
5.11.7: Men who lay out flower gardens travel in a Puṣpaka chariot; and those who build temples of the gods sport within a mansion. ॥7॥
5.11.8: Likewise those who build hermitages for ascetics and shelters for the destitute also sport within a mansion. ॥8॥
5.11.9: Men who worship the gods, the fire, the guru, brahmins, and their mother and father go on that road honoured, at their ease, in a vehicle that moves at will. ॥9॥
5.11.10: Those who give lamps go illuminating all the directions; by giving shelter to others men go happily, free from affliction. ॥10॥
5.11.11: Men who serve their guru go on that road resting along the way; those who give musical instruments to brahmins go happily, as if in their own home. ॥11॥
5.11.12: Givers of cows go as if provided with the fulfilment of every desire. Whatever food and drink a man has given here, he obtains on that road. ॥12॥
5.11.13: By providing water for washing the feet one travels on a road supplied with water; and he who massages others' feet with oil goes on horseback. ॥13॥
5.11.14: O Vyāsa, Yama does not approach the one who always gives foot-washing water, oil-massage, lamps, food and shelter. ॥14॥
5.11.15: By giving gold and gems one goes on, crossing over difficult places; by giving silver and oxen he reaches Yama's world with ease. ॥15॥
5.11.16: Through such gifts as these men go happily to Yama's abode, and in heaven they constantly obtain various enjoyments. ॥16॥
5.11.17: Of all gifts the gift of food is declared the highest: it gives immediate satisfaction, is pleasing to the heart, and increases strength and intelligence. ॥17॥
5.11.18: O best of sages, there is no gift equal to the gift of food. Living beings arise from food, and without it they die. ॥18॥
5.11.19: Blood, flesh, fat and semen develop from food in succession; from semen living beings are born. Therefore the world consists of food. ॥19॥
5.11.20: Even if they obtain gold, gems, horses, lordly elephants, women, garlands, sandal paste and all such things, the hungry take no delight in them. ॥20॥
5.11.21: Those in the womb, those being born, children, the old and the middle-aged, gods, Dānavas and Rākṣasas, all crave food. ॥21॥
5.11.22: Hunger is declared the foremost disease among all diseases, and here it is destroyed by the ointment of the medicine called food; there is no doubt. ॥22॥
5.11.23: There is no suffering equal to hunger, no disease equal to hunger, no happiness equal to health, and no enemy equal to anger. ॥23॥
5.11.24: Hence great merit is proclaimed in the gift of food, for all embodied beings, scorched by the fire of hunger, die. ॥24॥
5.11.25: The giver of food is called the giver of life, and the giver of life is the giver of everything. Therefore by giving food one obtains the fruit of all gifts. ॥25॥
5.11.26: When someone whose body has been nourished by another's food and drink accumulates merit, half of it belongs to that giver of food and half to the doer; there is no doubt. ॥26॥
5.11.27: Whatever jewels, enjoyments, women and vehicles exist in the three worlds, the giver of food obtains all that, both here and hereafter. ॥27॥
5.11.28: The body is the supreme means for dharma, wealth, desire and liberation. Therefore one should sustain one's body with food and drink. ॥28॥
5.11.29: They praise food alone; everything is founded on food. There has never been, nor will there ever be, a gift equal to food. ॥29॥
5.11.30: O sage, this entire universe is sustained by food. Food gives vigour in the world, for the life-breaths are founded on food. ॥30॥
5.11.31: One who desires his own prosperity should give food to a mendicant and to a high-souled brahmin, even at the cost of hardship to his family. ॥31॥
5.11.32: He who gives food to a supplicant, a distressed brahmin, lays up for himself the finest treasure for the next world. ॥32॥
5.11.33: A householder seeking prosperity should honour a brahmin who arrives at mealtime, weary from the road, coming to his house for sustenance. ॥33॥
5.11.34: O Vyāsa, the giver of food, good-natured and free of envy, should honour the guest, casting off any anger that has arisen; he gains great happiness in heaven and here. ॥34॥
5.11.35: One should not revile the one who has come, nor drive him away in any way. Even given to an outcaste (śvapāka) or a dog, the gift of food is never lost. ॥35॥
5.11.36: He who ungrudgingly gives food to a weary stranger, never seen before, who is on the road, attains prosperity. ॥36॥
5.11.37: O great sage, the man who gratifies the ancestors, the gods, brahmins and guests with food gains great fruit of merit. ॥37॥
5.11.38: The gift of food and drink is excellent whether to a śūdra or to a brahmin. One should not ask about the recipient's gotra, Vedic school, Vedic study or homeland. ॥38॥
5.11.39: The man who, when asked for alms by a brahmin here, gives him food goes to the highest heaven and stays there until the dissolution of beings. ॥39॥
5.11.40: For the giver of food, trees bearing the fruits of all desires come into being in heaven, just as the brahmins here are filled with joy by him. ॥40॥
5.11.41: O sage, the worlds that have been fashioned in heaven through the gift of food for the giver of food are exceedingly divine; listen to the description of them, O great sage. ॥41॥
5.11.42: In heaven the mansions of those great souls shine forth, of many shapes and forms and endowed with all kinds of desired things. ॥42॥
5.11.43: There are also trees standing beside the mansions that bear the fruit of every desire, golden ponds, auspicious wells, and long lakes everywhere. ॥43॥
5.11.44: And thousands of auspicious drinks proclaim themselves; there are mountains made of foods to be chewed and eaten, as well as garments and ornaments. ॥44॥
5.11.45: There are rivers flowing with milk, and likewise mountains of ghee, palaces of pale white radiance, and couches gleaming with gold. ॥45॥
5.11.46: Givers of food go to those worlds; therefore one should be a giver of food, if one desires one's own welfare in this world and the next. ॥46॥
5.11.47: These greatly radiant worlds belong to the meritorious givers of food; therefore food should certainly be given by humans, above all else. ॥47॥
5.11.48: Food is Prajāpati manifest; food is Viṣṇu, and Hara himself. Therefore there has never been, nor will there be, a gift equal to food. ॥48॥
5.11.49: Even having committed a very great sin, one who afterwards becomes a giver of food is freed from all sins and goes to the world of heaven. ॥49॥
5.11.50: Food, drink, horses, cows, garments, beds, umbrellas and seats—these eight gifts are especially commended for the world of the departed. ॥50॥
5.11.51: Since by such special gifts a man travels to the city of Dharmarāja in an aerial chariot, therefore one should practise giving. ॥51॥
5.11.52: Whoever reads this sinless account of the power of the gift of food, or causes others to read it, becomes prosperous. ॥52॥
5.11.53: O great sage, whoever listens to it, or recites it to Brāhmaṇas at a śrāddha, for him the gift of food reaches the ancestors as imperishable. ॥53॥
5.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The description of the greatness of the gift of food, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
5.12.1: Sanatkumāra said: The gift of water is supreme, always the best of gifts; it is held to be the refreshment and the life of all the multitudes of living beings. ॥1॥
5.12.2: Therefore one should, with great affection, provide a water-shed (prapā) open to all without restriction. Building a reservoir of water brings great joy. ॥2॥
5.12.3: It brings joy in this world or the next — truly, truly, there is no doubt. Therefore a man should have step-wells, wells and tanks constructed. ॥3॥
5.12.4: A well whose water flows removes half the sin of a man of wrong deeds, if it is kept constantly well-functioning. ॥4॥
5.12.5: He saves his whole lineage in whose dug reservoir cows, brāhmaṇas and good men always drink. ॥5॥
5.12.6: He whose water remains freely available in the hot season never meets with anything very difficult, perilous or distressing. ॥6॥
5.12.7: I shall also tell the merits that are declared for tanks that have been built. One who possesses a tank is honoured everywhere in the three worlds. ॥7॥
5.12.8: Or else, like friendship in a friend's house, free from the distress of friends — the establishing of tanks is excellent and produces fame. ॥8॥
5.12.9: The wise call it the fruit of dharma, artha and kāma. He by whom a tank is well made has endless merit. ॥9॥
5.12.10: A tank is the supreme refuge of the four kinds of beings; tanks and the like all bestow the highest prosperity. ॥10॥
5.12.11: Gods, humans, gandharvas, ancestors, nāgas and rākṣasas, and stationary beings too, take refuge in a reservoir. ॥11॥
5.12.12: He in whose tank water remains during the rainy season obtains the fruit of the agnihotra — so said the Self-born Brahmā. ॥12॥
5.12.13: He in whose tank water remains in autumn gains the fruit of giving a thousand cows; there is no doubt here. ॥13॥
5.12.14: He whose water remains in early winter and late winter obtains the fruit of a sacrifice with abundant gold. ॥14॥
5.12.15: For him whose water remains in spring and likewise in summer, the wise declare the fruit of the atirātra and aśvamedha sacrifices. ॥15॥
5.12.16: O sage Vyāsa, the fruit of reservoirs, the supreme delighting of living beings, has been told; now hear the merits of planting trees. ॥16॥
5.12.17: One who plants trees in a wilderness delivers all the generations of his ancestral line, past and future; therefore one should plant trees. ॥17॥
5.12.18: These trees become his sons there, no doubt about it; and he, having gone to the other world, attains imperishable worlds. ॥18॥
5.12.19: Trees worship all the hosts of gods with their flowers, the ancestors with their fruits, and all guests with their shade. ॥19॥
5.12.20: Kinnaras, serpents, rākṣasas, gods, gandharvas and humans, and likewise the hosts of sages, take shelter in trees. ॥20॥
5.12.21: Flowering and fruit-bearing, they satisfy people here; in this world and the next they are regarded, by dharma, as sons. ॥21॥
5.12.22: The maker of tanks, the planter of trees, the twice-born who has performed sacrifices, and others who speak the truth — these do not fall from heaven. ॥22॥
5.12.23: Truth alone is the supreme Brahman, truth alone the supreme austerity, truth alone the supreme sacrifice, truth alone the supreme scripture. ॥23॥
5.12.24: Truth stays awake among those who sleep; truth is the supreme state. By truth the earth is upheld; in truth everything is established. ॥24॥
5.12.25: Austerity, sacrifice and merit, in the worship of gods, sages and ancestors, water and knowledge — all of these, everything, rests on truth. ॥25॥
5.12.26: Truth is sacrifice, austerity, charity, the mantras and the goddess Sarasvatī; truth likewise is celibacy, and truth indeed is the syllable Om. ॥26॥
5.12.27: By truth the wind blows, by truth the sun gives heat, by truth fire burns, by truth heaven endures. ॥27॥
5.12.28: The preservation of all the Vedas and bathing in all the holy places — one who conducts himself by truth in the world obtains all this without doubt. ॥28॥
5.12.29: A thousand aśvamedhas and truth were weighed in the balance — even with hundreds of thousands of rites, truth alone outweighs. ॥29॥
5.12.30: By truth gods, ancestors, humans, serpents and rākṣasas are pleased; through truth all the worlds with moving and unmoving beings are pleased. ॥30॥
5.12.31: They call truth the supreme dharma, they call truth the supreme state, they call truth the supreme Brahman; therefore one should always speak the truth. ॥31॥
5.12.32: Sages devoted to truth, having performed very arduous austerity, devoted to the dharma of truth, became perfected, and thereupon went to heaven. ॥32॥
5.12.33: They went in aerial chariots filled with hosts of apsarases, with attendants all around. One should always speak the truth; nothing is higher than truth. ॥33॥
5.12.34: One should bathe, with a concentrated mind, in the fathomless, vast, perfected holy ford of truth, the pure lake; that place is regarded as supreme. ॥34॥
5.12.35: Those people who do not speak falsehood, whether for their own sake, for another's, or even for a son's sake — those men go to heaven. ॥35॥
5.12.36: The Vedas, sacrifices and mantras always abide in brāhmaṇas, but they do not shine in the untruthful; therefore one should practise truth. ॥36॥
5.12.37: Vyāsa said: O one rich in austerity, tell me again, in particular, the fruit of austerity for all the classes and for brāhmaṇas. ॥37॥
5.12.38: Sanatkumāra said: I shall expound the chapter on austerity, which accomplishes all desires and aims, and which is very hard for the twice-born to practise; hear it as I relate it. ॥38॥
5.12.39: Austerity is declared to be supreme; by austerity the fruit is attained. Those who are ever devoted to austerity rejoice together with the gods. ॥39॥
5.12.40: By austerity heaven is attained, by austerity fame is attained, by austerity one's desire is attained; austerity is the means to every aim. ॥40॥
5.12.41: By austerity one attains liberation; by austerity one obtains what is great: a wealth of knowledge and realised wisdom, good fortune, and beauty as well. ॥41॥
5.12.42: A man obtains things of many kinds through austerity; through austerity he obtains everything, whatever he desires in his mind. ॥42॥
5.12.43: Those who have not performed austerity never go to the world of Brahmā; Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, is not attainable by those who have not performed austerity. ॥43॥
5.12.44: Whatever purpose a person resolves upon when he performs austerity, all that the man attains, both in the next world and here. ॥44॥
5.12.45: The drinker of liquor, the adulterer with another's wife, the slayer of a brāhmaṇa, the violator of the teacher's bed — through austerity such a one crosses over everything and is freed on every side. ॥45॥
5.12.46: Even Sthāṇu, the lord of all, and the eternal Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Agni, Śakra, and others too are endowed with austerity. ॥46॥
5.12.47: Eighty-eight thousand sages of upward-drawn seed (celibates) rejoice in heaven through austerity, united with the gods. ॥47॥
5.12.48: Through austerity sovereignty is obtained; and that Śakra, lord of the gods, the slayer of Vṛtra, protected everything day after day through austerity. ॥48॥
5.12.49: The two gods Sun and Moon, devoted to the welfare of all worlds, shine through austerity alone; so also the stars and the planets. ॥49॥
5.12.50: Indeed there is no happiness in the world that comes without austerity; all happiness comes through austerity alone — so the knowers of the Veda know. ॥50॥
5.12.51: Knowledge, realised wisdom, health, and likewise beauty and good fortune — and happiness at all times — are obtained through austerity. ॥51॥
5.12.52: By austerity the universe is created — Brahmā creates the universe without toil; Viṣṇu protects it, Hara too devours it, and Śeṣa bears the entire earth. ॥52॥
5.12.53: O great sage, Viśvāmitra, son of Gādhi, a kṣatriya, then became a brāhmaṇa through austerity alone; this is renowned in the three worlds. ॥53॥
5.12.54: Thus, O greatly wise one, the supreme greatness of austerity has been told to you; now hear the greatness of Vedic study, which is superior to and higher than austerity. ॥54॥
5.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The description of the greatness of austerity, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
5.13.1: Sanatkumāra said: Whoever practises austerity in the forest, living on wild roots and fruits, and whoever studies even a single Ṛc verse — the fruit of the latter would be equal to that, O sage. ॥1॥
5.13.2: Whatever merit the best of the twice-born obtains from studying the Veda, he enjoys double that fruit from teaching it. ॥2॥
5.13.3: Just as the world becomes lightless without moon and sun, so is it without the Purāṇa; therefore, O sage, it should always be studied. ॥3॥
5.13.4: He who, by means of the scripture, awakens the world that is constantly tormented in hell through ignorance — therefore the one versed in the Purāṇa is worthy of honour. ॥4॥
5.13.5: Among all worthy recipients, the knower of the Purāṇa is the best; because he protects (trāyate) from falling (patana), he is therefore called a pātra (worthy recipient). ॥5॥
5.13.6: One should never regard a knower of the Purāṇa as a mere mortal; the knower of the Purāṇa is all-knowing — he is Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara, the guru. ॥6॥
5.13.7: Wealth, grain, gold and various garments should be given to the knower of the Purāṇa, for welfare here and hereafter. ॥7॥
5.13.8: The good man who with great affection gives auspicious things to the knower of the Purāṇa, a worthy recipient, attains the supreme state. ॥8॥
5.13.9: Hear the meritorious fruit of one who gives to a worthy recipient land, a cow, chariots, and fine elephants and horses. ॥9॥
5.13.10: That man obtains imperishable fulfilment of all desires, both in this birth and hereafter, and also the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice. ॥10॥
5.13.11: He who gives him land that is ploughed, fruitful and good, indeed delivers ten generations of his line before and ten after. ॥11॥
5.13.12: Having enjoyed all desires here, at the end, possessing a divine body, he goes to Śivaloka in a divine aerial car. ॥12॥
5.13.13: The gods are not so pleased by sacrifices, nor by sprinklings, offerings or flower-worship, as by the reading of the sacred book. ॥13॥
5.13.14: Whoever causes a religious book to be read in a temple of Śambhu, or of Viṣṇu, the Sun, or any god — hear the fruit of that too. ॥14॥
5.13.15: That man obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices, and swiftly piercing through the world of the Sun, he goes to Brahmaloka. ॥15॥
5.13.16: Having stayed there for hundreds of kalpas, he becomes a king on earth and enjoys pleasures free of hindrance; there is no need for doubt about this. ॥16॥
5.13.17: Whatever fruit is declared for a thousand Aśvamedhas, that fruit he obtains who performs japa before the deity. ॥17॥
5.13.18: Apart from the Itihāsa and Purāṇa recited in the auspicious temple of Śambhu, nothing else is so pleasing to Śambhu and likewise to the other gods. ॥18॥
5.13.19: Therefore the reading of the book should be done with every effort; likewise, hearing it with love grants the fruit of all desires. ॥19॥
5.13.20: By hearing the Purāṇa of Śambhu a man becomes sinless; having enjoyed abundant pleasures, he would attain Śivaloka. ॥20॥
5.13.21: Whatever merit comes from the Rājasūya and from a hundred Agniṣṭomas, that merit one obtains merely by hearing the story of Śambhu. ॥21॥
5.13.22: The fruit of bathing in all sacred waters and of giving a crore of cows — that fruit one obtains by hearing the story of Śambhu, O sage. ॥22॥
5.13.23: Those who always listen to the story of Śambhu, which purifies the worlds, should not be regarded as humans; they are Rudras indeed, without doubt. ॥23॥
5.13.24: The sages know the very dust of the lotus-feet of the good who listen to Śiva's noble glory and who proclaim it to be sacred places (tīrthas). ॥24॥
5.13.25: Embodied beings who long to reach the state of the highest good should always listen with devotion to the Purāṇic story of Śiva. ॥25॥
5.13.26: If one is unable to hear the Purāṇic story constantly, then, self-restrained, he should hear it daily, even for a short while (a muhūrta). ॥26॥
5.13.27: If a man is unable to hear it daily, O sage, he should hear the story of Śaṅkara in the holy months and other sacred times. ॥27॥
5.13.28: O lord of sages, a man who listens to the story of Śiva crosses over saṃsāra, having burnt the great forest of karma. ॥28॥
5.13.29: Men who with devotion listen to the story of Śiva for a muhūrta, or half of that, or even a moment, will meet no evil fate. ॥29॥
5.13.30: Whatever merit there is in all gifts or in all sacrifices, O sage, that fruit becomes steadfast through hearing the Purāṇa of Śambhu. ॥30॥
5.13.31: Especially in the Kali age, O Vyāsa, no higher dharma for men, devoted to meditation on liberation, is taught than hearing the Purāṇa. ॥31॥
5.13.32: Hearing the Purāṇa of Śambhu and likewise chanting his name are, for men, the delightful fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree, without doubt. ॥32॥
5.13.33: In the Kali age, for the welfare of dull-witted men whose minds have abandoned dharma and right conduct, Śambhu created the nectar-essence called the Purāṇa. ॥33॥
5.13.34: A man who drinks nectar becomes free from age and death alone; but by drinking the nectar of Śambhu's story, his whole family becomes free from age and death. ॥34॥
5.13.35: The state that belongs to the virtuous, to sacrificers and to ascetics — that state, dear one, is quickly attained indeed by hearing the Purāṇa. ॥35॥
5.13.36: When the attainment of knowledge does not come, the treatises on yoga should be studied with effort, and the Purāṇic scripture should indeed be heard. ॥36॥
5.13.37: Through hearing the Purāṇa, sin constantly diminishes and dharma grows; the man of knowledge does not fall into saṃsāra. ॥37॥
5.13.38: Therefore the Purāṇas should be heard with effort, for gaining dharma, wealth and desire, and likewise for attaining the path to liberation. ॥38॥
5.13.39: Whatever fruit comes from sacrifices, gifts, austerities and from resorting to sacred places — that fruit a man obtains by hearing the Purāṇa. ॥39॥
5.13.40: If the Purāṇas, which are the eyes for seeing the path of dharma, did not exist, then who here — even one keeping vows — would abide by or know the account of the world beyond? ॥40॥
5.13.41: Whoever, endowed with devotion, listens to or reads even one among the twenty-six Purāṇas is liberated; there is no doubt about this. ॥41॥
5.13.42: No other path bestowing happiness is seen; the path of the Purāṇas is indeed always the best. Without scripture all this does not shine, like the worlds of living beings deprived of the sun. ॥42॥
5.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The description of the greatness of the Purāṇa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
5.14.1: Sanatkumāra said: The formidable gifts and the great gifts are praised. They should always be given to worthy recipients, and they deliver one's own self, the donor. ॥1॥
5.14.2: O best of the twice-born, the gift of gold, the gift of a cow and the gift of land: those who receive these purifying gifts deliver both themselves and him the giver. ॥2॥
5.14.3: The gift of gold, the gift of a cow, and the gift of land: having made these excellent gifts, one is freed from sins. ॥3॥
5.14.4: Gifts of equal worth are praised: cows, land and Sarasvatī knowledge. Two are praised as equal in power, but Sarasvatī is superior. ॥4॥
5.14.5: Oxen, cows, an umbrella, clothing, a pair of sandals, as well as drink and food, should always be given to those who ask. ॥5॥
5.14.6: Whatever wealth, designated by a formal resolve, is given to brahmins and to supplicants in distress—by that one becomes noble-minded. ॥6॥
5.14.7: Gold, sesame, elephants, a maiden, a female servant, a house, a chariot, gems, and tawny cows: these indeed are the ten great gifts. ॥7॥
5.14.8: A brahmin who knows true knowledge, on accepting all these, at once delivers the generous donors and himself as well; there is no doubt. ॥8॥
5.14.9: Men who give gold with a pure mind—the deities bestow blessings upon such a one from all sides; so I have heard. ॥9॥
5.14.10: Agni indeed is all the deities, and gold is Agni (the fire). Therefore, by giving gold, all the deities are in effect given. ॥10॥
5.14.11: The gift of land is supremely excellent, bestowing the fruit of all desires—especially the gift of a golden earth, which was performed by Pṛthu of old. ॥11॥
5.14.12: Those who witness the earth being given along with gold are freed from all sins and go to the supreme state. ॥12॥
5.14.13: Now I shall describe another gift, the best of all, O sage, by which people do not see Yama's wilderness, which brings much suffering. ॥13॥
5.14.14: With a pure mind one should perform the wilderness gift according to rule, with wealth earned justly, free from miserliness with money. ॥14॥
5.14.15: Having made a cow out of a prastha of sesame, endowed with all good qualities, and a calf for the cow of gold, very splendid, bearing all auspicious marks, ॥15॥
5.14.16: and having made an eight-petalled lotus with auspicious unbroken rice-grains smeared with saffron, one should worship there all the gods beginning with Rudra with deep devotion. ॥16॥
5.14.17: Having thus worshipped, one should give that cow, with gems and gold and adorned with all ornaments, to a brahmin according to one's means. ॥17॥
5.14.18: Then one should eat only at night and give lamps in abundance. This should be carefully performed on the full-moon day of Kārttika. ॥18॥
5.14.19: Whoever does this properly, according to the rite and to his means, does not see the dreadful fear of Yama's road, nor hell. ॥19॥
5.14.20: Even having committed sins without number, he, with his kinsmen and friends, sports in heaven, O Vyāsa, for as long as fourteen Indras reign. ॥20॥
5.14.21: The gift of a cow made according to rule is regarded here as the best of all; O Vyāsa, no higher gift equal to it has been declared. ॥21॥
5.14.22: Whoever gives a tawny cow with her calf, with gold-tipped horns, with a bronze milking vessel, with silver hooves, marked with all auspicious signs— ॥22॥
5.14.23: that cow, through those very qualities, becomes a wish-yielding cow and comes to that man, the giver, O Vyāsa, in the next world and in this life. ॥23॥
5.14.24: Whatever is most desired in the world and whatever is dear in one's home—that should be given to a virtuous person by one who wishes that very thing to be imperishable. ॥24॥
5.14.25: The gift of the Tulāpuruṣa (one's own weight on the balance) is indeed the highest gift among gifts. If one desires one's own welfare, one should mount the balance. ॥25॥
5.14.26: By performing it one is freed from sins arising from killing and binding others. The balance-gift is of great merit and destroys all sins. ॥26॥
5.14.27: Whoever, having committed sins without number, performs the balance-gift is freed from all sins and goes to heaven without doubt. ॥27॥
5.14.28: Whatever sin was committed by day or at night, at the two twilights, at midday or at the end of night, in the three times, by body, mind and speech—the Tulāpuruṣa indeed removes it. ॥28॥
5.14.29: Whatever sin was committed by me as a child, as an old man, as a youth, knowingly, or even while devoted to knowledge—may the Tulāpuruṣa, the foe of Smara (Śiva), swiftly take away all that sin of mine. ॥29॥
5.14.30: The wealth bestowed by me today on a worthy recipient, full in measure, placed on the balance—together with it may whatever remaining merit of mine, done or not done, come to me. ॥30॥
5.14.31: Sanatkumāra said: Having uttered this, one, ever well-disposed, should give it to brahmins. It should not be given to a single one; otherwise there would be no deliverance from it. ॥31॥
5.14.32: Whoever, O Vyāsa, gives the excellent Tulāpuruṣa in this way, having destroyed his sin, would abide in a divine state for as long as fourteen Indras reign. ॥32॥
5.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The description of gifts in general, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
5.15.1: Vyāsa said: Tell me, for the welfare of human beings, that one gift which, when given alone, yields the fruit of all gifts. ॥1॥
5.15.2: Sanatkumāra said: Listen: from even a single gift given at the proper time, people obtain the fruit of all gifts. I shall tell you that. ॥2॥
5.15.3: The highest of all gifts is the gift of the Brahmāṇḍa (cosmic egg); it should be given by people who desire liberation, for crossing over saṃsāra. ॥3॥
5.15.4: Whatever fruit a man obtains when the whole Brahmāṇḍa is given, he obtains from that single gift; he becomes lord of the seven worlds. ॥4॥
5.15.5: As long as the moon and sun remain in the sky, or as long as the earth stands firm, so long does that man, the giver of the Brahmāṇḍa, together with his kinsmen, sport in the abode of the heaven-dwellers, in all the regions that follow his wishes; afterwards he goes, for joy, to the abode of Mādhava, which is very hard to attain even for the gods. ॥5॥
5.15.6: Vyāsa said: O Lord, tell me of the Brahmāṇḍa: of what measure it is, of what nature, on what it rests and how it came to be, so that I may have clear understanding. ॥6॥
5.15.7: Sanatkumāra said: O sage, listen; I shall declare in brief the height and extent of the Brahmāṇḍa; having heard it, one is freed from sin. ॥7॥
5.15.8: That which is the unmanifest cause, and also manifest, auspicious (Śiva) and free from ill — from that, having become twofold in the course of time, Brahmā is born. ॥8॥
5.15.9: Brahmā creates the Brahmāṇḍa consisting of fourteen worlds. I shall describe it in order, dear one, in brief; listen attentively. ॥9॥
5.15.10: There are seven Pātālas, and likewise seven worlds above; the height of that universe, which stands in the midst of the waters, is twofold. ॥10॥
5.15.11: Its support is the serpent, and he is declared to be Viṣṇu; on account of Brahmā's words he bears all this. ॥11॥
5.15.12: Neither gods nor dānavas are able to recount the virtues of this Śeṣa, who is called Ananta by the Siddhas and is worshipped by hosts of divine sages. ॥12॥
5.15.13: Possessing a thousand heads, he illumines all the directions with the thousand jewels of his hoods, adorned with spotless svastika marks. ॥13॥
5.15.14: His eyes rolling with intoxication, he shines like a white mountain with fire; garlanded and crowned, he always wears a single earring. ॥14॥
5.15.15: Clad in blue, overflowing with intoxication, he is like a white mountain adorned by the stream of the celestial Gaṅgā with its clouds — like a second Kailāsa mountain. ॥15॥
5.15.16: The tip of his hand resting on a plough, holding an excellent pestle, he is worshipped reverently by golden-hued serpent maidens. ॥16॥
5.15.17: He is Rudra in the form of Saṅkarṣaṇa, blazing with flames of poison-fire; at the end of the kalpa, flames of fire issue repeatedly from his mouths and, having burnt the three worlds, become quiet — so we have heard. ॥17॥
5.15.18: That Śeṣa, lord of beings, worshipped for his countless virtues, dwells at the root of Pātāla, bearing the circle of the earth on his back. ॥18॥
5.15.19: The power of his might cannot be described, nor his true form even be known, even by the eager gods. ॥19॥
5.15.20: Who can tell the might of him on whom this entire earth rests like a garland of flowers, reddened by the rays of his hood-jewels? ॥20॥
5.15.21: When Ananta yawns, his eyes rolling with intoxication, then this earth with its mountains, oceans and forests trembles. ॥21॥
5.15.22: Each Pātāla, O best of sages, is ten thousand yojanas in extent: Atala, Vitala, Sutala and Rasātala, ॥22॥
5.15.23: Tala, Talātala, and the foremost, Pātāla, held to be the seventh. These seven worlds below the earth should be known by the wise. ॥23॥
5.15.24: Their height is double; all of them have grounds of jewels; the palaces are jewelled and the grounds are made of gold. ॥24॥
5.15.25: In them dwell Dānavas and Daityas, likewise the races of Nāgas, great serpents, and Rākṣasas born of Daityas. ॥25॥
5.15.26: Nārada, having come from them to heaven, declared in the midst of the heavenly assembly: The Pātālas are far more delightful than the heaven-world. ॥26॥
5.15.27: Where there are ornaments of many kinds and radiant jewels, bright and gladdening — what can equal that Pātāla? ॥27॥
5.15.28: Who, even if liberated, would not feel delight in Pātāla, adorned here and there with Daitya and Dānava maidens? ॥28॥
5.15.29: Where there are no rays of the sun by day nor of the moon by night, where there is neither cold nor heat — here there is only the radiance of jewels. ॥29॥
5.15.30: Where foods to be chewed and eaten, rice and drinks are enjoyed abundantly by the joyful, and time, though passing, is not noticed, O best of sages. ॥30॥
5.15.31: Where there is the call of the male cuckoo, lotuses and lotus-ponds, rivers, delightful lakes and charming garments, ॥31॥
5.15.32: very bright ornaments and fragrant unguents, the sounds of lutes, flutes and drums, and songs, O brāhmaṇa. ॥32॥
5.15.33: And in Pātāla these pleasures are enjoyed by Daityas and serpents; they are attained through austerity by Dānavas, Siddhas and humans. ॥33॥
5.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The description of the Pātāla worlds, in the account of the universe, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
5.16.1: Sanatkumāra said: And hear from me, O best of eminent sages, about those hells situated above their heads, where sinners are cooked. ॥1॥
5.16.2: Raurava, Śūkara, Rodha, Tāla, Vivasana, likewise Mahājvāla, Taptakumbha, Lavaṇa and also Vilohita; ॥2॥
5.16.3: Vaitaraṇī, Pūyavahā, Kṛmiśa, Kṛmibhojana, the dreadful Asipatravana, and the terrible Lālābhakṣa; ॥3॥
5.16.4: Likewise Pūyavaha, Prāya, Vahnijvāla, Adhaśśiras, Sandaṃśa, Kālasūtra, Tamas, Avīci and Rodhana; ॥4॥
5.16.5: Then Śvabhojana, Ruṣṭa, Mahāraurava and Śālmalī — these and many others are the hells there, which bring suffering. ॥5॥
5.16.6: In them are cooked those men who delight in sinful deeds. I shall tell of them in order, O Vyāsa; listen attentively. ॥6॥
5.16.7: He who gives false testimony, except for the sake of brahmins, gods and cows, and he who always speaks untruth — that man goes to Raurava. ॥7॥
5.16.8: The killer of an embryo, the stealer of gold, the confiner of cows, the betrayer of trust, the drinker of liquor, the slayer of a brahmin, the stealer of others' property — ॥8॥
5.16.9: and whoever associates with them — he, when dead, goes to hell, O Vyāsa, as also for killing a guru. Into Taptakumbha goes the seller of a sister, mother, cow or daughter, ॥9॥
5.16.10: and the seller of a chaste woman. The usurer and the seller of hair are cooked in Taptaloha, as is he who abandons a devotee. ॥10॥
5.16.11: The vilest of men who despises his elders and eats selfishly afterwards, the defiler of the gods, and he who sells images of the gods, ॥11॥
5.16.12: and he who goes to forbidden women — at the end goes to Saptabala, O twice-born. The thief, the cow-killer, the outcast, and likewise the violator of moral bounds, ॥12॥
5.16.13: the hater of gods, brahmins and ancestors, and he who spoils gems — he goes to Kṛmibhakṣa; the performer of evil sacrifices eats worms. ॥13॥
5.16.14: The vilest man who eats before offering to the ancestors, gods and deities — that fool goes to Lālābhakṣa, as does the man who falsifies the scriptures. ॥14॥
5.16.15: He who is attended by an outcaste, the twice-born who accepts from the wicked, the one who sacrifices for those unfit to sacrifice, and likewise the eater of forbidden food — ॥15॥
5.16.16: these fall into Rudhiraugha, as do those who sell Soma. The destroyer of honey -hives and the destroyer of villages goes to the cruel river Vaitaraṇī. ॥16॥
5.16.17: Those intoxicated by fresh youth and those who break moral bounds go to Kṛmya, as do the impure and those who live off unchaste women. ॥17॥
5.16.18: He who cuts trees needlessly goes to Asipatravana. Keepers of rams and hunters of deer fall into Vahnijvāla. ॥18॥
5.16.19: The brahmin, kṣatriya or vaiśya whose conduct is corrupt goes at the end to that very place, O twice-born, as does he who gives fire to Śvapākas. ॥19॥
5.16.20: Those who break vows and those who have fallen from their own āśrama fall into the exceedingly dreadful torment of Sandaṃśa. ॥20॥
5.16.21: Celibate students who spill semen in dreams, and those by whom sons are not taught, fall into Śvabhojana. ॥21॥
5.16.22: These and other hells, by hundreds and thousands, exist, in which evildoers, subjected to torments, are cooked. ॥22॥
5.16.23: Likewise there are these sins and others by thousands, whose fruits are endured by men dwelling in the various hells. ॥23॥
5.16.24: Men who perform acts contrary to the duties of varṇa and āśrama, by deed, mind or speech, fall into hell. ॥24॥
5.16.25: The denizens of hell are seen by the deities in heaven as having their heads downward; the denizens of hell see all the gods below them, faces turned downward. ॥25॥
5.16.26: Immobile beings, worms, water-born creatures, birds, beasts, men, the righteous, the gods, and likewise those seeking liberation — each more numerous than the next in due order. ॥26॥
5.16.27: As many creatures as are in heaven, so many are the dwellers in hell. The sinner who turns away from expiation goes to hell. ॥27॥
5.16.28: Grave expiations for grave sins and light ones for light sins — so declared Svāyambhuva Manu, O Kāleya. ॥28॥
5.16.29: Of all those deeds that have been declared as expiations for all of them, the supreme and complete expiation is the constant remembrance of Hara. ॥29॥
5.16.30: For the man in whom remorse arises after a sin is committed, the one supreme expiation is the remembrance of Śiva. ॥30॥
5.16.31: Remembering Śiva at midday and other times — at dawn, at night and at twilight — a man attains the Māheśvara state and becomes one whose sins are destroyed. ॥31॥
5.16.32: Merely by remembering Śiva, that Śambhu, lord of Umā, one attains liberation or heaven, the complete destruction of all afflictions. ॥32॥
5.16.33: O chief of brahmins, for him no obstacle from sin — nor hindrance to japa, homa, worship and the like — arises anywhere in the three worlds, O best of sages. ॥33॥
5.16.34: He whose mind is fixed on Maheśvara during japa, homa, worship and the like — whatever merit there is, that is accomplished by him, with its fruit such as the lordship of the gods. ॥34॥
5.16.35: The man who remembers Śiva with devotion day and night does not go to hell, O sage, for he has all his sins destroyed. ॥35॥
5.16.36: Sin and merit are what are called hell and heaven, O best of the twice-born; of these two, one leads to suffering and the other to happiness and prosperity. ॥36॥
5.16.37: That very thing, having been a source of delight, becomes again a source of suffering. Therefore nothing is by nature suffering, nor is anything by nature happiness. ॥37॥
5.16.38: This is a transformation of the mind, marked by happiness and suffering. Knowledge alone is the supreme Brahman; knowledge leads to the truth. ॥38॥
5.16.39: This whole universe, with its moving and unmoving beings, is of the nature of knowledge. Nothing exists beyond supreme knowledge, O sage. ॥39॥
5.16.40: Thus I have described this entire circle of hells. Hereafter I shall now describe the sphere of the earth. ॥40॥
5.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The description of deliverance from hell, in the description of the universe, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
5.17.1: Sanatkumāra said: O son of Parāśara, listen as I describe, very briefly and properly, the sphere of the earth together with its seven continents and the rest. ॥1॥
5.17.2: Jambū, Plakṣa, Śālmali, Kuśa, Krauñca, Śāka, and Puṣkara as the seventh — all are surrounded by seven oceans. ॥2॥
5.17.3: The oceans are of salt water and sugarcane juice, ghee, curd, milk and fresh water. Jambūdvīpa stands in the middle of all these. ॥3॥
5.17.4: In its middle too, O Kāleya, is Meru, the golden mountain. It has entered sixteen thousand yojanas below the ground, and its height ॥4॥
5.17.5: is eighty-four thousand by those measures; at the summit it is extended thirty-two thousand. This is the mountain standing on the surface of the earth; its extent all around ॥5॥
5.17.6: at the base is sixteen thousand; it stands in the shape of the pericarp of a lotus. Himavān, Hemakūṭa and Niṣadha lie to its south. ॥6॥
5.17.7: Nīla, Śveta and Śṛṅgī are the boundary mountains (varṣa-parvata) in the north. These are of ten thousand yojanas, full of jewels, and of reddish lustre. ॥7॥
5.17.8: They are a thousand yojanas high and just as wide. Bhārata is known as the first region (varṣa), and after it Kimpuruṣa. ॥8॥
5.17.9: After that is another, Harivarṣa — these lie to the south of Meru, O sage. Ramyaka is on the northern side, and in its portion is Hiraṇmaya. ॥9॥
5.17.10: And in the north are the Kurus, just as Bhārata is in the south. Each of these is nine thousand yojanas, O best of sages. ॥10॥
5.17.11: Ilāvṛta is in the middle of them, and in its middle Meru rises high. Ilāvṛta extends there nine thousand yojanas in the four directions around Meru, ॥11॥
5.17.12: O best of seers. And here are four mountains, made as buttresses (viṣkambha) of Meru, joined to it and rising up again. ॥12॥
5.17.13: In the east is the one named Mandara, in the south Gandhamādana; Vipula stands in the western part and Supārśva in the north. ॥13॥
5.17.14: The Kadamba, the Jambū tree, the Pippala and the Vaṭa — trees eleven hundred yojanas in extent — are the banners of these mountains. ॥14॥
5.17.15: Listen, O great sage, to the reason for the name Jambūdvīpa. Great trees shine there; I shall tell you their nature. ॥15॥
5.17.16: The fruits of that Jambū tree, as large as great elephants, fall on the ridge of the mountain and burst open on every side. ॥16॥
5.17.17: From their juice there flows there a river famed as the Jambū river; it runs all around there and is drunk by those who dwell there. ॥17॥
5.17.18: No sweat, no foul odour, no old age, no seizure of the senses — none of that arises for the people who live on its bank. ॥18॥
5.17.19: And its juice, reaching the clay of the bank dried by pleasant winds, becomes the gold called Jāmbūnada, the ornament of the Siddhas. ॥19॥
5.17.20: Bhadrāśva lies to the east of Meru and Ketumāla to the west — these are two regions, O best of sages; between them is Ilāvṛta. ॥20॥
5.17.21: In the east is the forest Caitraratha, in the south Gandhamādana, likewise Vibhrāja in the west, and in the north Nandana is renowned. ॥21॥
5.17.22: Aruṇoda, Mahābhadra, Śītoda and Mānasa are renowned — these four lakes are in every way to be enjoyed by the gods. ॥22॥
5.17.23: Śītāñjana, Kuruṅga, Kurara and Mālyavān — headed by these, one after another, are the filament-mountains (kesarācala) to the east of Meru. ॥23॥
5.17.24: Trikūṭa, Śiśira, Pataṅga, Rucaka, Niṣadha, Kapila and others are the filament-mountains in the south. ॥24॥
5.17.25: Sinīvāsa, Kusumbha, Kapila, Nārada and the mountains beginning with Nāga are the filament-mountains in the west. ॥25॥
5.17.26: Śaṅkhacūḍa, then Ṛṣabha, the mountain named Haṃsa, and likewise Kālañjara and others are the filament-mountains in the north. ॥26॥
5.17.27: On top of Meru, in the middle, is the golden city of Brahmā (Vidhi), fourteen thousand yojanas in measure. ॥27॥
5.17.28: Around it, in due order, eight cities of the eight guardians of the worlds are arranged, each according to its direction and its form. ॥28॥
5.17.29: And into that city of Brahmā falls the river Gaṅgā, issuing from the foot of Viṣṇu, after flooding the orb of the moon. ॥29॥
5.17.30: Having fallen there, she became fourfold in the directions, in order: Sītā, Alakanandā, Cakṣu and Bhadrā. ॥30॥
5.17.31: Sītā goes to the east of the mountain, Nandā to the south, Cakṣu to the west, and Bhadrā to the north. ॥31॥
5.17.32: Passing over all the mountains, that Gaṅgā who travels the three paths, having become purified, went in the four directions to the great ocean. ॥32॥
5.17.33: Nīla and Niṣadha, and Mālyavān and Gandhamādana — in the midst of these stands Meru, shaped like the pericarp of a lotus. ॥33॥
5.17.34: Bhārata, Ketumāla, Bhadrāśva and the Kurus are the petals of the world-lotus; the boundary mountains are their limits. ॥34॥
5.17.35: Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa extend north–south in length; Gandhamādana and Kailāsa run east and west. ॥35॥
5.17.36: East and west of Meru stand Niṣadha and the Nīla mountain, stretching south and north, situated within the pericarp. ॥36॥
5.17.37: Jaṭhara and the others stand around Meru, set in pairs; these, Śveta and the rest, are the very lovely filament-mountains. ॥37॥
5.17.38: Between the mountains are valleys frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas, and in them are very delightful groves and cities. ॥38॥
5.17.39: These belong to all the gods, Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas; gods and Daityas sport day and night in those mountainous regions. ॥39॥
5.17.40: These are the abodes of the righteous, proclaimed as earthly heavens; doers of sin never go to them, nor do they ever see them. ॥40॥
5.17.41: O great sage, in the eight regions (varṣas) beginning with Kimpuruṣa there is no sorrow, no misfortune, no anxiety, nor hunger, fear and the like. ॥41॥
5.17.42: The people are healthy, free from dread, devoid of all suffering, and of stable lifespan, living ten or twelve thousand years. ॥42॥
5.17.43: And as for the ages Kṛta, Tretā and the rest, there is no such reckoning in those places; the waters everywhere are from the earth, and the god of rain does not rain upon them. ॥43॥
5.17.44: In these seven regions there are rivers, beautiful and with golden sands, by the hundreds, and small ones too; in them virtuous people would sport. ॥44॥
5.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The description of the varṣas of Jambūdvīpa, in the account of the universe, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
5.18.1: Sanatkumāra said: I shall describe the region (varṣa) Bhārata, which lies south of the Himālaya and north of the ocean, where the progeny of Bharata dwell. ॥1॥
5.18.2: Its extent, O great sage, is nine thousand yojanas. The wise regard it as the land of action for attaining heaven and final liberation. ॥2॥
5.18.3: From here men attain heaven and also hell. I now tell you the nine divisions of the region Bhārata. ॥3॥
5.18.4: Indradyumna, Kaseru, Tāmravarṇa, Gabhastimān, Nāgadvīpa, Saumya, Gandharva, and then Vāruṇa; ॥4॥
5.18.5: and this is the ninth of them, an island enclosed by the ocean. This island measures a thousand yojanas from south to north. ॥5॥
5.18.6: In its east live the Kirātas, in the south the Yavanas are settled, and likewise others are to be known in the west, while in the north are ascetics. ॥6॥
5.18.7: In the middle are Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras in large numbers, established in their livelihoods of sacrifice, warfare, trade and service. ॥7॥
5.18.8: Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Sudāmā, the Ṛkṣa mountain, Vindhya and Pāriyātra—these are the seven principal (kula) mountains here. ॥8॥
5.18.9: The rivers Vedasmṛti, Purāṇā and others arise from Pāriyātra, O sage; they are known to remove all sins by being seen and even by being touched. ॥9॥
5.18.10: Narmadā, Surasā and others—seven chief ones and thousands of others—are great rivers rising from the Vindhya, auspicious and removing all sins. ॥10॥
5.18.11: The rivers headed by Godāvarī, Bhīmarathī and Tāpī, issuing from the Ṛkṣa mountain, at once dispel sin and fear. ॥11॥
5.18.12: Likewise the rivers Kṛṣṇā, Veṇī and others rise from the foot of Sahya; those headed by Kṛtamālā and Tāmraparṇī rise from Malaya. ॥12॥
5.18.13: Triyāmā, Ṛṣikulyā and others are said to rise from Mahendra; Ṛṣikulyā, Kumārī and others arise from the foot of Śuktimat. ॥13॥
5.18.14: Various peoples dwell in those regions; they drink the water of these rivers and of various lakes. ॥14॥
5.18.15: In the region Bhārata, O great sage, there are the four ages, Kṛta and the rest; they do not prevail in the other continents. ॥15॥
5.18.16: Here gifts are given, and here virtuous sacrificers perform rites; ascetics practise austerity with devotion for the sake of the next world. ॥16॥
5.18.17: For this is the land of action in Jambūdvīpa, O great sage; and even here Bhārata is the best, whereas the other lands are lands of enjoyment. ॥17॥
5.18.18: Only rarely, O best of sages, does a mortal obtain human birth here, after thousands of births, through accumulations of merit. ॥18॥
5.18.19: The gods indeed sing songs: Blessed are they who live in the land of Bhārata, which is the path to the abode of heaven and liberation; even we gods become men there again. ॥19॥
5.18.20: Having surrendered all the fruits born of action unto Śambhu, whose form is the supreme Self, I shall attain oneness with his very being. ॥20॥
5.18.21: Blessed indeed are those men who will attain this, endowed with happiness and engaged in right action; those whose birth is in Bhārata gain both heaven and liberation. ॥21॥
5.18.22: I have described Jambūdvīpa, a hundred thousand yojanas in extent, perfectly circular, and well encircled by the salt ocean. ॥22॥
5.18.23: Encircling the salt ocean, which measures a hundred thousand yojanas, lies Plakṣadvīpa, said to be twice that in size, O Brahmin. ॥23॥
5.18.24: Gomanta, Candra, Nārada, Dardura, Somaka, the mountain Sumanas, and Vaibhrāja the excellent are its mountains. ॥24॥
5.18.25: On these lovely boundary mountains people live together constantly, and gods and Gandharvas always dwell in these regions. ॥25॥
5.18.26: There the people have no mental afflictions or diseases anywhere; men there live for ten thousand years. ॥26॥
5.18.27: Anutaptā, Śikhī, Pāpaghnī, Tridivā, Kṛpā, Amṛtā and Sukṛtā—these are the seven rivers here. ॥27॥
5.18.28: There are also thousands of small rivers and mountains there; the peoples, greatly delighted, drink from those rivers. ॥28॥
5.18.29: There too there is no succession of the ages; as in all the seven regions, time is always like the Tretā age, O great sage. ॥29॥
5.18.30: They are Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras, O best of sages. In its middle stands a very great tree, like the wish-fulfilling tree, ॥30॥
5.18.31: the Plakṣa; after its name the island is called Plakṣadvīpa, O best of the twice-born. There the Lord Śaṅkara, benefactor of the world, is worshipped, ॥31॥
5.18.32: as are Hari and Lord Brahmā, with yantras and Vedic mantras. Now hear from me, again in brief, about Śālmali. ॥32॥
5.18.33: There too are seven regions; hear their names from me: Śveta, Harita, Jīmūta, Rohita, ॥33॥
5.18.34: Vaikala, Mānasa, and Suprabha the seventh, O sage. Because of the Śālmala tree the island is called Śālmali. ॥34॥
5.18.35: It remains constantly surrounded by an ocean twice its size. The rivers mark out the regions; hear their names from me: ॥35॥
5.18.36: Śuklā, Raktā, Hiraṇyā, Candrā, Śubhrā, Vimocanā, and Nivṛtti the seventh of them—with holy, very cool waters. ॥36॥
5.18.37: Those seven regions are inhabited by the four classes, who ever worship the Lord Śambhu with various sacrifices. ॥37॥
5.18.38: In that most delightful land the gods are present. This island is surrounded by the ocean of wine (surā). ॥38॥
5.18.39: Beyond it on all sides lies Kuśadvīpa, twice as large. There dwell Daityas and Dānavas together with men, ॥39॥
5.18.40: and likewise gods, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Kimpuruṣas and others; there too are the four classes, each devoted to its own duties. ॥40॥
5.18.41: And right there in Kuśadvīpa they worship Brahmā and Janārdana, and likewise Īśāna, the giver of the fruits of all desires. ॥41॥
5.18.42: Its mountains are Kuśeśaya, Hari, Dyutimān and likewise Puṣpavān, Maṇidruma, Hemaśaila, and the seventh, Mount Mandara. ॥42॥
5.18.43: And there are seven rivers; hear their names truly: Dhūtapāpā, Śivā, Pavitrā, and likewise Sammiti, ॥43॥
5.18.44: Vidyā, Dambhā, and another, Mahī; these remove all sins. There are others by the thousands, with pure waters and golden sands. ॥44॥
5.18.45: In Kuśadvīpa there is a clump of kuśa grass; the island is surrounded by the ocean of ghee. O fortunate one, let the next great one, Krauñcadvīpa, be heard. ॥45॥
5.18.46: It is surrounded by an ocean of whey (curd-cream), twice its size. O wise one, hear from me the names of its regional mountains. ॥46॥
5.18.47: Krauñca and Vāmana, the third Andhakāraka, Divāvṛti, Manas, Puṇḍarīka and Dundubhi. ॥47॥
5.18.48: On those regional mountains, all golden and delightful, the people dwell free from fear, together with friendly hosts of gods. ॥48॥
5.18.49: Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras are named there in due order. There are seven great rivers there, and others by the thousands: ॥49॥
5.18.50: Gaurī, Kumudvatī, Sandhyā, Rātri, Manojavā, Śānti and Puṇḍarīkā, whose pure water the people drink. ॥50॥
5.18.51: There the Lord is worshipped in the form of Yoga-Rudra. And the ocean of whey is in turn surrounded by Śākadvīpa, ॥51॥
5.18.52: which is twice its size. It has seven mountains; hear their names from me. In the east there is the Udaya mountain, and beyond it Jaladhāra, ॥52॥
5.18.53: and at the back (west) the Asta mountain, as well as Avikeśa and Kesarī. There stands the great Śāka tree, frequented by Siddhas and Gandharvas. ॥53॥
5.18.54: There are holy countries there, endowed with the four social classes, and here are very holy rivers that remove all sins and fears: ॥54॥
5.18.55: Sukumārī, Kumārī, Nalinī and Veṇukā, Ikṣu, Reṇukā, and likewise Gabhasti the seventh. ॥55॥
5.18.56: O great sage, there are thousands of other small rivers there, and likewise mountains by the hundreds and thousands. ॥56॥
5.18.57: There is no decline of dharma among them. Men, having come from heaven, roam the earth together in those regions. ॥57॥
5.18.58: In Śākadvīpa the Sun is always worshipped with love by the peoples, properly, through the prescribed rites, by those of controlled self. ॥58॥
5.18.59: That island too is surrounded on all sides by the ocean of milk, twice its size; and the milk ocean, O Vyāsa, is surrounded all round by the island called Puṣkara, ॥59॥
5.18.60: which is twice its size. There is the great regional mountain famed here as Mānasa, rising fifty thousand yojanas upward, ॥60॥
5.18.61: and as many in extent on all sides, ring-shaped, as though dividing the ring of Puṣkaradvīpa through the middle. ॥61॥
5.18.62: By that very mountain the island takes the form of ring-shaped regions. There men live for ten thousand years, ॥62॥
5.18.63: free from disease, without sorrow, devoid of passion and hatred. Adharma is not known among them, O sage, nor captor and slayer. ॥63॥
5.18.64: Truth and falsehood as opposites do not exist there; it is ever a peaceful dwelling. The people are alike in dress, of one form, golden in colour. ॥64॥
5.18.65: And this region, O Kāleya, is earthly yet comparable to heaven. Time there gives happiness to all and is free from old age and disease. ॥65॥
5.18.66: In Puṣkara, in its regions Dhātakīkhaṇḍa and Mahāvīta, O great sage, in Puṣkaradvīpa there is a banyan tree, the supreme abode of Brahmā. ॥66॥
5.18.67: In it dwells Brahmā, worshipped by gods and asuras. Puṣkara is encircled by the ocean of sweet water. ॥67॥
5.18.68: Thus the seven islands are surrounded by the seven oceans; and the islands and oceans are matched by successive ones, each twice as large. ॥68॥
5.18.69: Their rise and excess has been stated; in the oceans the waters always remain the same; they never become diminished. ॥69॥
5.18.70: Just as water in a pot, resting below, swells through contact with fire, O best of sages, so when the moon waxes the water surely rises upward. ॥70॥
5.18.71: At the rising and setting of the moon the waters swell and subside; hence they are less and more in the bright and dark fortnights. ॥71॥
5.18.72: The rise and fall of the waters of all the oceans are seen to be a hundred and ten measures; this has been told to you, O best of sages. ॥72॥
5.18.73: In Puṣkaradvīpa, O brāhmaṇa, all the people always take as their food the sweet substance (khaṇḍa) that presents itself there of its own accord. ॥73॥
5.18.74: Beyond the sweet-water ocean there is no settlement of beings; there is a golden land, twice as large, devoid of all creatures. ॥74॥
5.18.75: Beyond that is the mountain Lokāloka; that mountain is so many thousands of yojanas in height and ten thousand yojanas in breadth. ॥75॥
5.18.76: Beyond lies darkness, enclosed by the shell of the cosmic egg. This earth, O great sage, with its islands and mountains, is fifty crores of yojanas in extent. ॥76॥
5.18.77: Being the support of all, surpassing all beings in qualities, this Ilā (Earth), O Kāleya, is the nourisher of all the worlds. ॥77॥
5.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The description of the seven dvīpas, in the account of the universe, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
5.19.1: Sanatkumāra said: As far as the rays of the sun and the moon illuminate, the earth is of that extent; it is called Bhūloka. ॥1॥
5.19.2: The orb of the sun is situated a hundred thousand yojanas from the earth; its measure is always reckoned in thousands of yojanas. ॥2॥
5.19.3: They likewise describe the measure of the moon of the world: the moon stands above the sun at a distance reckoned as a hundred thousand yojanas. ॥3॥
5.19.4: The entire sphere of the planets, together with the constellations, is situated above the moon, ten thousand yojanas higher all around. ॥4॥
5.19.5: Budha is above that, then Kāvya (Śukra); above him the sphere of Bhauma (Mars); above that Bṛhaspati, and above him Śanaiścara (Saturn). ॥5॥
5.19.6: The sphere of the Seven Sages is situated one hundred thousand yojanas beyond that; and a hundred thousand above the sages stands Dhruva. ॥6॥
5.19.7: That Dhruva is the pivot of the wheel of luminaries. The region above the earth and below Dhruva should be known as Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ. ॥7॥
5.19.8: One crore of yojanas above Dhruva is Maharloka, where dwell those who live for a kalpa. These seven sons of Brahmā dwell there: ॥8॥
5.19.9: Sanaka, Sananda, the third Sanātana, Kapila, Āsuri, Voḍhu, and likewise Pañcaśikha. ॥9॥
5.19.10: Above that, Śukra is situated within two hundred thousand yojanas; two hundred thousand yojanas below him is said to be the son of Soma (Budha). ॥10॥
5.19.11: Two hundred thousand yojanas above him stands Bhauma, O sage; two hundred thousand yojanas above that stands Jīva, the Guru (Jupiter). ॥11॥
5.19.12: Two hundred thousand yojanas above Jīva is placed Sauri (Saturn). These are declared the seven planets, each stationed in its own zodiacal sign. ॥12॥
5.19.13: At eleven (Rudra) hundred-thousand yojanas above stand the Seven Sages; the position of Dhruva is declared to be at thirteen (Viśva) hundred-thousand yojanas. ॥13॥
5.19.14: Four times further above Janaloka, Tapas-loka is said to be, where the Vairāja gods dwell, free from burning. ॥14॥
5.19.15: Six times beyond Tapoloka is set Satyaloka; it is to be known as Brahmaloka, where those of stainless mind dwell, ॥15॥
5.19.16: devoted to truth and dharma, wise, and celibate — those who have gone there; and humans dwell in Bhūloka. ॥16॥
5.19.17: In Bhuvarloka dwell perfected sages of divine form; in Svargaloka the gods: the Ādityas, Maruts, Vasus, the two Aśvins, ॥17॥
5.19.18: the Viśvedevas, likewise the Rudras, Sādhyas, Nāgas, birds and others; then there are the nine planets and the sages free from sin. ॥18॥
5.19.19: These seven great worlds have been told to you, O Kāleya, and the seven Pātālas too, and the extent of the cosmic egg. ॥19॥
5.19.20: Like the fruit of the wood-apple tree, it is round above and likewise below; this is enclosed on all sides by the shell of the egg. ॥20॥
5.19.21: That is enveloped on all sides by water ten times its size, and also by fire, air, ether and darkness likewise, ॥21॥
5.19.22: and by Bhūtādi and by Mahat, each tenfold greater in succession; and enveloping Mahat is Pradhāna, beyond which stands Puruṣa. ॥22॥
5.19.23: Of that infinite Supreme Self there is no reckoning at all; hence he is known as Ananta, since there is no measure of him. ॥23॥
5.19.24: That supreme Prakṛti is the cause of all, O sage. Thousands of thousands and tens of thousands of eggs— ॥24॥
5.19.25: many such have come forth from that unmanifest source. As fire is in wood, oil in sesame, and ghee in milk, ॥25॥
5.19.26: so this Supreme Self, self-aware, pervades all. From the primal seed they are produced; then from them other egg-born beings, ॥26॥
5.19.27: from them sons, and likewise from them other seeds of others. From Mahat down to the specific elements, thus arise the gods and the rest. ॥27॥
5.19.28: Just as there is no diminution of a tree through a tree sprouting from its seed, and as fire is produced from the sun-stone by the sun, ॥28॥
5.19.29: so creation comes forth, yet Śiva does not desire anything in it. Through the union of Śiva and Śakti the gods and others come into being. ॥29॥
5.19.30: Likewise, by their own karma alone they attain growth. He who is Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the Rudras — he is extolled as Śiva. ॥30॥
5.19.31: He from whom all comes forth and into whom all will dissolve, the doer of all actions — he is extolled as Śiva. ॥31॥
5.19.32: Vyāsa said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, dispel my great doubt: are there worlds above the cosmic egg or not, O sage? ॥32॥
5.19.33: Sanatkumāra said: There are indeed worlds above the cosmic egg, O lord of sages. Listen to them in detail; having come here, I shall tell you. ॥33॥
5.19.34: Beyond Brahmā's world is the world renowned as Vaikuṇṭha; it shines with great splendour, and there Viṣṇu is established. ॥34॥
5.19.35: Above that is the most wondrous Kaumāra world, where the radiant general, the son of Śambhu, shines. ॥35॥
5.19.36: Beyond that shines the supremely divine world of Umā, where the one Śakti, Śivā, mother of the three gods, is resplendent. ॥36॥
5.19.37: She is Prakṛti, higher than the highest, consisting of rajas, sattva and tamas; yet the Goddess herself is beyond the guṇas, changeless, of the nature of Śiva. ॥37॥
5.19.38: Above that is to be known the eternal Śivaloka, imperishable, supremely divine, ever endowed with great beauty, ॥38॥
5.19.39: where the supreme Brahman, Śambhu Maheśvara, shines — father of the three gods, lord of all, beyond the three guṇas. ॥39॥
5.19.40: Above that there are no worlds; near it is Goloka, where dwell the mother-cows called Suśīlā, dear to Śiva. ॥40॥
5.19.41: Its guardian, named Kṛṣṇa, shines there by Śaṅkara's command, established by Śiva himself, who moves freely by his own will, together with his Śakti. ॥41॥
5.19.42: O Vyāsa, the world of Śiva is wondrous, without any support, enchanting, likewise indescribable, and resplendent with manifold things. ॥42॥
5.19.43: Śiva himself is its presiding lord, the crest-jewel of all gods, to be served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Hara, the Supreme Self, stainless. ॥43॥
5.19.44: Thus, dear son, the arrangement of the whole cosmic egg has been told to you, and the arrangement of the worlds above it. What else do you wish to hear? ॥44॥
5.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The description of the worlds, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
5.20.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, O best of the virtuous, tell me how that state is attained, having reached which men endowed with devotion to Śiva do not return. ॥1॥
5.20.2: Sanatkumāra said: O Vyāsa, son of Parāśara, listen with affection to the auspicious goal: the vow of the pure devotees, and likewise the pure austerity of ascetics. ॥2॥
5.20.3: Those of pure deeds, endowed with very pure austerity, who constantly worship Śiva — they are worthy of reverence in every way, day after day. ॥3॥
5.20.4: Those who have not practised austerity do not reach Śiva's world, free from affliction. Austerity alone, O great sage, is the true cause of Śiva's grace. ॥4॥
5.20.5: By austerity the hosts of gods rejoice manifestly in heaven, and so do the seers and sages; know my words here to be true. ॥5॥
5.20.6: Whatever is very hard to bear, hard to propitiate, very far off, hard to overcome — all that is achievable by austerity, for austerity itself is insurmountable. ॥6॥
5.20.7: Brahmā is ever firmly established in austerity, and so are Viṣṇu and Hara; all the gods and goddesses have attained through austerity a fruit hard to obtain. ॥7॥
5.20.8: With whatever disposition one abides and performs austerity, from that austerity the corresponding result is obtained by them in this world; there is no doubt. ॥8॥
5.20.9: Austerity is traditionally held to be threefold — sāttvika, rājasa and tāmasa; O Vyāsa, it should be understood as the means of all means. ॥9॥
5.20.10: The sāttvika belongs to the gods and to celibate ascetics whose seed flows upward; the rājasa to the Dānavas and likewise to humans; the tāmasa to the Rākṣasas and to men of cruel deeds. ॥10॥
5.20.11: Its fruit is declared threefold by sages who see the truth. Japa, meditation and auspicious worship of the gods with devotion — ॥11॥
5.20.12: — that is designated sāttvika, accomplishing every fruit, the means to what the mind desires both in this world and the next. ॥12॥
5.20.13: Austerity aimed at the fruits of desires is called rājasa. Having severely tormented one's own body with unbearable practices that dry up the body — ॥13॥
5.20.14: — such austerity is declared tāmasa, a means to what the mind desires. ॥14॥
5.20.15: One should know the sāttvika to be the highest, and with it an unwavering righteous mind; bathing, worship, japa, fire-offering, pure cleanliness, non-violence, ॥15॥
5.20.16: the observance of vows and fasts, silence, restraint of the senses, intelligence, learning, truthfulness, freedom from anger, giving, forbearance, self-control, compassion, ॥16॥
5.20.17: the construction of step-wells, wells, tanks and the like, and of temples; the Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa penances, sacrifice, holy places of pilgrimage, and hermitages too — ॥17॥
5.20.18: these are the stations of dharma that bestow happiness on the wise; this is the supreme true dharma, O Vyāsa, and the cause of devotion to Śiva. ॥18॥
5.20.19: Let the yogic union of saṅkrānti and viṣuvat (the shifting and balancing of the breath) be applied in the state freed from sound (nāda); meditation at the three junctures of the day, contemplation of light, and holding the state of unmanī — ॥19॥
5.20.20: exhalation, inhalation and retention — prāṇāyāma is held to be threefold; knowledge of the movement through the channels (nāḍī), and restraint through withdrawal of the senses (pratyāhāra) — ॥20॥
5.20.21: the fourth state (turīya), and below it the intellect, accompanied by the eight powers beginning with aṇimā — this is declared superior to the former, the means to supreme knowledge. ॥21॥
5.20.22: The wood-like state, the death-like state, or the green state — so they are proclaimed; these are various attainments that destroy all sins. ॥22॥
5.20.23: Woman, bed and drink, garments, incense and unguents, the chewing of betel — these are the five splendours of royal power; ॥23॥
5.20.24: loads of gold, and copper, houses, gems and cows, learning in the Vedas and śāstras, song, dance and ornaments, ॥24॥
5.20.25: conches, vīṇās and drums, a lordly elephant, a parasol and chowries — these are the forms of enjoyment; attached to them, one becomes infatuated. ॥25॥
5.20.26: Like a mirror dimmed, O sage, he is crushed by attachments (sneha, also oil) like sesame; and, deluded in understanding, he even dismisses it, saying, go away quickly. ॥26॥
5.20.27: Though knowing, he wanders here in saṃsāra like a water-wheel, afflicted with sorrow in all kinds of births, among both the immobile and the moving. ॥27॥
5.20.28: Thus, having passed through all births in his wandering, by the course of time he attains the human state, which is extremely rare. ॥28॥
5.20.29: Even out of sequence human birth may be obtained through the weight of merit; the courses of actions are declared to be manifold, according to their heaviness and lightness. ॥29॥
5.20.30: Having obtained the human state, the means to heaven and liberation, he who does not pursue his own good grieves for a long time after death. ॥30॥
5.20.31: For all gods and asuras the human state is very hard to obtain; having obtained it, one should act in such a way that one does not go to hell. ॥31॥
5.20.32: If, having obtained the rare human state, there is no effort toward gaining heaven and final release, that birth is declared futile. ॥32॥
5.20.33: The human state is declared the root of everything, of the four aims of life; having obtained it through dharma, O Vyāsa, one should carefully preserve it. ॥33॥
5.20.34: Having obtained the human state, rooted in dharma and accomplishing all aims, if there is to be effort for gain, then one should oneself guard the root. ॥34॥
5.20.35: Who, having obtained even among humans the status of a Brahmin, which is truly rare, does not pursue his own good — who else is more senseless than he? ॥35॥
5.20.36: Of all the continents, this alone is called the land of action; from here heaven and liberation, once earned, are attained. ॥36॥
5.20.37: Having obtained the impermanent human state in this land, Bhārata-varṣa, whoever does not work for his own good has truly cheated himself. ॥37॥
5.20.38: This is the land of action, O Brahmin; that heaven is known as the land of fruits. Whatever action is done here is enjoyed in heaven. ॥38॥
5.20.39: As long as the body is healthy, one should practise dharma; when unwell, even if urged by others, one is unable to do anything. ॥39॥
5.20.40: He who does not accomplish the permanent by means of the impermanent body — for him the permanent is lost, and the impermanent perishes as well. ॥40॥
5.20.41: Pieces upon pieces of one's lifespan fall away before his very eyes; why does he not awaken, though taught by the passing of day and night? ॥41॥
5.20.42: Since it is not known when death will come, and to whom, who can find steadiness in the face of sudden death? ॥42॥
5.20.43: Since he will surely depart alone, abandoning everything, why does he not at some time give this wealth in charity as provisions for the journey? ॥43॥
5.20.44: One who has taken charity as provisions for the journey goes happily to the abode of Yama; otherwise the creature suffers on a road devoid of provisions. ॥44॥
5.20.45: Those whose merits are complete in every respect at the destined time—for them, as they go to the region of heaven, there is gain at every step. ॥45॥
5.20.46: Knowing this, a man should perform merit and avoid sin. Through merit one attains divinity; the one without merit goes to hell. ॥46॥
5.20.47: Those who have taken refuge, even slightly, in Śiva, the lord of the gods, do not see the terrible Yama, nor hell either. ॥47॥
5.20.48: But, because of sins and great delusions, such men dwell there for a short time by Śiva's command, and then go to Śiva's abode. ॥48॥
5.20.49: Those, however, who have taken refuge in Maheśvara with their whole being are not stained by sin, as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water. ॥49॥
5.20.50: Those by whom the name Śiva has been uttered, and likewise Hara, Hara—they have no fear of hell, nor indeed of Yama, O best of sages. ॥50॥
5.20.51: The two syllables Śi-va are the provisions for the other world, the untroubled means to liberation, the sole abode of all accumulated merit. ॥51॥
5.20.52: The name of Śiva alone is the sole remedy for the great disease of worldly existence; I see no other cure for the disease of saṃsāra. ॥52॥
5.20.53: Long ago a Pulkasa, having committed thousands of brahmin-slayings, attained liberation by hearing the pure name Śiva. ॥53॥
5.20.54: Therefore the wise man should constantly increase his devotion to the Lord. Through devotion to Śiva, O greatly wise one, one obtains both enjoyment and liberation. ॥54॥
5.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The particular account of Manu, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
5.21.1: Vyāsa said: Brāhmaṇa-hood is indeed hard to attain; by nature one becomes a brāhmaṇa. From the mouth of the Lord arose the kṣatriya class, from the arms and from the thighs the vaiśyas, ॥1॥
5.21.2: and the śūdra was born from the feet — such is the revealed word from his mouth. How then do they attain a higher position from a lower station? Tell me this. ॥2॥
5.21.3: Sanatkumāra said: Through evil deeds, O Kāleya, humans fall from their station; therefore, having attained the best station, a wise man should guard it. ॥3॥
5.21.4: He who, abandoning brāhmaṇa-hood, is born in a kṣatriya womb, fallen from brāhmaṇa-status, takes up kṣatriya-hood. ॥4॥
5.21.5: Likewise the deluded one, through practising adharma, keeps revolving downward, for he enters darkness for thousands of births. ॥5॥
5.21.6: Therefore, having obtained the highest station, one should not be careless nor ruin it; a man should always guard his own station, even when he meets with misfortunes. ॥6॥
5.21.7: He who, having attained auspicious brāhmaṇa-hood, despises brāhmaṇa-status and does not know what may and may not be eaten — that man becomes a kṣatriya. ॥7॥
5.21.8: By what action an intelligent śūdra is born a vaiśya, and by which one becomes of the highest class — all that I shall tell you. ॥8॥
5.21.9: Being a śūdra, one should practise the śūdra's duties as prescribed, and properly render service to the three higher classes always. ॥9॥
5.21.10: Even a śūdra who does so, desiring advancement, attains vaiśya-hood. The vaiśya who employs his wealth rightly and offers oblations according to rule, ॥10॥
5.21.11: taking up the agnihotra and eating only the food left over after offerings — that vaiśya is born in a kṣatriya family; there is no doubt about this. ॥11॥
5.21.12: The kṣatriya is born anew through properly consecrated sacrifices with fees given; seeking heaven, he studies the Veda and always takes refuge in the three sacred fires. ॥12॥
5.21.13: With hands and feet ever moist from charity and ablutions, he should protect the earth by dharma; and, devoted to dharma, approach his own wife in her season, ॥13॥
5.21.14: saying, let hospitality be given to all, to the three classes and to all beings; and for the sake of cows, brāhmaṇas and himself he should be slain in battle. ॥14॥
5.21.15: Thereby, his self purified by fire and mantras, the kṣatriya becomes a brāhmaṇa; becoming a brāhmaṇa according to rule, he is born as a sacrificial priest. ॥15॥
5.21.16: Ever devoted to his own duties, truthful, with senses conquered, he attains a vast heaven and becomes dear even to the gods. ॥16॥
5.21.17: Brāhmaṇa-hood is indeed hard to obtain; men achieve it with difficulty. Through brāhmaṇa-status one obtains everything, and liberation as well, O lord of sages. ॥17॥
5.21.18: Therefore with every effort a brāhmaṇa devoted to dharma should guard the supreme brāhmaṇa-status, the means of attaining all aims. ॥18॥
5.21.19: Vyāsa said: You have mentioned here the greatness of battle, O best of sages; I wish to hear this. Tell it, O best of speakers. ॥19॥
5.21.20: Sanatkumāra said: Having worshipped with sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma with abundant fees, one does not obtain the fruit that one would obtain in battle. ॥20॥
5.21.21: So the knowers of truth and the knowers of sacrificial rites have always declared. Therefore I shall tell you the fruit that belongs to those who live by weapons. ॥21॥
5.21.22: Gain of merit, gain of wealth, and likewise gain of fame come to the hero who longs for battle, crushing the enemy's army. ॥22॥
5.21.23: His are dharma, wealth and desire, and the merit of sacrifice with fees. He who, facing the enemy, gives his life mounts that celestial vehicle; ॥23॥
5.21.24: he is born in the world of Viṣṇu. And he who is unvanquished in battle, if he does not die, obtains the merit of four horse-sacrifices. ॥24॥
5.21.25: But the hero who, not abandoning his weapon, dies at the front of the army, standing face to face with the foe, does not return from heaven. ॥25॥
5.21.26: Whether king, prince, or army commander, the hero who is slain by a kṣatriya in combat attains an imperishable world. ॥26॥
5.21.27: As many of his hairs as are pierced by missiles in the great battle, so many imperishable worlds, yielding every desire, does he obtain. ॥27॥
5.21.28: The hero's seat, the hero's bed, and a firm abiding in the hero's station are always his, O Vyāsa, in this world and the next. ॥28॥
5.21.29: Those who die for the sake of cows, of brāhmaṇas, and of their land and master go to happiness just as the virtuous do. ॥29॥
5.21.30: Whoever, having killed a brāhmaṇa, afterwards gives up his life there in battle for his master — he does not return from heaven. ॥30॥
5.21.31: For one killed by flesh-eating beasts or by elephants for the sake of brāhmaṇas, cows or master, the destiny is supreme, abundant and imperishable. ॥31॥
5.21.32: A capable man here may manage to sacrifice even with hundreds of rites, but giving up one's own body in battle is extremely hard to do. ॥32॥
5.21.33: Battle is most meritorious, leads to heaven, reveals one's true nature, and is universal in scope — for all classes, and for the kṣatriya in particular. ॥33॥
5.21.34: I shall now fully declare the eternal law of war: whom one should strike and whom one should spare. ॥34॥
5.21.35: An assailant who approaches intent on killing, even a twice-born versed in the Vedāntas — one may kill him; one does not thereby become a slayer of a brāhmaṇa. ॥35॥
