5.21.36: Even one who deserves to be killed must not be killed if he begs for water. O Vyāsa, the man who kills the distressed in battle becomes a brāhmaṇa-slayer. ॥36॥
5.21.37: Having killed the sick, the weak, a child, a woman, an orphan, the pitiable, or one whose bow is broken or whose bowstring is cut, one certainly becomes a brāhmaṇa-slayer. ॥37॥
5.21.38: Reflecting thus, the truly wise man should gladly be devoted to battle; having obtained the fruit of his birth, he rejoices here and hereafter. ॥38॥
5.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The description of the fruit of battle, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
5.22.1: Vyāsa said: O dear one, O lord of sages, now tell me in due order the process of the birth of the living being, and also its stay in the womb, for the sake of cultivating dispassion. ॥1॥
5.22.2: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa: I shall tell you briefly yet completely the essence of the scriptures—the true dispassion of one seeking liberation, which severs the bondage of worldly existence. ॥2॥
5.22.3: Inside the cooking vessel of the stomach, food lies separately and water separately. The water is placed above the fire, and the food above the water. ॥3॥
5.22.4: Below the water is that fire; the vital air situated there slowly fans the fire. The fire, being fanned by the air, makes the water very hot. ॥4॥
5.22.5: That food is then cooked all over by the hot water. When cooked, it becomes twofold: the waste separately and the essence separately. ॥5॥
5.22.6: The waste, divided into twelve impurities, goes out of the body; but the essence flows within the body, and by it the body becomes nourished. ॥6॥
5.22.7: Ears, eyes, nose, tongue, teeth, penis, anus, nails—the seats of impurity—and phlegm, sweat, feces and urine: these are known as the twelve. ॥7॥
5.22.8: All the channels, bound to the heart-lotus on every side, should be known as carriers of the essence. I shall tell their manner, O sage. ॥8॥
5.22.9: At their openings the vital breath places that subtle essence; with that essence the vital breath fills those channels again. ॥9॥
5.22.10: Then, filled, they spread throughout the body. Thereupon that essence, lying within the channels, by the body's own heat… ॥10॥
5.22.11: …is cooked, and from its being cooked there arises again a twofold product. First the skin is enveloped by it, and blood is produced. ॥11॥
5.22.12: From blood come body-hair and flesh; from flesh, head-hair and sinew; likewise from sinew, the bones; nails and marrow arise from bone. ॥12॥
5.22.13: From marrow as cause, by transformation, comes semen, whose nature is procreation. Thus the twelvefold transformation of food is proclaimed. ॥13॥
5.22.14: Semen is born of food, and from semen comes the origin of the divine body. When, at the proper season, faultless semen is lodged in the womb, ॥14॥
5.22.15: then, touched by air, it becomes one with the woman's blood. At the time of the discharge of semen, the living being, joined with its causal subtle factors, ॥15॥
5.22.16: enveloped, enters the womb, impelled by its own deeds. That semen and blood, united in one place, becomes the embryonic fluid (kalala) in one day. ॥16॥
5.22.17: In five nights the kalala takes the form of a bubble; in seven nights the bubble becomes a lump of flesh. ॥17॥
5.22.18: The neck, head, shoulders, spine, belly, hands and feet, the sides, the waist, and the body likewise— ॥18॥
5.22.19: arise here gradually within just two months. In three months all the sprouting joints are formed. ॥19॥
5.22.20: In four months the fingers arise in due order; and in five months the mouth, nose and ears. ॥20॥
5.22.21: The row of teeth, the private part and the nails arise; and within six months the openings of the ears form. ॥21॥
5.22.22: The anus, urinary passage, genitals and navel come into being; and the joints in the limbs arise in seven months. ॥22॥
5.22.23: Complete with limbs and minor parts, fully matured, it remains in the mother's belly, covered by the caul, O best of sages. ॥23॥
5.22.24: By the six-flavoured essence stolen from the mother's food, conveyed through the attached umbilical cord, it grows day by day. ॥24॥
5.22.25: Then, when this little body is complete, the living being regains memory; it knows pleasure and pain, sleep and dream, and what was done before. ॥25॥
5.22.26: I died and was born again; born, I died again. Thousands of various wombs have been seen by me in being born. ॥26॥
5.22.27: Now, as soon as I am born and have gained right impressions, I shall pursue that good by which there will be no further birth in a womb. ॥27॥
5.22.28: Thinking thus while in the womb: When I have come out of the womb, I shall seek the knowledge of Śiva, which ends worldly existence. ॥28॥
5.22.29: Thus the living being, greatly tormented by the suffering of the womb, remains there under the sway of karma, pondering the means to liberation. ॥29॥
5.22.30: Just as someone crushed under a great mountain remains in pain, so the embodied one, wrapped in the caul, remains in pain. ॥30॥
5.22.31: As one who has fallen into the ocean remains in pain, utterly distraught, so then it is, its limbs soaked in the womb-fluid, constantly agitated. ॥31॥
5.22.32: Just as someone placed in an iron pot is cooked by fire, so, cast into the pot of the womb, it is cooked by the digestive fire. ॥32॥
5.22.33: Whatever pain arises for one ceaselessly pierced by red-hot needles, greater than that is the pain of one dwelling there. ॥33॥
5.22.34: For embodied beings there is nowhere any pain or hardship greater than dwelling in the womb—full of suffering, most dreadful, extremely oppressive. ॥34॥
5.22.35: This exceedingly great suffering is declared to befall sinners; for those of righteous mind, birth always takes place in seven months. ॥35॥
5.22.36: Pain even harder to bear than that of the womb arises from the squeezing in the vaginal passage—for sinful souls, O Vyāsa, not for those endowed with dharma. ॥36॥
5.22.37: Such is the pain of one squeezed all over like sugarcane in a press, and struck on the head with the mallet of sin. ॥37॥
5.22.38: Just as sesame seeds pressed in a mill become pithless in a moment, so the body becomes pithless from the squeezing of the vaginal passage. ॥38॥
5.22.39: This body has bones for its legs, beams and pillars, is held together by the binding of sinews, is plastered with the clay of blood and flesh, and is a vessel for the stuff of feces and urine; ॥39॥
5.22.40: covered with head-hair, body-hair and nails; an abode of disease, afflicted; with the mouth as its one great door, and adorned with eight windows. ॥40॥
5.22.41: The body has the two lips as its door-panels and is likewise furnished with the tongue as its bolt. It is tormented by thirst for enjoyments, deluded, and it follows the sway of attachment and aversion. ॥41॥
5.22.42: With its limbs and lesser limbs folded together, enveloped in the membrane of the womb, it comes out through the narrow, confined passage of the womb. ॥42॥
5.22.43: Its limbs are smeared with feces, urine and blood; it emerges from its sheath; it is known as a cage of bones — such is the body to be understood in this world. ॥43॥
5.22.44: It has three hundred and sixty bones and five hundred muscles, and is covered all around by three and a half crores of hairs. ॥44॥
5.22.45: The body is pervaded all around by as many crores of channels (nāḍīs), gross and subtle; they are declared to be both visible and invisible. ॥45॥
5.22.46: Through these channels what lies within flows outward as sweat and fluids. Thirty-two teeth are declared, and twenty nails are recorded. ॥46॥
5.22.47: Of bile there is to be known a kuḍava; of phlegm an āḍhaka is stated; of fat (vasā) twenty palas, and half that of kapila. ॥47॥
5.22.48: Two and a half tulās are to be known; ten palas of fatty tissue (medas); three palas of the vital blood, and four times that of marrow. ॥48॥
5.22.49: Semen is to be known as half a kuḍava; that seed is the strength of embodied beings. Of flesh, in a single mass, a thousand palas is stated. ॥49॥
5.22.50: Blood is to be known as a hundred palas; feces and urine, in measure, are four and four añjalis respectively, O best of sages. ॥50॥
5.22.51: Thus this body is the non-eternal house of the eternal Self, impure house of the pure Self, fashioned out of the bondage of karma. ॥51॥
5.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The description of the origin of the body, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
5.23.1: Sanatkumāra said: Listen, O Vyāsa of great intellect, O sage: I shall briefly tell you of the impurity of the body and of the power of its nature. ॥1॥
5.23.2: Since the body arises from the union of semen and blood, and is always filled with faeces and urine, it is therefore considered impure. ॥2॥
5.23.3: Just as a pot filled inside with excrement is not clean though washed outside, so this body, even while being cleansed, remains impure for that reason. ॥3॥
5.23.4: Even the most purifying things—the five products of the cow and sacrificial oblations—become impure in an instant on reaching it; what else then is impure, if not this? ॥4॥
5.23.5: Even delightful and fragrant foods and drinks quickly become impure on reaching it; what else then is impure? ॥5॥
5.23.6: O people, why do you not see the putrid filth that comes out of one's own body day after day? How can its container be pure? ॥6॥
5.23.7: Even when cleansed with the five cow-products, kuśa grass and water, the body does not become spotless, like a piece of charcoal being rubbed. ॥7॥
5.23.8: How can that body be purified whose streams constantly flow, like those of a mountain, with phlegm, urine, faeces and the like? ॥8॥
5.23.9: In the body, the receptacle of all impurities, there is not even a single pure spot, as in a leather bag of faeces and urine. ॥9॥
5.23.10: Having touched the outlets of one's own body, the hand is cleansed with earth and water; yet why does the hand of this vessel of impurity not fall off? ॥10॥
5.23.11: The body, though carefully refined with fragrant incense and the like, does not abandon its nature, like a dog's tail that has been bent straight. ॥11॥
5.23.12: Just as a thing black by its very nature cannot become white by any means, so the body, though thoroughly cleansed, would not become spotless. ॥12॥
5.23.13: Though smelling its own foul odour, though seeing its own filth, though pinching its nose, this world does not become dispassionate. ॥13॥
5.23.14: Ah, the might of delusion, by which this world is veiled! Though plainly seeing the body's own defect, one does not become detached. ॥14॥
5.23.15: For the man who does not become detached by the foul smell of his own body, what other cause of detachment can be taught? ॥15॥
5.23.16: In the whole world, the body alone is impure; by contact with its filthy parts even something pure becomes impure. ॥16॥
5.23.17: Cleansing of the body is declared to be for removing smell and smear; by the removal of both there is purity, and it is purified by contact with what is pure. ॥17॥
5.23.18: One may perform cleansing till death with all the water of the Gaṅgā and with loads of earth like mountains, yet one corrupt in disposition is not purified. ॥18॥
5.23.19: An evil-souled person is never purified by baths at holy places or by austerities. Does a dog's skin bag, washed at a holy place, attain purity? ॥19॥
5.23.20: For one corrupt in inner disposition, even entering the fire yields neither heaven nor liberation—only the burning of the body. ॥20॥
5.23.21: Even with all the water of the Gaṅgā and a mountain of earth, a man corrupt in disposition, devoted to bathing from birth, is not purified—thus indeed we declare. ॥21॥
5.23.22: Even if he kindles a great fire sprinkled with ghee and oil, its flames turning to the right, and enters it and is burnt, one corrupt in disposition gains neither merit nor any other fruit. ॥22॥
5.23.23: Fish dwell always in the Gaṅgā and other holy waters, and flocks of birds in temples; devoid of pious disposition, they gain no fruit from immersion in holy waters, nor likewise from gifts. ॥23॥
5.23.24: Purity of disposition is the supreme purity and the standard in all acts: a wife is embraced with one feeling, a daughter with another. ॥24॥
5.23.25: The mind's attitude differs even toward things that are not different: a woman thinks of her son in one way and of her husband in another. ॥25॥
5.23.26: Behold fully the great power of this disposition: even when embraced by a woman, one without amorous feeling does not desire. ॥26॥
5.23.27: One would not eat the various foods and fragrant delicacies if one's mind is fixed in thought on the three—desire and the rest. ॥27॥
5.23.28: By disposition a man is bound; by disposition he is released. Through disposition, pure and pure-souled, he attains heaven and liberation. ॥28॥
5.23.29: One whose self is purified by single-minded disposition—whether burning offerings, making oblations, or praising—when he dies, quickly attains, through the gaining of knowledge, the worlds of those who have performed very many sacrifices. ॥29॥
5.23.30: For men, cleansing of the smear and stench of the faeces and urine of ignorance and passion is done with the spotless water of knowledge and, further, with the earth of true dispassion. ॥30॥
5.23.31: Thus this body is regarded as impure by nature; its substance is mere skin, it is pithless, like the hollow core of a plantain. ॥31॥
5.23.32: The wise one who, knowing the body thus to be full of defects, becomes loosened from the feeling arising from bodily enjoyment, calm in mind and serene in intellect— ॥32॥
5.23.33: —he crosses beyond saṃsāra and becomes liberated while living; but one who firmly clings to saṃsāra, hollow as the core of a plantain, remains bound. ॥33॥
5.23.34: Thus has been described this greatly painful suffering of birth, which befalls men through the fault of ignorance and under the sway of various actions. ॥34॥
5.23.35: In half a verse I shall state what has been said in crores of texts: mine is supreme sorrow, not mine is supreme happiness. ॥35॥
5.23.36: Many kings have gone from here to the other world; those endowed with freedom from possessiveness were freed, while others were bound by hundreds of thousands. ॥36॥
5.23.37: The memory that he had while in the womb is lost to him, through the stupefying pain of being pressed in the mechanism of the birth canal. ॥37॥
5.23.38: And merely by the touch of the dreadful outer air, bringing delusion, a fever arises in this embodied being. ॥38॥
5.23.39: From that great fever stupor arises, and in the stupefied one loss of memory quickly occurs again. ॥39॥
5.23.40: Then, through loss of memory, he has no memory of his former deeds, and attachment swiftly arises in the creature for that very birth. ॥40॥
5.23.41: This world, attached and deluded, does not engage in what ought to be done; it knows neither the self, nor the Supreme, nor the deity. ॥41॥
5.23.42: O good sage, though he has ears, he does not hear the highest good; though he has eyes capable of it, he does not see the highest good. ॥42॥
5.23.43: Walking slowly on a level path, he stumbles, as it were, at every step; though possessing intellect, he does not understand, even when being instructed by the wise. ॥43॥
5.23.44: Therefore a man suffers in saṃsāra, following the sway of craving that leads back to the womb, his understanding lost through sin, though the misery of the womb was once remembered. ॥44॥
5.23.45: Thus this great, supreme, divine scripture was spoken by Śiva for the purpose of expounding austerity, the means of attaining heaven and liberation. ॥45॥
5.23.46: That those who, while this auspicious knowledge exists — the means to all desires and goals — do not work for their own good: that indeed is a great wonder. ॥46॥
5.23.47: Again, in childhood there is great suffering, because the functions of the senses are undeveloped; even wishing, the child cannot speak or do anything to remedy it. ॥47॥
5.23.48: At teething there is great pain, and likewise from minor illness; and there is affliction from various childhood diseases and also from the child-seizing spirits. ॥48॥
5.23.49: Sometimes his body is overcome by hunger and thirst, sometimes he stays crying loudly; and out of delusion the child may do things like eating faeces and urine. ॥49॥
5.23.50: In boyhood, with the piercing of the ears, the disciplinary measures of mother and father, and the learning of letters and the like, various sufferings arise. ॥50॥
5.23.51: Even having just passed through the suffering of childhood and seeing it, the deluded-minded one does not do what is good for himself — that is the great wonder here. ॥51॥
5.23.52: Because the functions of the senses are fully active, from the torment of the disease of lust, and constantly when that object is not obtained — whence can there be happiness in youth? ॥52॥
5.23.53: And there is great suffering from jealousy for him who is infatuated through delusion, as for an inflamed eye; and renunciation of the beloved leads only to sorrow. ॥53॥
5.23.54: Tormented by the fire of lust, he finds no sleep at night; and even by day, whence happiness, with anxiety about earning wealth? ॥54॥
5.23.55: The drops of semen of a man whose mind is fixed on women are not considered a source of happiness; they are just like drops of sweat. ॥55॥
5.23.56: Whatever relief there is for a leper or a monkey tormented by worms from the burning of scratching — that, the knowers say, is the pleasure in women. ॥56॥
5.23.57: Such pleasure as one feels from pus discharging from a boil, such should be considered the pleasure in women; nothing more is found in them. ॥57॥
5.23.58: Such pleasure as arises from the evacuation of faeces and urine, such should be known the pleasure in women; the deluded imagine it otherwise. ॥58॥
5.23.59: In women, who are without substance and the abode of all faults, there is not even an atom of happiness — so it was declared by Pañcacūḍā. ॥59॥
5.23.60: Through honour and dishonour, through separation after union with the beloved, and youth seized by old age — where is happiness free of trouble? ॥60॥
5.23.61: In old age the body is slackened by wrinkles, grey hair and baldness, incapable in all activities, worn out by old age. ॥61॥
5.23.62: The youth of woman and man, charming and formerly dear to each other — that very youth, seized by old age, is no longer dear even to the two of them. ॥62॥
5.23.63: He who, even seeing his own self transformed by old age as if into something never seen before, still remains attached — who else is more senseless than he? ॥63॥
5.23.64: A man overcome by old age, because of his incapacity, is treated with contempt by kinsmen such as daughters and sons, and by servants who are hard to control. ॥64॥
5.23.65: One greatly afflicted by old age is unable to accomplish dharma, wealth, desire, or liberation; therefore one should practise dharma while young. ॥65॥
5.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The description of the impurity of the body and of the sorrows of childhood and the other stages, in the treatment of saṃsāra, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
5.24.1: Vyāsa said: That censure concerning women which was declared by Pañcacūḍā, tell it to me briefly, O sage, if you are pleased with me. ॥1॥
5.24.2: Sanatkumāra said: I shall describe the nature of women exactly as it is; listen, O brahmin. By merely hearing it, supreme dispassion would arise. ॥2॥
5.24.3: Women indeed are the root of faults, ever light-minded, O sage. Therefore attachment to them should not be formed by vigilant seekers of liberation. ॥3॥
5.24.4: Here too they cite this ancient story: the dialogue of Nārada with the courtesan Pañcacūḍā. ॥4॥
5.24.5: Long ago the wise divine sage Nārada, roaming the worlds, saw the young, peerless apsaras Pañcacūḍā. ॥5॥
5.24.6: Nārada, best of sages, asked the fair-browed apsaras: There is a certain doubt in my heart; resolve it for me, O slender-waisted one. ॥6॥
5.24.7: Thus addressed, that excellent apsaras replied to the brahmin: If it is within my scope, I shall speak—if you consider me capable. ॥7॥
5.24.8: Nārada said: I shall by no means engage you in what is beyond your scope, gentle lady. I wish to hear from you about the nature of women, O slender-waisted one. ॥8॥
5.24.9: Sanatkumāra said: Hearing these words of the divine sage, the best of apsarases replied to that lord of sages, the divine sage, best of munis. ॥9॥
5.24.10: Pañcacūḍā said: Listen, O sage: a woman cannot be censured by one who is herself a woman. You know what women are and what they are like by nature. ॥10॥
5.24.11: You ought not to set me such a question, O divine sage. Having said this, Pañcacūḍā, best of apsarases, fell silent. ॥11॥
5.24.12: Then the foremost divine sage, having heard her excellent words, spoke to her again, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. ॥12॥
5.24.13: Nārada said: There would be fault in speaking falsely; in truth no fault exists. Know this, and therefore speak that truth, O slender-waisted one. ॥13॥
5.24.14: Sanatkumāra said: Thus addressed, the sweetly smiling one, having made up her mind, eagerly began to speak of the perennial, true faults of women. ॥14॥
5.24.15: Pañcacūḍā said: Even women of good family, who have protectors and are beautiful, do not stay within bounds; that is the fault in women, O Nārada. ॥15॥
5.24.16: There is indeed nothing else more sinful than women. Women are truly the root of sins—so you too know. ॥16॥
5.24.17: Even having renowned, wealthy, handsome husbands as they desire, women, on finding an opportunity, cannot wait faithfully for them. ॥17॥
5.24.18: This wicked way belongs to us women, O lord: that, abandoning shame, we resort even to very sinful men. ॥18॥
5.24.19: Whoever courts a woman, comes near her, and renders her a little service—him alone do women desire. ॥19॥
5.24.20: It is because men do not solicit them, and from fear of the husband's people, that women, who know no bounds, keep within bounds with their husbands. ॥20॥
5.24.21: There is no one they reject; they have no fixed rule about age. Handsome or ugly, they enjoy a man. ॥21॥
5.24.22: Not from fear, nor from reproach, nor in any way for the sake of wealth, nor from ties of kin and family, do women remain with their husbands. ॥22॥
5.24.23: Women of good family envy women who are in their youth, wear the ornaments and garments they like, and live as they please. ॥23॥
5.24.24: Even those beloved women who are always highly honoured and guarded become attached to the hunchbacked, the blind, the dull-witted, and the dwarfish, ॥24॥
5.24.25: and even to the lame, O divine sage, and to other despicable men. In the worlds there is no one whom women will not approach, O great sage. ॥25॥
5.24.26: If somehow access to men is not available, O brahmin, they turn even to one another, and do not remain faithful to their husbands. ॥26॥
5.24.27: Only through not obtaining men, fear of attendants, and fear of death and bondage are those women thwarted in their hopes. ॥27॥
5.24.28: Fickle by nature, of wicked conduct, and hard to fathom in their intentions even for a wise man here, as they are driven by the pursuit of sexual pleasure. ॥28॥
5.24.29: Fire is never satisfied with fuel, nor the great ocean with rivers, nor Death with all beings, nor fair-eyed women with men. ॥29॥
5.24.30: And this is another secret of all women, O divine sage: on merely seeing a man, a woman's private part at once becomes moist. ॥30॥
5.24.31: On seeing a man well bathed, fragrant and free of dirt, women's private parts become moist, like water from a leather-bag vessel. ॥31॥
5.24.32: Women do not tolerate even an excellent husband who provides even for their bodily needs, who shows them honour and conciliation, and who protects them. ॥32॥
5.24.33: Neither from the highest enjoyment of pleasures nor from an accumulation of ornaments and wealth do they consider good to come, so much as from sexual union. ॥33॥
5.24.34: The Ender, Yama, Death, the netherworld, the submarine mare-fire, a razor's edge, poison, a serpent and fire—all these on one side, and women on the other. ॥34॥
5.24.35: Ever since the five great elements arose, since the world was ordained by the Creator, since men and women were fashioned—ever has fault resided in women, O Nārada. ॥35॥
5.24.36: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard her words, Nārada, pleased at heart, deemed them true, and thereupon became indifferent to women. ॥36॥
5.24.37: Thus I have respectfully told you the nature of women as declared by Pañcacūḍā, a cause of dispassion, O Vyāsa. What else do you wish to hear? ॥37॥
5.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The description of the nature of women, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥24॥
5.25.1: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing sage, I have listened with delight to the account of the nature of women from you. Now tell me the knowledge of time (of death). ॥1॥
5.25.2: Sanatkumāra said: This very question Pārvatī once asked the Supreme Lord, after hearing many divine stories, pleased, and having bowed deeply to him. ॥2॥
5.25.3: Pārvatī said: O Lord, by your grace I have understood the whole doctrine: how you are to be worshipped, O god, and with which mantras, according to rule. ॥3॥
5.25.4: Yet even now one doubt remains, O Lord, concerning the wheel of time: what the signs of death are, O god, and what the measure of one's lifespan is. ॥4॥
5.25.5: Tell me everything, O Lord, if I am dear to you. Thus questioned by the goddess, Maheśvara replied. ॥5॥
5.25.6: Īśvara said: Truly I shall tell you, beloved, the most excellent teaching, by which, O queen of the gods, men come to know the time of death. ॥6॥
5.25.7: It is known to within a day, a fortnight, a month, a season, a half-year or a year, through signs gross and subtle, external and internal. ॥7॥
5.25.8: That I shall now explain to you; listen truly, O beautiful one, O Umā, for the benefit of the worlds and for the sake of detachment. ॥8॥
5.25.9: If the body suddenly turns pale all over, with redness in its upper part, then one should know death will come within six months, beloved. ॥9॥
5.25.10: When the mouth, ears, eyes and tongue become stiff, then one should know death will come within six months, beloved. ॥10॥
5.25.11: If, O gentle one, one does not readily hear the roaring sound within, those who know time should recognise death within six months. ॥11॥
5.25.12: When one does not see the brightness coming from sun, moon and fire, and everything appears wholly black, then life lasts six months. ॥12॥
5.25.13: When, O goddess, beloved, the left hand throbs for a week, then his life lasts one month; there is no doubt. ॥13॥
5.25.14: When the limbs loosen and the palate dries up, then his life lasts one month; there is no doubt. ॥14॥
5.25.15: He whose nose runs while all three humours are disturbed lives a fortnight; one whose mouth and throat dry up has his life end at the close of six months. ॥15॥
5.25.16: He whose tongue becomes swollen and whose teeth grow moist, O lovely lady, meets death after six months; one should recognise it by these signs. ॥16॥
5.25.17: When, O fair-complexioned one, one does not see oneself reflected in water, oil, ghee or a mirror, or sees it distorted, as mere flesh, ॥17॥
5.25.18: he should be known by one who understands the wheel of time as having six months of life. Hear another sign, O queen of the gods, by which death is recognised. ॥18॥
5.25.19: When one sees one's own shadow headless, or finds oneself without a shadow, one does not live a month. ॥19॥
5.25.20: I have told the bodily signs of death, O Pārvatī. Now hear, gentle one, the external signs I now describe. ॥20॥
5.25.21: When, O goddess, the disc of the moon or sun appears rayless and of a pale-red hue, one perishes within half a month. ॥21॥
5.25.22: He who cannot see Arundhatī, the great path of the sky, the moon with its mark — seeing it without its mark — and the stars, lives one month. ॥22॥
5.25.23: If on seeing a planet there is confusion of directions, death surely comes in six months; likewise if one cannot see Utathya, the pole star, or the sun's disc. ॥23॥
5.25.24: When one sees a rainbow at night and a falling meteor at midday, and is surrounded by vultures and crows, one has six months of life; no doubt. ॥24॥
5.25.25: If the Seers (the Great Bear) and the path to heaven are not seen in the sky, men who know time should recognise six months of life. ॥25॥
5.25.26: If one suddenly sees the sun or the moon seized by Rāhu, or sees the circle of directions as if whirling, one clearly dies within six months. ॥26॥
5.25.27: If a man is suddenly swarmed by blue flies, his life should truly be known as one month. ॥27॥
5.25.28: If a vulture, crow or pigeon alights and stays on one's head, that creature dies quickly, within one month; no doubt. ॥28॥
5.25.29: Thus the varieties of external ill omens have been described. For the welfare of men I now speak briefly. ॥29॥
5.25.30: I tell how, O goddess, people know the time of death from both hands; between the left and right it is said to be directly perceptible. ॥30॥
5.25.31: Thus, in brief, the two fortnights are placed on the two hands, O beautiful goddess. Becoming pure, well bathed, with senses restrained, remembering the Lord, ॥31॥
5.25.32: having washed the hands with milk, one should rub them with red lac; having adorned the hands with perfumes and flowers, one should examine what is auspicious and inauspicious. ॥32॥
5.25.33: Starting from the little finger up to the thumb, beloved, in order of the three joints, on both hands, ॥33॥
5.25.34: having placed the lunar days beginning with the first (pratipad) on the joints, with hands held in a cupped form, seated facing east, ॥34॥
5.25.35: one should recite mentally the nine-syllabled mantra a hundred and eight times, and then carefully examine the hands at each joint. ॥35॥
5.25.36: On whichever joint a line appears black like a bee, on that lunar day death should be known to come, in the dark or bright fortnight accordingly, beloved. ॥36॥
5.25.37: Now I shall briefly describe the sign of time arising from the inner sound (nāda). Having known the going and coming of breath, one should act; listen, beloved. ॥37॥
5.25.38: Having carefully understood self-knowledge and the movement of the breath, O fair-hipped one — time runs as kṣaṇa, truṭi, lava, nimeṣa, kāṣṭhā and kalā, ॥38॥
5.25.39: muhūrta, day and night, fortnight, month, season, year, the cycle of years, yuga, kalpa and mahākalpa likewise — ॥39॥
5.25.40: thus Time, who is Sadāśiva, carries all away in due succession. Left, right and middle — these are remembered as the three paths of the breath. ॥40॥
5.25.41: Beginning from five days and going up to a limit of twenty-five days, when the breath moves in the left course, the sound (nāda) is the measure; this has been told to you. ॥41॥
5.25.42: The elements, the openings, the directions and the banner, O fair-complexioned one: in the left course the sound is the measure for one who knows time. ॥42॥
5.25.43: And the qualities that are modifications of the seasons, there itself, O spirited lady, are declared as the measure for the right course; this should be known by those who understand the breath. ॥43॥
5.25.44: When Iḍā and the other channels carry the breaths for a number of days equal to the elements (five), his life lasts within a year; there is no doubt. ॥44॥
5.25.45: With a flow of ten days he lives the measure of a year; with a flow of fifteen days, his life is ended in one year. ॥45॥
5.25.46: With a flow of twenty days one should then mark six months. When the left channel flows for a measure of twenty-five days, ॥46॥
5.25.47: then the life of that man whose life is ending is three months. With a measure of twenty-six days, two months are declared. ॥47॥
5.25.48: If it flows without any rest for a measure of twenty-seven days, one month of life is declared in the left range. ॥48॥
5.25.49: This measure should be understood according to the measure of the left breath. For the one other than the left (the right), the days are arranged in four groups in due order. ॥49॥
5.25.50: Placed in four positions, O Goddess, these sixteen are proclaimed. Now I shall tell their measure accurately. ॥50॥
5.25.51: Taking six days as the beginning of the count, according to rule, what falls within this in the left opening is set forth. ॥51॥
5.25.52: When it has prevailed for six days, he lives two years; one should also know eight months and eight days besides. ॥52॥
5.25.53: And when the breaths flow at the seventeenth, know it to be a year, no doubt; one should know seven months with six days, no doubt. ॥53॥
5.25.54: With the eight-day division he lives two years; four months are to be understood, with a limit of twenty-four days. ॥54॥
5.25.55: When the breaths flow for nine days, the span is three months; two months and another two months, and twelve days are declared. ॥55॥
5.25.56: For those that were stated before, their time is as given earlier; as for the intermediate days, their span is reckoned by that month. ॥56॥
5.25.57: With an eleven-day flow he lives one year; likewise nine months are declared, and days numbering eight as well. ॥57॥
5.25.58: With a twelve-day flow he lives one year; one should know seven months and also state six days. ॥58॥
5.25.59: And when the channel flows up to a limit of thirteen days, he will have a year, and four months are declared besides, ॥59॥
5.25.60: and the remaining life is twenty-four days; there is no doubt. When the flows of breath in the left last fourteen days, ॥60॥
5.25.61: he will have a year, and six months are declared, and twenty-four days of life as well; there is no doubt. ॥61॥
5.25.62: With a fifteen-day flow he lives nine months and twenty-four days; so it is stated by the knowers of time. ॥62॥
5.25.63: With a sixteen-day flow he lives ten months, with an excess of twenty-four days; so it is stated by the knowers of time. ॥63॥
5.25.64: With a seventeen-day flow one's life ends in nine months, with eighteen days here added; so it is stated, O mistress of adepts. ॥64॥
5.25.65: When, O Goddess, the left course lasts up to a limit of eighteen days, life is eight months, and twelve days are declared besides. ॥65॥
5.25.66: Ascertain here with certainty twenty-four days. When, O Goddess, the flow of breath lasts up to a limit of twenty-three days, ॥66॥
5.25.67: four months are declared, and likewise six days in addition. With a twenty-four-day flow he lives three months, ॥67॥
5.25.68: with eighteen days here; they draw life to a close through their movement. Whatever pertains to the intermediate days, those have been declared in brief. ॥68॥
5.25.69: The left course has been described; now hear about the right. With a twenty-eight-day flow he lives for the measure of a lunar fortnight. ॥69॥
5.25.70: With the flow remaining fixed in that next stage, he perishes in ten days; with a flow of thirty days, he perishes in five days. ॥70॥
5.25.71: When, O Goddess, it flows without interruption for thirty-one days, then his life is three days; there is no doubt. ॥71॥
5.25.72: And when the sun (the right channel) flows for a breath-count of thirty-two days, then his life is two days; there is no doubt. ॥72॥
5.25.73: The right breath has been described; I shall tell you of the middle one. When the flow of air goes into one part in the region of the face, ॥73॥
5.25.74: with a rushing flow, he lives one day. This wheel of the dying man has been declared by those who know the ancient lore. ॥74॥
5.25.75: This wheel of time concerning one whose life is ending has been told to you, O Goddess, for the welfare of the worlds. What else do you wish to hear? ॥75॥
5.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of the knowledge of time, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥25॥
5.26.1: The Goddess said: O god, you have described to me the knowledge of the signs of time truly. Now tell me about the cheating of Time (death), how yogins accomplish it in truth. ॥1॥
5.26.2: Time indeed abides close at hand in all creatures; and how one for whom there is no death cheats Time when it has arrived— ॥2॥
5.26.3: Tell me that, O god, showing your affection toward me; and speak for the benefit of yogins, O giver of all happiness. ॥3॥
5.26.4: Śaṅkara said: Listen, O goddess; I shall explain briefly what you have asked me, O Śivā, for the benefit of all human beings. ॥4॥
5.26.5: Earth, water, likewise fire, wind and space: the combination of these is the body made of the five elements. ॥5॥
5.26.6: Space, then, is pervasive, abiding as all-reaching in all of them. In space they dissolve, and from it they arise again. ॥6॥
5.26.7: At separation, the elements of anyone always return to their own abode; there is no permanence of that combination, O beautiful one. ॥7॥
5.26.8: Likewise the wise there, through the power of austerity and mantras as well—they all know all this well; there is no doubt. ॥8॥
5.26.9: The Goddess said: Kāla, of dreadful form and terrifying, by whom all perishes into space, was burnt by you, O sole lord of heaven; then you, pleased again, being praised with hymns—he regained his own nature. ॥9॥
5.26.10: And he was told by you: With your form unseen, you will move among people known only by report. There your great power was seen, and by the boon of you, the Lord, he rose up again. ॥10॥
5.26.11: So now, sir, is there anything here by which Kāla is slain? Tell me that. You are the best of yogins, the Lord, self-dependent, who took on a body for the good of others, O Maheśa. ॥11॥
5.26.12: Śaṅkara said: He is not slain by the best of gods, nor by daityas, nor by yakṣas, rākṣasas, serpents and humans. But those yogins who, intent on meditation, remain in the body, slay Kāla with ease. ॥12॥
5.26.13: Sanatkumāra said: Having heard this from the guru of the three worlds, Gaurī laughed and said: Tell me truly how, and by what, this Kāla is slain. Śambhu at once said to her: O moon-faced one, hear how sinless yogins, single-minded, cast away the whole serpent of Time. ॥13॥
5.26.14: Śaṅkara said: The body, composed of the five elements, always endowed with their qualities, is produced, O fair-hipped one; and the earthly body dissolves into them. ॥14॥
5.26.15: From space wind is born, and from wind fire is born; from fire water is declared to arise, and from that earth comes into being. ॥15॥
5.26.16: The elements beginning with earth go successively into the higher one. Earth is said to have five qualities, and water four. ॥16॥
5.26.17: Fire likewise has three qualities, and wind two; space has sound as its single quality—so it is declared regarding earth and the rest. ॥17॥
5.26.18: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell the fifth: when an element gives up its own respective quality, then that element perishes. ॥18॥
5.26.19: When it takes up its quality, it is said to be manifested. Know the five elements thus in truth, O queen of the gods. ॥19॥
5.26.20: Therefore, O goddess, the yogin desiring to conquer Time should constantly and diligently contemplate the qualities arising from the elements' portions, each at its own time. ॥20॥
5.26.21: The Goddess said: How is Time thoroughly conquered by yogins, O Lord, knower of yoga? Whether by meditation or by mantra—tell me all that. ॥21॥
5.26.22: Śaṅkara said: Listen, O goddess; I shall explain, out of a wish for the welfare of yogins. This exposition of supreme knowledge should not be given to just anyone. ॥22॥
5.26.23: It should be given to one who has faith, who is devoted and wise, not an unbeliever, pure, and ever devoted to dharma, O lovely lady. ॥23॥
5.26.24: The knower of yoga should practise yoga with steady breath on a good seat; in darkness, without a lamp, when people are asleep, he should hold concentration. ॥24॥
5.26.25: Closing the ears with the index fingers and pressing them for a short while, a piercing sound is then heard, arising from the inner fire. ॥25॥
5.26.26: Thus practising from twilight, food eaten is digested even in a moment; it quickly destroys all diseases and the many afflictions such as fever. ॥26॥
5.26.27: He who daily observes this form of sound for two ghaṭikās, having conquered death and desire, may roam here at his own will. ॥27॥
5.26.28: He becomes all-knowing and all-seeing and attains every siddhi. As a cloud thunders in the sky, well laden with the waters of the rainy season, so is that sound. ॥28॥
5.26.29: Hearing it, the yogin is at once freed from the bondage of saṃsāra. Then for yogins it constantly becomes subtler than the subtle. ॥29॥
5.26.30: Thus, O goddess, I have told you the method and sequence of śabdabrahman. As one seeking grain discards the straw, one should abandon bondage entirely. ॥30॥
5.26.31: Those who, having obtained this śabdabrahman, still long for something else, strike the sky with their fist and crave hunger and thirst. ॥31॥
5.26.32: One should know this supreme brahman—giver of happiness, cause of liberation, not external, imperishable, and free of all limiting adjuncts. ॥32॥
5.26.33: Deluded by the noose of Time, fallen under the sway of death's noose, those sinful, evil-minded ones do not know śabdabrahman. ॥33॥
5.26.34: They wander in saṃsāra as long as one does not find the abode; but when the supreme reality is known, one is freed from the bondage of birth. ॥34॥
5.26.35: Having diligently conquered that enemy, sleep and sloth, the great obstacle, sitting always in a comfortable posture, practising śabdabrahman thus— ॥35॥
5.26.36: Even a man a hundred years old, having obtained this, should practise it as long as he lives: it brings conquest of death, firmness of body, health, and increase of vital breath. ॥36॥
5.26.37: Its proof is seen in an old man; how much more in a young person. It is not Oṃkāra, nor a mantra, nor a seed-syllable, nor a letter. ॥37॥
5.26.38: The unstruck, unutterable śabdabrahman, auspicious and supreme—on that the wise constantly and diligently meditate, O goddess, my dear. ॥38॥
5.26.39: Therefore nine sounds are declared, discerned by knowers of prāṇa. I shall carefully describe them—the attainment of nāda—in due order. ॥39॥
5.26.40: The roar (ghoṣa), the ring of bell-metal, the horn, the bell, those born of the vīṇā, flute and the like, the kettledrum, the sound of the conch, and ninth, the thunder of clouds. ॥40॥
5.26.41: Having set aside the nine sounds, one should practise the tuṅkāra. Meditating in this way at all times, the yogin is not stained by merits or by sins. ॥41॥
5.26.42: O Devī, when one who listens through the practice of yoga no longer hears the sound, he dies; therefore the yogin should remain practising day and night. ॥42॥
5.26.43: From that practice the sound arises, and within seven days one conquers death. That sound, O Devī, is ninefold; I shall describe it as it truly is. ॥43॥
5.26.44: First it sounds as ghoṣa, supreme, purifying the self; this sound removes all diseases and is excellent for subjugation and attraction. ॥44॥
5.26.45: Second it sounds like bronze; with it one can halt the movement of living beings, and can bind poison and all spirits and planetary seizers—there is no doubt of this. ॥45॥
5.26.46: Third it sounds like a horn; one should employ it in sorcery, and apply it for causing enmity, for driving away, and for killing an enemy. ॥46॥
5.26.47: The fourth, the Supreme Lord declares, is the sound of a bell; it attracts all the gods—how much more men on earth. ॥47॥
5.26.48: And the maidens of the Yakṣas and Gandharvas, drawn by it, grant the yogin great siddhi as he desires, or even at his will. ॥48॥
5.26.49: The fifth sound is the vīṇā, always heard by yogins; from it, O Devī, arises the power of seeing from afar. ॥49॥
5.26.50: For one meditating on the sound of the flute, knowledge of all principles arises; and one meditating on the kettledrum becomes free from old age and death. ॥50॥
5.26.51: By the sound of the conch, O Queen of the gods, one attains the power of taking any form at will; by the sound of thunder-clouds, the yogin meets with no calamity. ॥51॥
5.26.52: He who with one-pointed mind constantly meditates on the tuṅkāra, which has the form of Brahman—what is there that he cannot accomplish as he wishes, O fair-faced one? ॥52॥
5.26.53: He becomes all-knowing and all-seeing, and goes about taking forms at will; he is not touched by changes—he is Śiva himself, without doubt. ॥53॥
5.26.54: Thus, O Supreme Lady, I have told you all about the nature of Śabdabrahman in its ninefold form. What more do you wish to hear? ॥54॥
5.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of cheating Time, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥26॥
5.27.1: The Goddess said: The yogin attains the state of Vāyu, which arises from the ether of yoga. Tell me all of that, O Lord, if you are pleased with me. ॥1॥
5.27.2: Śaṅkara said: Earlier, wishing for the welfare of yogins, I explained everything: how one has properly conquered Time, and what the sign of Vāyu is. ॥2॥
5.27.3: Knowing by that sign the day of death, the yogin who remains devoted to prāṇāyāma conquers the Time that has come within just half a month, O beautiful one. ॥3॥
5.27.4: The wind dwelling in the heart always kindles the fire; it is the companion of fire. That wind, both outer and inner, is pervasive, all-reaching and great. ॥4॥
5.27.5: Knowledge, understanding, energy — everything proceeds from the wind. He by whom the wind is conquered here has conquered this whole world. ॥5॥
5.27.6: Desiring to destroy old age and death, the yogin, delighting in yoga and wholly intent on concentration and meditation, should always remain in dhāraṇā. ॥6॥
5.27.7: Just as a blacksmith, O sage, fills the bellows through the mouth and accomplishes his work by means of air, so should the yogin practise. ॥7॥
5.27.8: The God is thousandfold, having a thousand eyes, feet and hands; covering the entire earth, he stands beyond it by ten fingers' breadth; on him one should meditate. ॥8॥
5.27.9: One should mutter the Gāyatrī together with its head (śiras), preceded by the vyāhṛtis, three times with breath restrained; that is called prāṇāyāma. ॥9॥
5.27.10: The planets such as the Moon and the Sun go and come back; but those devoted to yoga and meditation do not return even now. ॥10॥
5.27.11: The fruit a twice-born gains by performing austerity for a hundred years, drinking only water from the tip of kuśa grass — that fruit, O Devī, he obtains by a single retention of the breaths. ॥11॥
5.27.12: The twice-born who, rising at dawn, performs even a single prāṇāyāma quickly destroys all sin and goes to Brahmā's world. ॥12॥
5.27.13: He who, untiring, is always devoted to prāṇāyāma in solitude, having conquered old age and death, moves with the wind and becomes a sky-goer (khecarī). ॥13॥
5.27.14: He acquires the form of a siddha, radiance, intelligence, prowess and valour; he equals the wind in speed, and gains praiseworthy well-being and supreme happiness. ॥14॥
5.27.15: I have told in full the perfection of Vāyu which the yogin attains. What he obtains from the practice of light (tejas) too, I shall now tell you, O Queen of the gods. ॥15॥
5.27.16: Sitting in a comfortable posture in his own place, resting where there is no sound of people's talk, he should make the light shine in the middle region by the breath joined with moon and sun. ॥16॥
5.27.17: The vigilant yogin in whom the light residing in fire shines between the eyebrows sees without doubt even what is minute in the world, in darkness devoid of lamps. ॥17॥
5.27.18: Pressing the eyes slightly and carefully with the fingers, the yogin, looking at the star of light, should meditate on it with one-pointed mind for half a muhūrta. ॥18॥
5.27.19: Then, meditating in darkness, he sees the divine light of the Lord — white, red, yellow, black, with the lustre of the rainbow. ॥19॥
5.27.20: It is between the brows, situated on the forehead, with radiance like the rising sun. Knowing it, he, with a body as he wishes, sports assuming any form at will. ॥20॥
5.27.21: There arise absorption in the quieting of causes, entry into another's body, attainment of the powers beginning with aṇimā, and seeing by the mind; ॥21॥
5.27.22: hearing and knowing from afar, invisibility, assuming many forms — and through constant practice, the power of moving in the sky arises. ॥22॥
5.27.23: Even the wise, endowed with learning and study and skilled in many śāstras, are deluded when they follow the power of past karma. ॥23॥
5.27.24: Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they are like the deaf — like blind men in the world, foolish, deluded by sin. ॥24॥
5.27.25: I know this great Person, of the colour of the sun, beyond darkness. Only by knowing him does one pass beyond death; there is no other path for going there. ॥25॥
5.27.26: Thus I have properly told you the excellent method of the light, by which the yogin, conquering Time, attains immortality. ॥26॥
5.27.27: Again I shall tell something still higher, by which death does not occur. Listen attentively, O Devī, with one-pointed mind. ॥27॥
5.27.28: O Devī, this is the fourth (turīya) state for beings, for yogins and meditators alike. The yogin, with mind controlled, seated in a comfortable posture in a suitable place, ॥28॥
5.27.29: keeping his body erect and joining his hands into a cup, drinking the air slowly, slowly with the mouth shaped like a beak, ॥29॥
5.27.30: then in a moment the life-giving waters situated in the palate flow forth. He should draw them in, taking up with the breath that cool water, the nectar. ॥30॥
5.27.31: Drinking it every day, the yogin does not fall under the power of death; he has a divine body, great splendour, and is free from thirst and hunger. ॥31॥
5.27.32: In strength he is an elephant, in speed a horse, in sight Suparṇa (Garuḍa), with keen hearing even from afar; his black hair is curled and wavy, his complexion equal to that of Gandharvas and Vidyādharas. ॥32॥
5.27.33: Such a man would live a hundred years of the gods and attain equality with the wise Vākpati (Bṛhaspati). Living thus he attains the state of a sky-goer, moving as he pleases, ever happy. ॥33॥
5.27.34: Again I shall tell another method, which is guarded with effort even by the gods; listen to it, O fair-faced one. ॥34॥
5.27.35: Curling back the tongue towards the palate, the yogin should practise; within a short time he gradually reaches the lambikā (the uvula region). ॥35॥
5.27.36: Then, when touched, it releases cool nectar; drinking it constantly, that yogin attains immortality. ॥36॥
5.27.37: The tip of the tongue (the ra-point), the tip of the lambikā, the contact as of a palm, reaching the bindu of the white lotus — drawn by that, this nectar falls in the supreme abode, delighting the deities. It is the essence, the deliverer from saṃsāra, that which carries one across committed sins, the deliverer from Time, joined with Tāra (Om). He whose body is flooded by it does not die and is freed from hunger and thirst. ॥37॥
5.27.38: O daughter of the mountain, this earth is indeed sustained by these four kinds of yogins; through their constancy, how could there be an end to the whole world, which exists for the attainment of happiness? In a dream the embodied one always creates everything, regarding as real even what is sorrow; so too in heaven; and from the earth, or from that, something of the four comes forth. ॥38॥
5.27.39: Therefore the earth, joined with yoga, is protected in due order by men endowed with prudence and modesty, knowers of dharma, through mantras, austerities, and herbs together with vows and observances. The primal God of beings, united with the four, does not waver. Therefore I shall now set forth the method handed down, concerning the shadow, which is called Śiva's. ॥39॥
5.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of cheating Time and attaining Śiva, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥27॥
5.28.1: The Goddess said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, you have told me the cheating of death, the nature of Śabdabrahman, and the excellent marks of yoga. ॥1॥
5.28.2: You have told in brief the excellent knowledge concerning the shadow; explain it in detail, out of desire for the welfare of yogins. ॥2॥
5.28.3: Śaṅkara said: Listen, O Devī, I shall describe the marks of the shadow-person, knowing which properly a man is freed from all sins. ॥3॥
5.28.4: Placing the sun, or the moon, behind oneself, O fair-complexioned one, wearing white garments, garlanded, perfumed with scents, incense and the like, ॥4॥
5.28.5: one should call to mind my great mantra, which grants the fruit of all desires, nine-fold and condensed into a seed (piṇḍa), and should gaze intently at one's own shadow. ॥5॥
5.28.6: Having seen it again in the sky, white in form, he, single-minded, sees Śiva, the supreme cause. ॥6॥
5.28.7: He attains Brahman — so it is declared by the knowers of time; he is freed from sins such as the killing of a brahmin; there is no doubt in this. ॥7॥
5.28.8: When he sees it headless, death will come within six months; for that yogin all this that has been said holds exactly so. ॥8॥
5.28.9: If the shadow is white, one should know it signifies dharma; if black, one should declare sin; if red, one should know bondage; if yellow, one should foretell enmity. ॥9॥
5.28.10: If it appears armless, there will be destruction of kinsmen; if with two mouths, fear of hunger; if without hips, the wife perishes; if without shanks, wealth indeed is lost. ॥10॥
5.28.11: If the feet are absent, there will be going to a foreign land. This has been told by me; it should be carefully examined by a man, O Maheśvarī. ॥11॥
5.28.12: Having properly seen that figure and settling it by oneself within oneself, one should repeat the nine-fold mantra, my heart mantra, O Maheśvarī. ॥12॥
5.28.13: When a year has passed, there is nothing the mantra-practitioner cannot accomplish; he attains the eight qualities beginning with aṇimā and the power of moving through the sky. ॥13॥
5.28.14: Again I shall tell something else: how to know the Śakti, hard to approach, who is seen directly in the world, standing before the wise. ॥14॥
5.28.15: She who is unknowable, who in the world is depicted as Kuṇḍalī coiled like a serpent — that mātrā, though dwelling in the vehicle of the body, is seen, yet is not recited. ॥15॥
5.28.16: She who abides at the crown of the cosmic egg, who is ever praised by the Vedas, the mother of all knowledges, is celebrated as the Secret Knowledge. ॥16॥
5.28.17: She is declared to be Khecarā, abiding in all living beings, visible and invisible, immovable, eternal, manifest and unmanifest, everlasting. ॥17॥
5.28.18: Without letters yet joined with letters, she is called Bindumālinī; the yogin who always beholds her becomes one who has accomplished all that is to be done. ॥18॥
5.28.19: Whatever fruit of charity would arise from bathing at all tīrthas, and whatever fruit of all sacrifices there is — that, then, from the sight of Mālinī, ॥19॥
5.28.20: he obtains here; there is no doubt — this has truly been told by me. Whatever fruit comes from bathing at all tīrthas and giving gifts in every way, ॥20॥
5.28.21: and whatever fruit there is of all sacrifices, O Devī — that fruit a man would obtain. Why say more, O Maheśānī? He attains all desires. ॥21॥
5.28.22: Therefore the wise one should constantly practise this knowledge in accordance with yoga. From practice arises accomplishment; through practice yoga grows. ॥22॥
5.28.23: Through practice understanding is gained; through practice one attains liberation. Practice, the cause of liberation, should be constantly undertaken by the intelligent. ॥23॥
5.28.24: Thus this has been told, O Devī, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. What other truth is asked? Speak; I tell you the truth. ॥24॥
5.28.25: Sūta said: Having heard thus the words of Brahmā's son, which bestow the highest goal, Vyāsa, the son of Parāśara, became extremely pleased, O lords of sages. ॥25॥
5.28.26: Vyāsa, supremely satisfied, bowed again and again to Sanatkumāra, the all-knowing son of Brahmā, treasure of compassion. ॥26॥
5.28.27: Then Vyāsa, that lord of sages, son of Kālī, praised him, Sanatkumāra, the ocean of divine knowledge, O sages. ॥27॥
5.28.28: Vyāsa said: I am fulfilled, O best of sages; Brahmanhood has been bestowed on me by you. Salutation to you, salutation to you. You are blessed, the foremost knower of Brahman! ॥28॥
5.28.29: Sūta said: Having thus praised the great sage, Brahmā's son, Vyāsa the son of Kālī fell silent, well pleased and filled with supreme bliss. ॥29॥
5.28.30: Brahmā's son, honoured by him, took leave of him and went, well pleased, to his own abode, O Śaunaka; Vyāsa too was delighted at heart. ॥30॥
5.28.31: Thus, O brahmins, I have described to you the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and the son of Kālī, which gives happiness, is joined with the highest truth, and increases knowledge. ॥31॥
5.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of seeing the shadow-person, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥28॥
5.29.1: Śaunaka said: I have heard the great narrative you recounted, the dialogue between Sanatkumāra and Kāleya Vyāsa, which bestows the highest truth. ॥1॥
5.29.2: Therefore I wish to hear how Brahmā's creation came about. Tell me, just as you heard it from Vyāsa. ॥2॥
5.29.3: Sūta said: O sage, listen to the divine story, destroyer of all sins, which I am narrating: wondrous, rich in meaning, and expansive as it has been heard in tradition. ॥3॥
5.29.4: Whoever has it recited, or hears it repeatedly, sustains his own lineage and is honoured in the heavenly world. ॥4॥
5.29.5: That which is Pradhāna and Puruṣa, eternal, whose nature is both being and non-being — having become Pradhāna-Puruṣa, the fashioner of the worlds created all. ॥5॥
5.29.6: Know him, O best of sages, to be Brahmā of immeasurable power, the creator of all beings, devoted wholly to Nārāyaṇa. ॥6॥
5.29.7: Since he devised them, from whom all the pure kalpas come into being, O tiger among sages — salutation to that Self-born one. ॥7॥
5.29.8: Having bowed to that Hiraṇyagarbha, the Puruṣa and Lord, I shall again relate the unsurpassed creation. ॥8॥
5.29.9: Brahmā is the creator, Hari the protector, and Maheśvara the destroyer; for that creation there is no other agent, as it proceeds thus age after age. ॥9॥
5.29.10: That Self-born Lord, wishing to create various beings, first created the waters alone, and released his seed into them. ॥10॥
5.29.11: The waters are called nārā, for the waters are the offspring of Nara. Since they were formerly his abode (ayana), he is therefore known as Nārāyaṇa. ॥11॥
5.29.12: That egg lying in the water became golden in colour; in it Brahmā himself was born, renowned as Svayambhū. ॥12॥
5.29.13: Lord Hiraṇyagarbha, having dwelt there for a year, split the egg in two and fashioned heaven and earth. ॥13॥
5.29.14: The fourteen worlds were arranged below and above; between those two halves the Lord created the sky (ākāśa). ॥14॥
5.29.15: He set the earth floating on the waters and established the ten directions. At that time he created mind, speech, desire and anger, and also delight. ॥15॥
5.29.16: That greatly radiant one created the seven mind-born sons: Marīci, Atri and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasiṣṭha. ॥16॥
5.29.17: These are determined in the Purāṇa to be the seven Brahmās. Then Brahmā again created the Rudras, born of anger, ॥17॥
5.29.18: and the sage Sanatkumāra, the eldest of all. These seven are born first, and afterwards the Rudras on all sides. ॥18॥
5.29.19: Hence Sanatkumāra remains with his radiance withdrawn. Of those seven, seven great divine lineages, honoured by the divine sages, ॥19॥
5.29.20: come forth, active in rites and adorned with great sages. He created lightnings, thunderbolts and clouds, and red rainbows (Indra's bows), ॥20॥
5.29.21: and in the beginning he created the waters, and he created Parjanya the rain-god. For the accomplishment of sacrifice he fashioned the Ṛk verses, the Yajus formulas and the Sāman chants. ॥21॥
5.29.22: With these they worshipped the venerable gods — so we have heard. From his mouth he produced the gods, and from his chest the Pitṛs; from his organ of generation he made humans, and from his loins he fashioned the Asuras. ॥22॥
5.29.23: Beings high and low were born from the limbs of that Prajāpati Āpava as he brought forth the creation of beings. ॥23॥
5.29.24: When the beings being created did not multiply, then, dividing his own body in two, he became woman and man. ॥24॥
5.29.25: Then he created all beings, pervading everything by his greatness. Viṣṇu created Virāj; that Virāj, once created, brought forth the Puruṣa. ॥25॥
5.29.26: Know him to be the second Manu, and the beginning of the Manu-period as well. That Vairāja Puruṣa, the lord, created all beings. ॥26॥
5.29.27: These are the progeny of that emanation of Nārāyaṇa, he too being not born of a womb. From that knowledge one becomes long-lived, famous, fortunate and rich in offspring. ॥27॥
5.29.28: Thus the primal creation has been described to you, O best of sages. Knowing the primal creation in this way, one would attain whatever destiny one desires. ॥28॥
5.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the first creation, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥29॥
5.30.1: Sūta said: When the creatures had been created, then the Prajāpati Āpava, the Puruṣa, obtained as his wife Śatarūpā, who was not born from a womb. ॥1॥
5.30.2: Through the greatness of Āpava, who stood pervading heaven, and through dharma alone, that great-souled Śatarūpā too was born. ॥2॥
5.30.3: She, having practised for a hundred years austerity most difficult to perform, obtained as husband the Puruṣa of blazing austerity. ॥3॥
5.30.4: That Puruṣa was born as Svāyambhuva and is called Manu; his Manvantara is said here to be of seventy-one yugas. ॥4॥
5.30.5: From the Vairāja Puruṣa the heroic Śatarūpā bore offspring; Priyavrata and Uttānapāda were born of Vīrakā Śatarūpā. ॥5॥
5.30.6: The highly fortunate one named Kāmyā was the daughter of Prajāpati Kardama; Kāmyā had three sons: Saṃrāṭ, Sākṣi and Raviṭ, each mighty. ॥6॥
5.30.7: The lord Uttānapāda begot sons equal to Śakra, and the divine son Dhruva, radiant with the bliss of the Self. ॥7॥
5.30.8: The daughter of Dharma, fair-hipped, renowned by the name Sunīti, born of Dharma, was the mother of Dhruva. ॥8॥
5.30.9: Dhruva, though a boy, performed austerity in the forest for three thousand divine years, praying for an imperishable abode. ॥9॥
5.30.10: Pleased, the lord Brahmā, the Prajāpati, gave him an abode equal to his own, immovable, in front of the seven sages. ॥10॥
5.30.11: From that Dhruva two sons were born, Puṣṭi and Dhānya. Puṣṭi likewise begot from Samutthā five sinless sons: ॥11॥
5.30.12: Ripu, Ripuñjaya, Vipra, Vṛkala and Vṛṣatejas. And thus Ripu's queen bore Cākṣuṣa, renowned in all directions. ॥12॥
5.30.13: Cākṣuṣa Manu begot Varuṇa in Puṣkariṇī. From Manu, in Naḍvalā, ten sons of great vigour were born, ॥13॥
5.30.14: in the daughter of Prajāpati Vairāja, O best of sages: Puru, Māsa, Śatadyumna, Tapasvin, Satyavit, Kavi, ॥14॥
5.30.15: Agniṣṭoma, Atirātra, Atimanyu and Suyaśas — these ten. Āgneyī bore to Pūru six sons of great splendour: ॥15॥
5.30.16: Aṅga, Sumanas, Khyāti, Sṛti, Aṅgiras and Gaya. Sunīthā, the wife of Aṅga, bore from Aṅga a single son, Vena. ॥16॥
5.30.17: Because of Vena's misconduct, great wrath arose in them; the sages devoted to dharma slew him with a mere hum. ॥17॥
5.30.18: Then, entreated by Sunīthā for the sake of progeny, the Sārasvata sages churned his right hand. ॥18॥
5.30.19: When Vena's hand was churned, Pṛthu came forth from it; he was born with bow and armour, resembling the sun in splendour. ॥19॥
5.30.20: He was indeed an incarnation of Viṣṇu, for the protection of the people, for the safeguarding of dharma, and for the punishment of the wicked. ॥20॥
5.30.21: Then Pṛthu, son of Vena, the forefather of the kṣatriyas, protected the earth; that lord of the earth was the first of those consecrated by the Rājasūya. ॥21॥
5.30.22: From him too arose the skilful Sūta and Māgadha. By him, O best of sages, this earth-cow was milked for the welfare of all. ॥22॥
5.30.23: The king, performer of a hundred sacrifices, became the giver of livelihood to all — gods, sages, suras and rākṣasas — and especially to humans. ॥23॥
5.30.24: To Pṛthu were born two sons, kings on earth who knew dharma: Vijitāśva and Haryakṣa, great heroes, well renowned. ॥24॥
5.30.25: Śikhaṇḍinī bore a son, Prācīnabarhis; his kuśa grass, with tips pointing east, spread over the surface of the earth. ॥25॥
5.30.26: The daughter of the Ocean was duly married by him according to dharma; having taken a wife, the king, a great lord, shone all the more. ॥26॥
5.30.27: From the daughter of the Ocean, ten divine sons were born to Prācīnabarhis, the performer of many sacrifices. ॥27॥
5.30.28: All of them, called the Prācetasas, masters of the science of archery, following one common dharma, performed great austerity, ॥28॥
5.30.29: for ten thousand years, lying in the waters of the ocean, chanting the Rudra-song and intent on meditation upon Śiva. ॥29॥
5.30.30: While they were practising austerity, trees grew over the earth; and the earth being unprotected, destruction of the people ensued. ॥30॥
5.30.31: Having returned from austerity with excellent boons obtained, they saw those trees, O tiger among sages, and grew angry, wishing to burn them, mighty through austerity. ॥31॥
5.30.32: Those Prācetasas emitted fire and wind from their mouths; the wind uprooted the trees and the fire burned them. ॥32॥
5.30.33: Then, seeing the destruction of the trees, when only a few trees remained, the powerful King Soma approached them and said: ॥33॥
5.30.34: Soma said: Restrain your anger, O kings, all you sons of Prācīnabarhis. This fair-complexioned maiden has come into being as the daughter of the trees. ॥34॥
5.30.35: Knowing the future, I have nurtured her from the embryo. Let her be your wife, O highly fortunate ones, she who will increase the lunar race. ॥35॥
5.30.36: In her will be born the learned Prajāpati named Dakṣa, the maker of creation, of great splendour, the ancient son of Brahmā. ॥36॥
5.30.37: With half of your splendour and with this splendour of mine, that king, full of Brahmā's splendour, will increase the creatures. ॥37॥
5.30.38: Then, at Soma's word, the Pracetases lovingly took as wife, according to dharma, that fair-complexioned maiden born of the trees. ॥38॥
5.30.39: From them, in her, the Prajāpati named Dakṣa was born; and he, of great splendour, was born with a portion of Soma, O sage. ॥39॥
5.30.40: Having created by mind the immobile and mobile beings, the two-footed and the four-footed, Dakṣa began creation through sexual union. ॥40॥
5.30.41: He married, with proper rites and in accordance with right dharma, the daughter of Prajāpati Vīraṇa, Vīraṇī by name, a woman devoted to her husband. ॥41॥
5.30.42: In her he begot ten thousand virtuous sons, the Haryaśvas; and they became detached from worldly life through the instruction of Nārada. ॥42॥
5.30.43: Hearing that, Dakṣa again begot in her sons named the Subalāśvas, numbering a thousand. ॥43॥
5.30.44: They too, through that sage's instruction, went the way of their brothers; detached and following the path of mendicants, they did not return to their father's presence. ॥44॥
5.30.45: Hearing that, enraged, he gave the sage an unbearable curse: O lover of strife, may you find no stable abode anywhere. ॥45॥
5.30.46: Then, pacified by the Creator (Brahmā), he afterwards created daughters, of the nature of great radiance and endowed with virtues, O lord of sages. ॥46॥
5.30.47: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, two likewise to the son of Brahmā, and two then to Aṅgiras. ॥47॥
5.30.48: Two he gave to the learned sage Kṛśāśva, O best of sages; and the remaining ones, called the Nakṣatras, lord Dakṣa gave to Soma. ॥48॥
5.30.49: From those daughters of Dakṣa were born the gods, the asuras and others—many renowned sons; by all of them the world was filled. ॥49॥
5.30.50: From then on, O chief of brahmins, creatures have been born of sexual union; the creation of earlier beings is said to have been through will, sight and touch. ॥50॥
5.30.51: Śaunaka said: Dakṣa was born from Brahmā's thumb, as you told earlier. How then did that great ascetic again obtain the status of being son of the Pracetases? ॥51॥
5.30.52: O Sūta, you should resolve this doubt of mine. This is a wonder: how did he become Soma's father-in-law? ॥52॥
5.30.53: Sūta said: Origin and dissolution always take place among beings; in every kalpa all these—Dakṣa and the others—come into being anew, O sage. ॥53॥
5.30.54: Whoever knows this creation of Dakṣa, with all its moving and unmoving beings, is blessed with offspring, full of life-span, and is honoured in the heavenly world. ॥54॥
5.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The description of creation, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥30॥
5.31.1: Śaunaka said: O son of Sūta, quickly tell me in detail this creation of the gods and the Dānavas, and of the Gandharvas, serpents and Rākṣasas. ॥1॥
5.31.2: Sūta said: When that creation did not increase, the Prajāpati summoned the daughter of Vīraṇa, endowed with excellent austerity, for the purpose of creation. ॥2॥
5.31.3: He created various beings by the law of sexual union. Hear of them, O very wise one; I shall tell you briefly. ॥3॥
5.31.4: Uniting with that Vīriṇī, the mighty Prajāpati Dakṣa himself begot five thousand sons. ॥4॥
5.31.5: Seeing these sons who had been created, the sage Nārada spoke to them — that Nārada who was born at the sacrificial session of Parameṣṭhin (Brahmā). ॥5॥
5.31.6: Or rather, having heard from Kaśyapa that the creation of beings would take place in the daughters of Dakṣa alone, he therefore spoke to them. ॥6॥
5.31.7: Not knowing the world, how will you, foolish ones, carry out creation, ignorant as you are of any direction? Therefore, first learn the extent of that earth. ॥7॥
5.31.8: Thus addressed, they all set out vigourously to learn the regions; and not reaching their end, they did not return to their father's house. ॥8॥
5.31.9: Knowing that, he again begot five hundred sons; and to them too the all-seeing Nārada spoke once more. ॥9॥
5.31.10: Nārada said: Not knowing the measure of the earth, how will you carry out creation? You are all fools indeed; why are you eager to perform creation? ॥10॥
5.31.11: Sūta said: They too, the Subalāśvas, sons of Dakṣa, hearing his words, went forth in every direction, just as the Haryaśvas had done before. ॥11॥
5.31.12: Reaching the endless expanse (puṣkara), they too met their ruin; even today they do not return, like rivers that do not return from the oceans. ॥12॥
5.31.13: From that time on, O sage, a brother who sets out intent on searching for a brother perishes; therefore a wise man should not do so. ॥13॥
5.31.14: Learning that these sons too were lost, Prajāpati Dakṣa in anger pronounced a curse upon the great-souled Nārada: ॥14॥
5.31.15: O lover of strife, may you not find a settled abode anywhere; and wherever you are present in the world, may there always be strife. ॥15॥
5.31.16: Then, pacified by the Creator (Brahmā), Prajāpati Dakṣa afterwards created sixty daughters in Vīriṇī — so we have heard. ॥16॥
5.31.17: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, twenty-seven to Soma, and four to Ariṣṭanemi. ॥17॥
5.31.18: Likewise two to the son of Brahmā, two to Aṅgiras, and two to the learned Kṛśāśva. Hear from me their names. ॥18॥
5.31.19: Arundhatī, Vasu, Yāmi, Lambā, Bhānu, Marutvatī, Saṅkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sandhyā and Viśvā, O sage — ॥19॥
5.31.20: these, O sage, are the wives of Dharma. Hear from me their offspring: the Viśvedevas were born of Viśvā, and Sādhyā gave birth to the Sādhyas. ॥20॥
5.31.21: From Marutvatī were born the Marutvats, from Vasu the Vasus, from Bhānu all the Bhānus, and from Muhūrtā the Muhūrtas. ॥21॥
5.31.22: From Lambā was born Ghoṣa; Nāgavīthī was born of Yāmi; and from Arundhatī was born Pṛthivīviṣama (the earthly realm). ॥22॥
5.31.23: From Saṅkalpā was born Saṅkalpa, whose nature is truth. The sons of Vasu are eight, Aya and the rest; hear of them, O Śaunaka. ॥23॥
5.31.24: Aya, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa — these by name are the eight Vasus. ॥24॥
5.31.25: The sons of Aya were Vaitaṇḍa, Śrama, Śānta and Muni. The son of Dhruva was the blessed Kāla, who sustains the worlds. ॥25॥
5.31.26: The son of Soma was the blessed Varcas, through whom one becomes radiant. The son of Dhara was Draviṇa, and likewise Hutahavyavaha. ॥26॥
5.31.27: From Manoharā were born Śiśira, Prāṇa and Ramaṇa. The wife of Anila was Śivā, whose sons were Purojava ॥27॥
5.31.28: and Avijñātagati — these two were the sons of Anila. The son of Agni was Kumāra, born in a clump of reeds enveloped in splendour. ॥28॥
5.31.29: After him were born Śākha, Viśākha and Naigameya. Being the offspring of the Kṛttikās, he is known as Kārttikeya. ॥29॥
5.31.30: To Pratyūṣa was born a son, a seer named Devala. Devala too had two wise sons, who had progeny. ॥30॥
5.31.31: The sister of Bṛhaspati, an excellent woman devoted to celibacy and perfected in yoga, then roamed all over the entire world. ॥31॥
5.31.32: She became the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth of the Vasus; and from him, O highly fortunate one, was born Prajāpati Viśvakarman, ॥32॥
5.31.33: the maker of thousands of crafts, the carpenter of the gods, the maker of all ornaments, the foremost of craftsmen, ॥33॥
5.31.34: who made the aerial chariots of all the deities, and by whose craft, that great-souled one's, human beings make their living. ॥34॥
5.31.35: Raivata, Aja, Bhava, Bhīma, Vāma, Ugra, Vṛṣākapi, Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Bahurūpa and Mahān — ॥35॥
5.31.36: Rudras were born by the crore of the woman Sarūpā; among them eleven are chief. Hear their names, O sage. ॥36॥
5.31.37: Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Tvaṣṭṛ, the mighty Rudra, Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka, Aparājita, ॥37॥
5.31.38: Vṛṣākapi, Śambhu, Kapardin and Raivata — these are declared the eleven Rudras, lords of the three worlds. ॥38॥
5.31.39: Thus a hundred Rudras of immeasurable might have been described. Now hear the names of Kaśyapa's wives, O best of sages. ॥39॥
5.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named The description of creation, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥31॥
5.32.1: Sūta said: Aditi, Diti, Surasā, Ariṣṭā, Ilā and Danu; Surabhi, Vinatā, Tāmrā, Krodhavaśā and Khaśā, ॥1॥
5.32.2: and Kadrū and Muni, O best of brahmins — hear from me the offspring born of them. In the excellent former manvantara there were twelve foremost gods, ॥2॥
5.32.3: named the Tuṣitas. They spoke to one another, when the Vaivasvata period was approaching, in the period of the illustrious Manu Cākṣuṣa: ॥3॥
5.32.4: For the welfare of all the worlds, having gathered together, come quickly, O gods, and having entered into Aditi, ॥4॥
5.32.5: let us be born in the coming manvantara; there will be good for the virtuous. Thus addressed, all of them, in the period of Manu Cākṣuṣa, ॥5॥
5.32.6: were born of Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, in Aditi, the daughter of Dakṣa. There Viṣṇu and Śakra were born once again. ॥6॥
5.32.7: And Aryaman, Dhātṛ, Tvaṣṭṛ and Pūṣan likewise, Vivasvat, Savitṛ, and Mitra and Varuṇa, ॥7॥
5.32.8: Aṃśa and Bhaga of surpassing splendour — these are remembered as the twelve Ādityas. Those who were formerly the Tuṣita gods in the period of Cākṣuṣa, ॥8॥
5.32.9: they, long ago in that period, are remembered as the twelve Ādityas. Thus the offspring of Aditi have been told in order, O Śaunaka. ॥9॥
5.32.10: The twenty-seven of good vows who were declared to be the wives of Soma — of them were born offspring, radiant ones of immeasurable splendour. ॥10॥
5.32.11: Of the wives of Ariṣṭanemi there were here sixteen offspring. Of the learned Bahuputra, four Lightnings are remembered as offspring. ॥11॥
5.32.12: Of Kṛśāśva, O divine sage, the divine weapons are remembered as offspring; and likewise, O sage, Dhūmrakeśa was born in his wife Arcis. ॥12॥
5.32.13: Svadhā and Satī were two wives: Svadhā the elder, Satī the younger. Svadhā bore the Pitṛs; Satī bore the Atharvāṅgirasa Veda. ॥13॥
5.32.14: These are born again at the end of a thousand yugas; and all the hosts of gods, the thirty-three, are born at will. ॥14॥
5.32.15: Just as the sun constantly rises and sets here, so those hosts of gods come into being age after age. ॥15॥
5.32.16: In Diti two sons were born of Kaśyapa — so we have heard: Hiraṇyakaśipu and the mighty Hiraṇyākṣa. ॥16॥
5.32.17: A daughter, Siṃhikā, was born, who became the wife of Vipracitti. Hiraṇyakaśipu had four sons of renowned vigour: ॥17॥
5.32.18: Anuhrāda, Hrāda and the mighty Saṃhrāda, and the youngest among them, Prahrāda, whose mind was set on contemplating devotion to Viṣṇu. ॥18॥
5.32.19: Of Anuhrāda, in Sūryā, were born Pulomā and Mahiṣa; Hrāda's wife Dhamani bore Vātāpi and Ilvala. ॥19॥
5.32.20: Saṃhrāda's wife Kṛti then bore Pañcajana. Virocana was the son of Prahrāda; of him, in Devī, Bali was born. ॥20॥
5.32.21: Bali had a hundred sons in Aśanā, O lord of sages. Bali was a great Śaiva, wholly devoted to devotion to Śiva, ॥21॥
5.32.22: generous by nature and noble, remembered as one whose fame and austerity were holy. His son named Bāṇa was also an eminent, wise Śaiva, who, having fully pleased Śiva, obtained the leadership of the Gaṇas. ॥22॥
5.32.23: That story of the great-souled Bāṇa you have heard before — the hero who in battle made Kṛṣṇa well pleased. ॥23॥
5.32.24: The sons of Hiraṇyākṣa were five, learned and exceedingly mighty: Kukura, Śakuni, and Bhūtasantāpana, ॥24॥
5.32.25: the valiant Mahānāda, and likewise Kālanābha. Thus the sons of Diti have been told; now hear, O sage, of the sons of Danu. ॥25॥
5.32.26: The sons of Danu were a hundred, of fierce valour: Ayomukha, Śambara, Kapola and Vāmana, ॥26॥
5.32.27: Vaiśvānara and Pulomā, Vidrāvaṇa and Mahāśiras, Svarbhānu, Vṛṣaparvan and the mighty Vipracitti. ॥27॥
5.32.28: All these sons of Danu were born of Kaśyapa. Hear of their daughters, O sage; I tell you incidentally, O sinless one. ॥28॥
5.32.29: Of Svarbhānu the daughter was Prabhā; of Pulomā the daughter was Śacī; Upadānavī, Hayaśirā and Śarmiṣṭhā were the daughters of Vṛṣaparvan. ॥29॥
5.32.30: Pulomikā and Pulomā, both daughters of Vaiśvānara, of many offspring and great might, became the wives of Mārīci (Kaśyapa). ॥30॥
5.32.31: In those two, Marīci('s son) begot sixty thousand sons, delights of the Dānavas, endowed with great austerity. ॥31॥
5.32.32: The Paulomas and Kālakhañjas, the mightiest of the Dānavas, dwellers in Hiraṇyapura, who could not be slain by the gods, ॥32॥
5.32.33: invulnerable by the grace of the Grandfather, were slain by Savyasācin (Arjuna). Then, born in Siṃhikā, were likewise the sons of Vipracitti, ॥33॥
5.32.34: born of the union of Daitya and Dānava, of fierce valour — thirteen very mighty ones, known as the Saiṃhikeyas: ॥34॥
5.32.35: Rāhu, Śalya — very powerful ones — and Bala of great strength, Vātāpi, Namuci, then Ilvala, and Svasṛpa, ॥35॥
5.32.36: Ajika, Naraka, and likewise Kālanābha, Śaramāṇa, Śara and Kalpa — these were the increasers of the lineage. ॥36॥
5.32.37: Their sons and grandsons, who increased the lineage of Danu, arose in great numbers; because of their extent they are not described. ॥37॥
5.32.38: In the family of Saṃhrāda were born the Daitya Nivātakavacas; in it also arose the Maruts, whose selves were refined by austerity. ॥38॥
