5.32.39: The six principal ones, of great strength, are proclaimed as daughters of Tāmrā: Kākī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Sugrīvī, and likewise Śukī, ॥39॥
5.32.40: Gṛdhrikā, Aśvī and Ulūkī — these are proclaimed as the daughters of Tāmrā. Kākī gave birth to crows, Ulūkī to owls. ॥40॥
5.32.41: Śyenī bore hawks, Bhāsī bore bhāsa-birds, Gṛdhrī bore vultures, Śukī bore parrots, and Sugrīvī bore auspicious birds. ॥41॥
5.32.42: Tāmrā, the beloved of Kaśyapa, also gave birth to horses, camels and donkeys. Thus the lineage of Tāmrā has been declared. ॥42॥
5.32.43: Vinatā had two sons, Aruṇa and Garuḍa; Suparṇa Garuḍa was the best of flying creatures, fearsome by his own deeds. ॥43॥
5.32.44: Of Surasā were born a thousand serpents of immeasurable might, many-headed, moving through the sky, great-souled. ॥44॥
5.32.45: Their chief kings were Śeṣa, Vāsuki and Takṣaka, Airāvata, Mahāpadma, and both Kambala and Aśvatara, ॥45॥
5.32.46: Elāpatra and Padma, Karkoṭaka and Dhanañjaya, Mahānīla and Mahākarṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Balāhaka, ॥46॥
5.32.47: Kuhara and Puṣpadanta, Durmukha and Sumukha, Bahuśa and Khararoman, and Pāṇi — these and others. ॥47॥
5.32.48: Then come the hosts of Krodhavaśā, and all of her offspring are fanged creatures; egg-born birds and water-born creatures are also counted, and the beasts are held to be of Varāhī. ॥48॥
5.32.49: Of Anāyuṣā fifty sons of great strength were born: Bala and Vṛkṣa, then Vikṣara, and likewise Bṛhan. ॥49॥
5.32.50: Surabhi gave birth to hares and likewise buffaloes; Ilā gave birth to trees, creepers, vines and all species of grasses. ॥50॥
5.32.51: Khaśā bore the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, and Muni likewise the Apsarases; Ariṣṭā gave birth to serpents, and Prabhā indeed to the best of men. ॥51॥
5.32.52: These descendants of Kaśyapa have been described to you, O lord of sages, whose sons and grandsons number in the hundreds and thousands. ॥52॥
5.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The description of the lineage of Kaśyapa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥32॥
5.33.1: Sūta said: This, dear one, is known as the creation in the Svārociṣa Manvantara. But in the Vaivasvata Manvantara, at the great, extended sacrifice of Varuṇa, ॥1॥
5.33.2: the creation of beings by Brahmā as he offered oblations is told here. Those seven mind-born brahmarṣis who had been born earlier, ॥2॥
5.33.3: the Grandfather himself made them his sons. Among them arose the conflict of the gods and the Dānavas, O great sage. ॥3॥
5.33.4: Diti, whose sons had been destroyed, approached Kaśyapa. That Kaśyapa, pleased at heart, having been duly propitiated by her, ॥4॥
5.33.5: offered her a boon; and she then chose a boon: a son capable of slaying Indra, of immeasurable might. ॥5॥
5.33.6: And he, of very great austerity, granted her the boon she asked, and also prescribed the observance of celibacy and other rules for a hundred years. ॥6॥
5.33.7: That pure, fair-complexioned lady carried the embryo; Diti likewise kept the rule of celibacy and the rest. ॥7॥
5.33.8: Then, having placed that embryo in Diti, Kaśyapa of praiseworthy vows went off to perform austerity, delighted in mind. ॥8॥
5.33.9: And Pākaśāsana (Indra) became eager to find a lapse in her; when the hundred years were short by one, he saw just such a lapse in her. ॥9॥
5.33.10: Without washing her feet, Diti then lay down to sleep with her head turned downward, owing to the weight of what was destined to happen. ॥10॥
5.33.11: At that moment Śakra, the thunderbolt-wielder, entering her womb, cut that embryo into seven parts. ॥11॥
5.33.12: That embryo, being split by the thunderbolt, then cried loudly. Saying, do not weep, the thunderbolt-wielder again cut each of the seven that were weeping; yet even so they did not die. ॥12॥
5.33.13: Being cut, all of them, with joined palms, said to him, O sage: Why do you wish to kill us, Śakra? We are your brothers, the Maruts. ॥13॥
5.33.14: All of them were accepted by Indra into brotherhood, and they abandoned their Daitya nature, O brahmin-seer, by the will of Śaṅkara. ॥14॥
5.33.15: Those gods, named the Maruts, became very mighty—forty-nine sky-rovers, companions of the thunderbolt-wielder. ॥15॥
5.33.16: To those beings, once they had multiplied, Hari, the Prajāpati, gave kingdoms in due order, beginning with Pṛthu; hear about that. ॥16॥
5.33.17: He is Ariṣṭa, the Puruṣa, the hero, Kṛṣṇa, Jiṣṇu, Prajāpati, Parjanya and the lord of wealth; this whole world is his. ॥17॥
5.33.18: I have properly told you this creation of beings, O great sage. Hear the division of the kingdoms; I shall now tell it to you in order. ॥18॥
5.33.19: Having consecrated Pṛthu, son of Vena, to supreme sovereignty, the Grandfather then began to assign the kingdoms in order. ॥19॥
5.33.20: He consecrated Soma to the rule of the twice-born, the plants, the stars and planets, the sacrifices and the austerities. ॥20॥
5.33.21: He installed Varuṇa in the rule of the waters, the lord Vaiśravaṇa over kings, Viṣṇu likewise over the Ādityas, and Pāvaka over the Vasus. ॥21॥
5.33.22: Dakṣa over the Prajāpatis, Vāsava over the Maruts, and Prahlāda of immeasurable might over the Daityas and Dānavas. ॥22॥
5.33.23: He consecrated Yama Vaivasvata to the rule of the ancestors. Over the Mothers, the vows, the mantras, and likewise the cows, ॥23॥
5.33.24: over the Yakṣas, the Rākṣasas and likewise the kings, and over all beings and Piśācas, he installed Giriśa, the trident-holder. ॥24॥
5.33.25: Himavat over the mountains, the ocean over the rivers, the tiger over the wild beasts, and the bull over the cattle. ॥25॥
5.33.26: He consecrated the banyan to the rule of the forest-lords and trees. Thus kingship everywhere was bestowed in order by the Lord of creatures. ॥26॥
5.33.27: In the eastern quarter the all-souled, pervading lord of the universe installed in kingship the son of Prajāpati Vairāja. ॥27॥
5.33.28: Likewise, O tiger among sages, in the southern quarter he appointed Sudhanvan, the son of Prajāpati Kardama. ॥28॥
5.33.29: In the western quarter likewise the lord appointed as king the great-souled, unfailing Ketumant, son of Rajas. ॥29॥
5.33.30: Likewise he consecrated as king in the northern quarter the invincible Hiraṇyaroman, son of Prajāpati Parjanya. ॥30॥
5.33.31: Its extent has been told, O Śaunaka, together with the account of Pṛthu, son of Vena; that foundation is proclaimed as the Purāṇa, for great prosperity. ॥31॥
5.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The description of the lineage of Kaśyapa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥33॥
5.34.1: Śaunaka said: Recount all the Manvantaras in detail. And however many Manus there are, I wish to hear about them. ॥1॥
5.34.2: Sūta said: Svāyambhuva Manu, then Svārociṣa, likewise Uttama, Tāmasa, Raivata and Cākṣuṣa. ॥2॥
5.34.3: These six Manus have been declared to you, O foremost of sages. Vaivasvata, O best of sages, is said to be the present Manu. ॥3॥
5.34.4: And Sāvarṇi Manu, then Raucya as the next, and likewise Brahmasāvarṇi: these are four Manus. ॥4॥
5.34.5: Likewise Dharmasāvarṇi and Rudrasāvarṇi; Devasāvarṇi is named, and also Indrasāvarṇi. ॥5॥
5.34.6: Those Manus who are past, present and likewise yet to come have all been recounted by me, just as I heard them. ॥6॥
5.34.7: O sage, these fourteen Manvantaras, spanning the three times, have been told to you. A kalpa is constituted as a cycle of a thousand yugas. ॥7॥
5.34.8: I shall tell you of their sages, their sons and likewise their groups of gods. Listen, Śaunaka, with great delight, to those illustrious ones in order. ॥8॥
5.34.9: Marīci, Atri, the revered Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya and Vasiṣṭha: these seven are the sons of Brahmā. ॥9॥
5.34.10: They are likewise the Seven Sages in the northern quarter, O sage; and in the Svāyambhuva period the gods were those named Yāmas. ॥10॥
5.34.11: Āgnīdhra, Agnibāhu, Medhā, Medhātithi, Vasu, Jyotiṣmān, Dhṛtimān, Havya, Savana and Śubhra — ॥11॥
5.34.12: these are declared to be the ten sons of the great-souled Manu Svāyambhuva, O tiger among sages. In that period the Indra is said to be Yajña. ॥12॥
5.34.13: Thus, dear one, the first divine Manvantara has been told. I shall tell you the second; understand it exactly as it is. ॥13॥
5.34.14: Ūrjastambha, Parastambha, Ṛṣabha, Vasumān, Jyotiṣmān, Dyutimān, and Rociṣmān as the seventh — ॥14॥
5.34.15: these are to be known as the great sages; the Indra there was Rocana, and the gods in the Svārociṣa period are remembered as those named Tuṣitas. ॥15॥
5.34.16: Harighna, Sukṛti, Jyoti, Ayomūrti, Ayasmaya, Prathita, Manasyu, Nabha and likewise Sūrya — ॥16॥
5.34.17: these are declared, O tiger among sages, as the ten sons of the great-souled Manu Svārociṣa, of great vigour and valour. ॥17॥
5.34.18: This second Manvantara has been told by me, O sage. I shall tell you the third; understand it exactly as it is. ॥18॥
5.34.19: There were seven sons of Vasiṣṭha, famed as the Vāsiṣṭhas, sons of Hiraṇyagarbha, of great vigour, named the Ūrjas. ॥19॥
5.34.20: These are declared as the sages here. Now learn from me those being recounted: O best of sages, the ten sons of Manu Uttama are remembered as the Auttameyas: ॥20॥
5.34.21: Iṣa, Ūrjita, Ūrja, Madhu, Mādhava, Śuci, Śukravaha, Nabhasa and Nabha — ॥21॥
5.34.22: and Ṛṣabha. The gods there were Satya, Veda, Śruta and others; and the Indra there, lord of the three worlds, was named Satyajit, O sage. ॥22॥
5.34.23: This excellent third Manvantara has been related. I shall tell you the fourth Manvantara, O sage; listen. ॥23॥
5.34.24: Gārgya, Pṛthu, likewise Vāgmī, Jaya, Dhātā, Kapīnaka and Kapīvān are the seven sages; and the Satyas are the groups of gods. ॥24॥
5.34.25: The Indra there is to be known as Triśikha. Hear, O sage, of the sons of Manu: Dyūtipota, Sautapasya, Tapas, Śūla and Tāpana, ॥25॥
5.34.26: Taporati, Akalmāṣa, Dhanvī, Khaḍgī, and the great sage Mahān — these are remembered as the ten sons of Tāmasa, of great vows. ॥26॥
5.34.27: The fourth period, that of Manu Tāmasa, has been told to you by me. Now hear, dear one, the next, the fifth Manvantara. ॥27॥
5.34.28: Devabāhu, Jaya, the sage Vedaśiras, Hiraṇyaromā, Parjanya, Ūrdhvabāhu and Somapa, ॥28॥
5.34.29: and others such as Satyanetra and Rata — these are the other Seven Sages; and the gods were the Bhūtarajasas and likewise the Tapaḥprakṛtis. ॥29॥
5.34.30: The Indra there, lord of the three worlds, was named Vibhu; and the Manu there is to be known as the one called Raivata, the uterine brother of Tāmasa. ॥30॥
5.34.31: Arjuna, Paṅkti, Vindhya and others are the sons of Dayā, O sage; endowed with great austerity, they dwell on the ridge of Meru. ॥31॥
5.34.32: The son of the Prajāpati Ruci is remembered as the Manu named Raucya; and the son begotten by Ruci in the goddess Bhūti became the one named Bhautya. ॥32॥
5.34.33: These seven Manus are remembered as those yet to come in this kalpa; and likewise seven great sages in heaven are remembered as those yet to come. ॥33॥
5.34.34: Kaśyapa, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra, then Gautama, Jamadagni and Bharadvāja — these are remembered as the seven sages of the present period. ॥34॥
5.34.35: Rāma, Vyāsa, likewise Ātreya the radiant and very learned, Bharadvāja, and likewise Drauṇi Aśvatthāmā of great splendour, ॥35॥
5.34.36: and the son of Gautama, Kṛpa Gautama son of Śaradvān; Gālava the Kauśika, Ruru and Kaśyapa — ॥36॥
5.34.37: these seven great-souled ones will be the future best of sages. And there, three groups of future gods have been declared by Svayambhū. ॥37॥
5.34.38: They are the sons of the great-souled Kaśyapa, son of Marīci. Among them, Bali, the son of Virocana, will be Indra. ॥38॥
5.34.39: Viṣāṅga, Avanīvān, Sumanta, Dhṛtimān, Vasu, Sūri, Surākhya, Viṣṇu, and King Sumati — ॥39॥
5.34.40: these will be the ten sons of Manu Sāvarṇi, O Śaunaka. Here the eighth period has been told; now hear the ninth period. ॥40॥
5.34.41: First I shall describe the Manu Dakṣasāvarṇi; listen. Medhātithi of Pulastya's line, Vasu of Kaśyapa's line, ॥41॥
5.34.42: Jyotiṣmān of Bhṛgu's line, Dhṛtimān of Aṅgiras' line, Savana of Vasiṣṭha's line, and Havya of Atri's line, ॥42॥
5.34.43: and Pulaha — these are the seven sages in the Rauhita interval. There, O great sage, the groups of gods are three. ॥43॥
5.34.44: They are the sons of Rohita the Prajāpati, the son of Dakṣa. Dhṛṣṭaketu, Dīptaketu, Pañcahasta, Nirākṛti, ॥44॥
5.34.45: Pṛthuśravas, Bhūridyumna, Ṛcīka, Bṛhata and Gaya — these are the nine mighty sons of the first Sāvarṇi. ॥45॥
5.34.46: Then in the tenth cycle, in the interval of the second Sāvarṇa Manu: Haviṣmān of Pulaha's line, and Prakṛti of Bhṛgu's line, ॥46॥
5.34.47: Āpomukti of Atri's line likewise, Avyaya of Vasiṣṭha's line is recorded, Prayati of Pulastya's line, and Bhāmāra of Kaśyapa's line, ॥47॥
5.34.48: and the truthful Anenas of Aṅgiras' line — these are the seven supreme sages. And the groups of gods are those known as the Dviṣimants. ॥48॥
5.34.49: Their Indra is said to be Śambhu, this very Maheśvara. Akṣatvān, Uttamaujas, and the valiant Bhūriṣeṇa, ॥49॥
5.34.50: Śatānīka, Nirāmitra, Vṛṣasena, Jayadratha, Bhūridyumna, Suvarcas and Arcis — these are the ten sons of the Manu. ॥50॥
5.34.51: In the eleventh cycle, in the interval of the third Sāvarṇa Manu, learn from me his seven sages too as they are named. ॥51॥
5.34.52: Haviṣmān of Kaśyapa's line, Vapuṣmān of Varuṇa's line, then the Ātreya and the Vasiṣṭha, and Anaya of Aṅgiras' line, ॥52॥
5.34.53: Cārudhṛṣya of Pulastya's line, and Niḥsvara, the fiery Agni — these seven are declared the sages; three groups of gods are recorded. ॥53॥
5.34.54: They are the sons of Brahmā; these are known as the Vaidhṛtas. Sarvaga, Suśarman, Devānīka, Kṣemaka, ॥54॥
5.34.55: Dṛḍheṣu, Khaṇḍaka, Darśa, Kuhu and Bāhu are recorded as sons of the Manu; these nine are known as the sons of the third Sāvarṇa. ॥55॥
5.34.56: Learn from me the seven sages of the fourth Sāvarṇi: Dyuti the son of Vasiṣṭha, and Sutapas of Atri's line, ॥56॥
5.34.57: Tapomūrti of Aṅgiras' line, Tapasvin of Kaśyapa's line likewise, Tapodhana of Pulastya's line, and Taporati of Pulaha's line; ॥57॥
5.34.58: the seventh of them should be known as Taponidhi of Bhṛgu's line. Five groups of gods are declared, the mind-born sons of Brahmā. ॥58॥
5.34.59: Ṛtadhāman is their Indra, happily ruling the three worlds. And in the twelfth cycle, in the future interval of Raucya, O sage, ॥59॥
5.34.60: Dhṛtimān of Aṅgiras' line, Havyavān who is of Pulastya's line, Tattvadarśin of Pulaha's line, Nirutsava of Bhṛgu's line, ॥60॥
5.34.61: Niṣprapañca of Atri's line likewise, Nirdeha of Kaśyapa's line, and Sutapas of Vasiṣṭha's line — these are the seven great sages. ॥61॥
5.34.62: Three groups of gods are declared by the Self-born; their Indra is Divaspati. Vicitra and Citra, ॥62॥
5.34.63: Naya, Dharma, Dhṛta, Andhra, Sunetra, Kṣatravṛddhaka, Nirbhaya, Sutapas and Droṇa — these are the sons of the Manu Raucya. ॥63॥
5.34.64: The thirteenth Manu to come will be the self-possessed Devasāvarṇi; Citrasena, Vicitra and others will be the sons born of Devasāvarṇi's body. ॥64॥
5.34.65: The gods will be those called Sukarmans and Sutrāmans, the Indra Divaspati; Nirmoka, Tattvadarśa and others will then be the seers. ॥65॥
5.34.66: In the fourteenth cycle, in the interval of the Manu Bhautya: Āgnīdhra of Kaśyapa's line, and Māgadha who is of Pulastya's line, ॥66॥
5.34.67: Ativāhya of Bhṛgu's line, Śuci of Aṅgiras' line likewise, Yukta of Atri's line, and Śukra of Vasiṣṭha's line, ॥67॥
5.34.68: and Ajita of Pulaha's line — these are the last seven sages. The gods will be the Pavitras and Cākṣuṣas, and Śuci will be Indra. ॥68॥
5.34.69: By people always rising at dawn and reciting the names of these great sages, past and future, happiness increases. ॥69॥
5.34.70: The groups of gods have been declared as five; hear, O great sage the sons: Turaṅgabhīru, Budhna, Tanugra and Anugra, ॥70॥
5.34.71: Atimānin, Pravīṇa, Viṣṇu, Saṅkrandana likewise, Tejasvin and Sabala — these are the sons of the Manu Bhautya. ॥71॥
5.34.72: When the reign of Bhauma is complete, the kalpa is completed. Thus have I described these Manus, future and past. ॥72॥
5.34.73: They were told by Sanatkumāra to Vyāsa of boundless splendour. At the close of a full thousand yugas, having ruled according to their own dharma, ॥73॥
5.34.74: they, together with their subjects and endowed with austerity, go to Brahmā's world. Seventy-one yugas, with something over, is called an interval (manvantara). ॥74॥
5.34.75: These fourteen Manus, increasers of fame, have been described. In all the manvantaras there is rebirth at the end of dissolution. ॥75॥
5.34.76: Their intervals cannot be told even in hundreds of years. When a full hundred thousand is complete, the kalpa is said to be ended. ॥76॥
5.34.77: Then all beings, burnt by the rays of the sun, placing Brahmā at their head, together with the hosts of Ādityas, O sage, ॥77॥
5.34.78: enter, O best of gods, Hari Nārāyaṇa the supreme, the creator of all beings, again and again at the ends of kalpas. ॥78॥
5.34.79: And further, the Lord Rudra is the destroyer, Time itself, at the end of the kalpa. I shall describe that concerning the Manu Vaivasvata. ॥79॥
5.34.80: Thus I have told you everything arising from the manvantaras — the secondary creation, a meritorious, auspicious narrative that increases one's lineage. ॥80॥
5.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The recounting of all the manvantaras, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥34॥
5.35.1: Sūta said: Vivasvān was born from Kaśyapa, the great sage, in Dākṣāyaṇī. His wife was Saṃjñā, the goddess, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, also called Sureṇukā. ॥1॥
5.35.2: O sage, she, endowed with beauty and youth, was not pleased with her husband's form, with that fierce and unbearable brilliance. ॥2॥
5.35.3: Unable to bear that form of Āditya, so intensely brilliant, the fair-complexioned lady, being scorched, then became deeply distressed. ॥3॥
5.35.4: O sage, Bhāskara begot three children in her, in Saṃjñā: first Manu Śrāddhadeva, the Prajāpati; ॥4॥
5.35.5: and Yama and Yamunā were born as twins. Thus three children were born in her from the Sun. ॥5॥
5.35.6: Seeing that spherical form of Vivasvat and being unable to bear it, Saṃjñā then created a lovely shadow (Chāyā) of herself. ॥6॥
5.35.7: That illusory Chāyā spoke devotedly to Saṃjñā: O fair one, what task of yours shall I do here? Tell me, O bright-smiling one. ॥7॥
5.35.8: Saṃjñā said: I shall go to my own father's house—blessings on you. You must truly dwell in this house without any change of conduct. ॥8॥
5.35.9: These two good boys of mine and this slender-waisted girl are to be cared for with all comfort, if you wish to do what pleases me. ॥9॥
5.35.10: Chāyā said: O goddess, up to the point of being seized by the hair I shall bear even grave ill-treatment; I will not disclose your plan. Go as you please, O goddess. ॥10॥
5.35.11: Sūta said: Thus addressed, the goddess went, abashed, into her father's presence. There, rebuked by her father, she was enjoined again and again to return. ॥11॥
5.35.12: Then, concealing her own form and becoming a mare, she went away; reaching the Northern Kurus, she grazed there on grass. ॥12॥
5.35.13: Thinking her to be Saṃjñā, Ravi, the Savitṛ, then begot in Chāyā a fine son, Manu Sāvarṇi, so it is said. ॥13॥
5.35.14: Though requested by Saṃjñā, that Chāyā constantly showed greater affection for her own son, not so for the elder-born sons. ॥14॥
5.35.15: Manu tolerated that of hers, but Yama did not tolerate it; he, angered, both out of childishness and because of the weight of what was destined to be, ॥15॥
5.35.16: Yama, son of Vivasvat, threatened Chāyā with his foot. Then Chāyā, sullied by anger, cursed him in wrath: ॥16॥
5.35.17: May this foot of yours fall off — so she said in great fury. Then Yama, with joined palms, reported everything to his father. ॥17॥
5.35.18: Greatly troubled by fear of the curse and agitated by the words of the false Saṃjñā, he said: A mother should behave with affection towards all her sons. ॥18॥
5.35.19: Withdrawing her affection from us, she cherishes the younger one. Therefore I raised my foot; please be pleased to forgive that. ॥19॥
5.35.20: I have been cursed by my mother, O lord of gods, O best of those who shine. By your grace, O lord of rays, may my foot not fall. ॥20॥
5.35.21: Savitā said: Without doubt, son, there must be a great cause here, by which anger entered you, who know dharma and speak the truth. ॥21॥
5.35.22: That word of your mother cannot be made false. Worms will take flesh from your foot and go to the earth. ॥22॥
5.35.23: Thus her word will come true, and you will be saved. Have no doubt, dear son; console your own mind, O lord. ॥23॥
5.35.24: Sūta said: O lord of sages, having said this to his son named Yama, Sūrya, the Āditya, filled with anger, spoke to that Chāyā: ॥24॥
5.35.25: Sūrya said: O dear one, ill-minded, fierce woman, what is this you have done? And why this excessive affection for one son? You should explain this to me. ॥25॥
5.35.26: Sūta said: Hearing Ravi's words, she told him the truth exactly as it was; and, scorched by fear of the impassioned Sun, she then appeased him. ॥26॥
5.35.27: Hearing her words, Sūrya went to Tvaṣṭṛ and asked him: Where is Saṃjñā? Then Tvaṣṭṛ said to Sūrya: ॥27॥
5.35.28: Tvaṣṭā said: Scorched by your excessive brilliance—this form of yours is not pleasing—and unable to bear it, Saṃjñā lives in a grassy forest. ॥28॥
5.35.29: Praiseworthy and endowed with yogic power, she has taken to yoga, O lord of rays. If you are agreeable, O lord of gods, having given your own consent, ॥29॥
5.35.30: I shall alter your form today and make it lovely. Sūta said: Hearing that, the anger of Mārtaṇḍa Vivasvat subsided. ॥30॥
5.35.31: Setting him upon a lathe, the sage pared down that brilliance. Then the form shone forth, with its brilliance contained. ॥31॥
5.35.32: The form, made more lovely by Tvaṣṭṛ, then shone beautifully. Then, resorting to deep yoga, he saw his own wife, ॥32॥
5.35.33: unassailable by all beings through her brilliance and self-discipline. Taking the form of a horse, he went to her with desire for union, ॥33॥
5.35.34: and as she resisted the union out of suspicion of a strange male, O sage, he deposited that seed through her mouth into her nostrils. ॥34॥
5.35.35: From that were born the two gods, the Aśvins, best of physicians. Those two Aśvins are also known as Nāsatya and Dasra. ॥35॥
5.35.36: Bhāskara then revealed himself to her in his lovely form; seeing him, her husband, she rejoiced and received him with respect. ॥36॥
5.35.37: The virtuous lady, with a joyful face, went with her husband to her own home. Then the couple rejoiced in love more than before. ॥37॥
5.35.38: Yama, his mind greatly pained by that deed, as Dharmarāja delighted these creatures through dharma. ॥38॥
5.35.39: By that deed the greatly radiant Dharmarāja obtained sovereignty over the Pitṛs and the status of a Lokapāla. ॥39॥
5.35.40: Manu Sāvarṇi, rich in austerity, became a Prajāpati; by that deed he is to be the Manu in the future Sāvarṇika manvantara. ॥40॥
5.35.41: On the summit of Meru the lord performs severe austerity even today. And the younger of those two, the glorious maiden Yamī, ॥41॥
5.35.42: she became the best of rivers, the Yamunā, purifier of the worlds. He is called Manu in the world, and is also called Sāvarṇi. ॥42॥
5.35.43: Whoever hears this account of the birth of the gods, or retains it in memory, would be freed when he meets with calamity and would attain very great fame. ॥43॥
5.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of Vaivasvata, in the recounting of the manvantaras, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥35॥
5.36.1: Sūta said: Vaivasvata Manu had nine sons equal to him; later they became greatly eminent, steadfast, and devoted to the dharma of the kṣatriyas. ॥1॥
5.36.2: They were Ikṣvāku, Śibi and Nābhāga, Dhṛṣṭa, and Śaryāti, then Nariṣyanta, Nābhāga, Karūṣa and Priyavrata. ॥2॥
5.36.3: Desiring a son, Manu the Prajāpati performed a sacrifice (iṣṭi) when sons had not yet been born; in that sacrifice, O foremost of sages— ॥3॥
5.36.4: —she, wearing divine garments, adorned with divine ornaments, and of divine form, the renowned Ilā, was born. ॥4॥
5.36.5: Manu, the bearer of the rod of rule, addressed her as Iḍā and said, follow me. Iḍā then replied to him— ॥5॥
5.36.6: with these righteous words to the Prajāpati who desired a son. Iḍā said: I was born from portions of Mitra and Varuṇa, O best of speakers. ॥6॥
5.36.7: I shall go to their presence; let my inclination not be towards adharma. Having spoken thus, that virtuous one then went to Mitra and Varuṇa— ॥7॥
5.36.8: having gone near them, the fair-hipped one, with folded hands, spoke these words: Born from portions of you two at Manu's sacrifice, O great sages, ॥8॥
5.36.9: I have come into your presence; tell me, what shall I do for you two? She had told Manu: Create other sons, O lord; through them your lineage will continue. ॥9॥
5.36.10: Sūta said: To that virtuous Iḍā, born of Manu's sacrifice, who spoke thus, the two sages named Mitra and Varuṇa spoke with respect. ॥10॥
5.36.11: Mitra and Varuṇa said: O knower of dharma, O fair-hipped one, O lovely one, we two are pleased with this modesty, self-restraint and truthfulness of yours. ॥11॥
5.36.12: O greatly fortunate one, you will attain fame as ours, and you yourself will become a son who perpetuates Manu's lineage, ॥12॥
5.36.13: renowned as Sudyumna, famed in the three worlds, dear to the world, righteous in conduct, and the increaser of Manu's lineage. ॥13॥
5.36.14: Sūta said: Having heard that, she turned back; as she was going to her father, Budha, finding an opportunity, invited her to union. ॥14॥
5.36.15: Then from Soma's son was born in her King Purūravas—a very handsome, wise, exalted son, the husband of Urvaśī. ॥15॥
5.36.16: Having lovingly borne the son Purūravas there, she, by Śiva's grace, again became Sudyumna. ॥16॥
5.36.17: Sudyumna had three heirs, supremely righteous: Utkala, Gaya, and the valiant Vinatāśva. ॥17॥
5.36.18: To Utkala belonged the Utkalas, O brahmins; to Vinatāśva the western region; and the eastern quarter, O tiger among sages, is remembered as Gayā, belonging to Gaya. ॥18॥
5.36.19: When Manu, dear one, then entered the body of the Sun, he divided this earth there into ten realms. ॥19॥
5.36.20: Ikṣvāku, the eldest heir, obtained the Middle Country; by Vasiṣṭha's word, Pratiṣṭhāna belonged to the great-souled Sudyumna. ॥20॥
5.36.21: Then Sudyumna, of great fame, having obtained the kingdom, established the righteous rule and later gave that kingdom to Purūravas. ॥21॥
5.36.22: He was the son of Manu, O best of sages, the lord who bore the marks of both woman and man. From Nariṣyanta came the Śakas as sons; to Nabhaga a son was born— ॥22॥
5.36.23: Ambarīṣa; and Bāhleya obtained the Bāhlaka region. Śaryāti had twins: a renowned one named Ānarta, ॥23॥
5.36.24: a son, and a daughter Sukanyā, who became the wife of Cyavana. Ānarta's heir was named Raibhya; he was called Raivata, ॥24॥
5.36.25: whose city in the land of Ānarta was named Kuśasthalī, most divine, which is regarded as the seventh among the seven sacred cities. ॥25॥
5.36.26: He had a hundred sons; Kakudmī was the eldest and best—radiant, very strong, accomplished, most righteous, a protector of brahmins. ॥26॥
5.36.27: To Kakudmī was born a maiden named Revatī, endowed with great loveliness, like a second divine Lakṣmī. ॥27॥
5.36.28: To ask about a husband for the maiden, King Kakudmī, lord of all, went duly with his daughter to Brahmā's world, to the Creator. ॥28॥
5.36.29: While the Gāndharva performance was going on, he waited for a moment to get an opportunity, and there, near Brahmā, he listened to the Gāndharva music during the dancing. ॥29॥
5.36.30: Then, in that time, many yugas passed as if a mere muhūrta, but King Kakudmī, O sages, noticed nothing. ॥30॥
5.36.31: Then, bowing to the Creator with folded hands, he of humble mind made known his intention to Brahmā, the Supreme Self. ॥31॥
5.36.32: Having heard his intention, Prajāpati laughed, addressed the great king Kakudmī, and said: ॥32॥
5.36.33: Brahmā said: Listen, O king, son of Raibhya, Kakudmī, lord of the earth: out of affection I shall tell you my words truly and in detail. ॥33॥
5.36.34: Those suitors whom you had in mind have been carried away by Time; their lineage no longer exists there—Time devours all. ॥34॥
5.36.35: Even your city, O king, was destroyed by the Puṇyajana rākṣasas; now, in the twenty-eighth Dvāpara, it has been rebuilt by Kṛṣṇa, ॥35॥
5.36.36: made into a city named Dvārāvatī, many-gated and charming, guarded by the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas led by Vāsudeva. ॥36॥
5.36.37: So go there with a glad heart, O king, and give this maiden, your own daughter, to Baladeva, the son of Vasudeva. ॥37॥
5.36.38: Sūta said: Thus instructed, the king bowed to him and went to that city with his daughter, amazed on learning that many yugas had passed. ॥38॥
5.36.39: Then there he promptly gave that young maiden, his own Revatī, with due rites, to Bala, the brother of Kṛṣṇa. ॥39॥
5.36.40: Then the great lord went to the divine peak of Meru; there that king, established in austerity, worshipped Śiva. ॥40॥
5.36.41: The sages said: That Revata stayed there in Brahmaloka for many yugas, yet he came back to the mortal world still young. This is our great doubt. ॥41॥
5.36.42: Sūta said: There, indeed, there is no old age, hunger or thirst, nor any changes of the body. Near Brahmā, O sages, there is no untimely death for anyone. ॥42॥
5.36.43: Therefore the king did not undergo old age or death, nor did that daughter. Having taken counsel there about the best groom, he came back still young. ॥43॥
5.36.44: Having gone to the divine city Dvārāvatī, built by Kṛṣṇa, he had his daughter married to Balarāma. ॥44॥
5.36.45: That righteous great lord Balarāma had a hundred sons; and to Kṛṣṇa too countless sons were born from his many wives. ॥45॥
5.36.46: There the lineage of both great souls became vast; the kṣatriyas of it, joyful and very righteous, spread into all directions. ॥46॥
5.36.47: Thus the lineage of Śaryāti has been told. Now I shall speak briefly of the other descendants of Manu; listen attentively, O twice-born. ॥47॥
5.36.48: Nābhāga was the son of Diṣṭa; but he attained brahminhood, having established his own kṣatriya lineage and devoted himself to brahminical rites. ॥48॥
5.36.49: From Dhṛṣṭa arose the Dhārṣṭa kṣatriya clan, which attained brahminhood on earth. From Karūṣa came the Kārūṣas, kṣatriyas fierce in battle. ॥49॥
5.36.50: Nṛga, who was a son of Manu, was an especially great giver, gladly bestowing various riches and also cows upon brahmins. ॥50॥
5.36.51: Because of an error in a gift of cows, through his own poor judgment and his own sin, he fell into the state of a lizard, and was rescued by Śrī Kṛṣṇa. ॥51॥
5.36.52: He had one excellent son, Prayāti, a knower of dharma. Thus have I heard from Vyāsa, and it has been told briefly. ॥52॥
5.36.53: Vṛṣaghna, a son of Manu, was made a cowherd by his preceptor; he guarded the cows vigilantly, keeping at night the vow of the hero's posture (vīrāsana). ॥53॥
5.36.54: Once, hearing the cows crying out, the strong one, awake, perceived that a tiger had come into the cowpen to kill the cows, and went, sword in hand, to slay it. ॥54॥
5.36.55: Unknowingly, suspecting it to be the tiger, he struck off the head of a tawny cow. The tiger, frightened at seeing that lord with his sword, ran out. ॥55॥
5.36.56: Believing the tiger slain, he went back to his own place, confused in that night, his judgment ruined by the rain and wind. ॥56॥
5.36.57: When the night had dawned, he rose early and went there; he saw the tawny cow slain, not the tiger, and was grieved. ॥57॥
5.36.58: Hearing of that incident and understanding it, the preceptor, though considering that it was unintentional, cursed the offender: Become a śūdra, not a kṣatriya. ॥58॥
5.36.59: Thus cursed in anger by his preceptor, the family teacher, Pṛṣadhra departed and went into the great forest. ॥59॥
5.36.60: Despondent through hardship, he became detached and devoted to yoga; his body burnt in a forest fire, he reached the supreme goal. ॥60॥
5.36.61: Kavi, the wise son of Manu, by the grace of Śiva enjoyed divine happiness here and attained liberation, which is very hard to obtain. ॥61॥
5.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the lineages of the nine sons of Manu, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥36॥
5.37.1: Sūta said: From Manu, long ago, was born a son, Ikṣvāku, from his nostril. That Ikṣvāku had a hundred sons, all givers of abundant sacrificial fees. ॥1॥
5.37.2: Of them, some became kings in the east in Āryāvarta, O twice-born ones. Among them Vikukṣi was the eldest; he became king in Ayodhyā. ॥2॥
5.37.3: Hear with interest that deed of his which took place in the lineage sprung from Vidhi (Brahmā). Having been assigned to fetch meat for the śrāddha rite, while the śrāddha rite had not yet been performed, ॥3॥
5.37.4: he hastily ate a hare, and hence came to be called Śaśāda ('hare-eater'). Abandoned by Ikṣvāku, Śaśāda entered the forest. ॥4॥
5.37.5: When Ikṣvāku had passed away, he became king by Vasiṣṭha's word. His sons, headed by Śakuni, are remembered as fifteen, ॥5॥
5.37.6: kings who were protectors of the northern region. The heir of Ayodha was the valiant one named Kakutstha. ॥6॥
5.37.7: Kakutstha's son was Arinābha; his son was Pṛthu. Pṛthu's son was Viṣṭarāśva, and from him came Indra, a lord of the people. ॥7॥
5.37.8: Indra's son was Yuvanāśva; his son was Śrāva, a lord of the people. From him was born the wise Śrāvastaka, by whom Śrāvastī was built. The heir of Śrāvasta was the greatly renowned Bṛhadaśva. ॥8॥
5.37.9: His son was Yuvanāśva, and Kuvalāśva was his son. He, the best of kings, became known as Dhundhumāra from slaying Dhundhu. ॥9॥
5.37.10: Kuvalāśva had a hundred sons, excellent archers. Then the father appointed Kuvalāśva to the kingship. ॥10॥
5.37.11: The king, having transferred his royal fortune to his son, set out for the forest. Then Uttaṅka stopped that royal sage as he was departing. ॥11॥
5.37.12: Uttaṅka said: Listen: the protection of the earth according to dharma is to be carried out by you. For, O king, the earth, being protected by you, the great-souled one, ॥12॥
5.37.13: will be free from distress; you should not go to the forest. Near my hermitage, in the level desert lands, ॥13॥
5.37.14: in a place filled with sea-sand, there is a Dānava proud of his strength, huge-bodied and mighty, who cannot be slain by the gods. ॥14॥
5.37.15: Having gone beneath the ground, he lies there hidden within the sand — the son of the Rākṣasa Madhu, named Dhundhu, exceedingly terrible. ॥15॥
5.37.16: He lies there for the destruction of the worlds, having undertaken fierce austerity. At the end of each year he releases his breath. ॥16॥
5.37.17: Whenever he does so, the earth shakes with its mountains, woods and forests; his breath is full of sparks, embers and smoke, exceedingly dreadful. ॥17॥
5.37.18: Because of that, O king, I cannot stay in that hermitage of mine. Kill him, O mighty-armed one, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. ॥18॥
5.37.19: Let the worlds be at ease today, once he is slain by you. For you alone, O lord of the earth, are capable of killing him. ॥19॥
5.37.20: And a boon was granted to me by Viṣṇu in a former age, O sinless one: Viṣṇu will augment your energy with his own energy. ॥20॥
5.37.21: For great dharma is seen here in protecting the people; it is not seen in the same way in the forest. Do not let such an idea be yours. ॥21॥
5.37.22: For nowhere, O king of kings, is there dharma such as that which was practised of old by royal sages in protecting the people. ॥22॥
5.37.23: The royal sage, thus addressed by the great-souled Uttaṅka, gave him his son Kuvalāśva for the subduing of Dhundhu, ॥23॥
5.37.24: saying: O revered one, I have laid down my weapons; but this son of mine, O best of brahmins, will be the slayer of Dhundhu, no doubt. ॥24॥
5.37.25: Having said this and instructed his son, the king went off for austerity; and Kuvalāśva, together with Uttaṅka, went to subdue Dhundhu. ॥25॥
5.37.26: Then the lord, the blessed Viṣṇu, entered him with his energy, at Uttaṅka's behest, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. ॥26॥
5.37.27: When that invincible one set out, a great voice arose in heaven: This glorious prince will be Dhundhumāra. ॥27॥
5.37.28: The gods covered him all around with heavenly garlands, and praised him, crying, Victory! Long life! ॥28॥
5.37.29: Having gone there, that king, best of victors, together with his sons had the sand-ocean dug up from its middle. ॥29॥
5.37.30: Invigorated by the energy of Nārāyaṇa and of the brahmin sage, he became exceedingly brilliant and still more endowed with strength. ॥30॥
5.37.31: As his sons dug, O brahmin, Dhundhu, who lay within the sand, was reached, resting toward the western direction. ॥31॥
5.37.32: In his rage, as if consuming the worlds with the fire born from his mouth, he poured forth water with force, like the ocean at the rising of the moon. ॥32॥
5.37.33: Then that group of a hundred sons, struck by the fires, was burnt; only three among them remained, O lord of sages. ॥33॥
5.37.34: Then, O chief of brahmins, that greatly brilliant king attacked that mighty Rākṣasa Dhundhu, the destroyer of brahmins. ॥34॥
5.37.35: Drinking up his watery torrent, that ruler of men struck with a fire-arrow, and quenched the fire with water. ॥35॥
5.37.36: Having slain by his might that huge-bodied water-Rākṣasa, the ruler of men showed Uttaṅka the deed accomplished. ॥36॥
5.37.37: Uttaṅka then granted a boon to that king, O great sage: he gave him inexhaustible wealth and invincibility by enemies, ॥37॥
5.37.38: a mind ever set on dharma, and likewise an imperishable dwelling in heaven; and an imperishable world for his sons who had been slain by the Rākṣasa. ॥38॥
5.37.39: Of his three surviving sons, Dṛḍhāśva is called the eldest; and Haṃsāśva and Kapilāśva were the two princes younger than him. ॥39॥
5.37.40: Dṛḍhāśva, the son of Dhundhumāra — his son was Haryaśva; and Haryaśva's son was Nikumbha, ever devoted to dharma. ॥40॥
5.37.41: Saṃhatāśva, skilled in battle, was the son of Nikumbha. Akṣāśva and Kṛtāśva were the two sons of Saṃhatāśva, O brahmins. ॥41॥
5.37.42: His wife was Haimavatī, Dṛṣadvatī, honoured by the virtuous and famed in the three worlds; her son was Prasenajit. ॥42॥
5.37.43: Prasenajit obtained a devoted wife named Gaurī; but she, cursed by her husband, was turned into the river Bāhudā. ॥43॥
5.37.44: His son was the great king Yuvanāśva. Yuvanāśva's son was Māndhātā, renowned in the three worlds. ॥44॥
5.37.45: His wife was Caitrarathī, daughter of Śaśabindu; she was devoted to her husband and the eldest among ten thousand brothers. ॥45॥
5.37.46: Then Māndhātā begot on her two sons: Purukutsa, knower of dharma, and the righteous Mucukunda. ॥46॥
5.37.47: Purukutsa's son was the learned and wise Trayyāruṇi. His son was a very mighty prince named Satyavrata. ॥47॥
5.37.48: He obstructed the marriage mantras being recited by noble persons, he by whom formerly the bride of another was carried off while his wedding was being performed. ॥48॥
5.37.49: When, out of force, lust, delusion and intense excitement, he carried off, from desire, the maiden of a certain citizen, ॥49॥
5.37.50: King Trayyāruṇi, filled with anger, renouncing him who clung to unrighteousness, said again and again, begone. ॥50॥
5.37.51: Then the wicked one said to his father: Where shall I go? The king then told him: Live near the dog-eaters (śvapākas). ॥51॥
5.37.52: So that hero Satyavrata, abandoned by his father, the dharma-protecting king, lived near the dwellings of the dog-eaters. ॥52॥
5.37.53: Then King Trayyāruṇi, disgusted by his son's deed, abandoned everything and went to the forest to perform austerities to Śaṅkara. ॥53॥
5.37.54: Then, because of that unrighteousness, Indra (Pākaśāsana) did not rain in his realm for twelve years, O brahmin sage. ॥54॥
5.37.55: In his realm, the great ascetic Viśvāmitra, leaving his wife behind, practised vast austerity in the marshy land by the sea. ॥55॥
5.37.56: His wife, binding a rope round the neck of her middle son, born of her own husband, sold him for a hundred cows to sustain the rest. ॥56॥
5.37.57: Seeing her selling her own son, bound at the neck, the righteous one then had that son of the great sage released. ॥57॥
5.37.58: The mighty-armed Satyavrata maintained him, to please Viśvāmitra and out of compassion. ॥58॥
5.37.59: From then on, that son of the sage Viśvāmitra became known as Gālava, a great ascetic, because of the binding of his neck (gala-bandha). ॥59॥
5.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the lineage of Manu, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥37॥
5.38.1: Sūta said: Satyavrata, out of devotion to him (Viśvāmitra), out of compassion, and because of his vow, then indeed supported Viśvāmitra's wife and family. ॥1॥
5.38.2: Having killed deer, boars, buffaloes and other forest-roaming animals, he would throw their meat near Viśvāmitra's hermitage, O sage. ॥2॥
5.38.3: The sage Vasiṣṭha, owing to the bond between sacrificer and family priest, protected the sacred places, the cows, the king's person and likewise the inner palace. ॥3॥
5.38.4: Whether because of Satyavrata's words or by the force of what was destined to be, Vasiṣṭha constantly held ever greater anger towards him. ॥4॥
5.38.5: When he, the king's own son, was then banished from the kingdom by his father, the sage Vasiṣṭha did not prevent it, and for a reason. ॥5॥
5.38.6: The completion of the marriage mantras takes place at the seventh step; and Satyavrata did not understand that secret intention of his. ॥6॥
5.38.7: In that matter he, Vasiṣṭha, acted for the satisfaction of the great-souled father, thinking, this would be an atonement made for the family, O brahmin. ॥7॥
5.38.8: The blessed Vasiṣṭha did not restrain him when he was abandoned by his father; nor did the sage say, I shall consecrate his son. ॥8॥
5.38.9: That strong one kept that vow for twelve years. Once, when there was no meat to be had, ... ॥9॥
5.38.10: ... that prince saw the milch cow of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha that yields all desires. Then, out of anger, greed and weariness, and overcome by hunger, ... ॥10॥
5.38.11: ... the king, following the conduct of the Dāśas, killed her, O sage. He himself ate that meat and gave it to Viśvāmitra's son ... ॥11॥
5.38.12: ... he fed. Hearing that, Vasiṣṭha became angry with him, and the best of sages, filled with wrath, then said to him: ॥12॥
5.38.13: Vasiṣṭha said: O cruel one, I would without doubt bring down a spike (śaṅku) upon you, if these two spikes had not already been made by you before. ॥13॥
5.38.14: By your father's displeasure, by killing your preceptor's milch cow, and by using meat not consecrated with sprinkling — threefold is your transgression. ॥14॥
5.38.15: He called him Triśaṅku, and thus he is remembered as Triśaṅku. Viśvāmitra, for his part, returned after the maintenance of his wife and family had been accomplished. ॥15॥
5.38.16: For that reason the sage, pleased, granted a boon to Triśaṅku; and being offered a boon, the prince chose his boon. ॥16॥
5.38.17: When this fear of a twelve-year drought had arisen, the sage installed him in his father's kingdom and had him perform a sacrifice. ॥17॥
5.38.18: Then, while the gods and Vasiṣṭha looked on, the mighty Kauśika raised him to heaven in his body. ॥18॥
5.38.19: His wife, named Satyarathā, born of the Kekaya lineage, bore a son, the sinless Hariścandra. ॥19॥
5.38.20: That king Hariścandra is remembered as Traiśaṅkava (son of Triśaṅku); as the performer of the Rājasūya he is famed as an emperor. ॥20॥
5.38.21: Hariścandra's son was the famous one named Rohita; Rohita's son was Vṛka, and from Vṛka Bāhu was born. ॥21॥
5.38.22: The Haihayas and Tālajaṅghas drove out that king. He was not very righteous, O brahmins, though he lived in the age of dharma. ॥22॥
5.38.23: Bāhu begot a son, Sagara, who was born together with poison (gara), after his mother reached Aurva's hermitage and was protected by the Bhārgava. ॥23॥
5.38.24: Having obtained the fire-missile (āgneya) from the Bhārgava, King Sagara conquered the earth, slaying the Tālajaṅghas and the Haihayas. ॥24॥
5.38.25: Subduing the Śakas, the Bahūdakas, the Pāradas with their hosts, and the Khaśas, he established true dharma and ruled the earth righteously. ॥25॥
5.38.26: Śaunaka said: How was he born of a kṣatriya together with poison, and how did he conquer? Tell this in detail, O son of Sūta. ॥26॥
5.38.27: Sūta said: What Vaiśampāyana related when asked by Pārīkṣita (Janamejaya) — that I shall tell; listen with an undivided mind, O sage. ॥27॥
5.38.28: The son of Parīkṣit said: O sage, how was that King Sagara born together with poison, and how did he slay the kings? You should relate this. ॥28॥
5.38.29: Vaiśampāyana said: The kingdom of Bāhu, who was given to vices, was seized, it is said, my dear, by the Haihayas and Tālajaṅghas together with the Śakas, O lord of the people. ॥29॥
5.38.30: The Yavanas, the Pāradas, the Kāmbojas, the Pāhlavas and the Bahūdakas — these five are declared to be the hosts of the rākṣasas. ॥30॥
5.38.31: These five hosts of the rākṣasas, O king, displaying their valour on behalf of the Haihayas, forcibly gave them the kingdom taken from Bāhu. ॥31॥
5.38.32: Then King Bāhu, his kingdom taken, went to the forest; followed by his wife and grief-stricken, he gave up his life. ॥32॥
5.38.33: His wife, a Yādava princess, who was pregnant, had followed behind him; and poison had been given to her by her co-wife out of jealousy over her bearing the first son. ॥33॥
5.38.34: She, having prepared her husband's pyre, was ascending the fire; but Aurva the Bhārgava, O king, out of compassion restrained her. ॥34॥
5.38.35: Dwelling in his hermitage for the protection of the embryo, the queen served that best of sages, remembering Śaṅkara in her heart. ॥35॥
5.38.36: One day her embryo indeed came forth together with the poison, at an auspicious hour and under an auspicious ascendant, joined with five exalted planets. ॥36॥
5.38.37: And with that ascendant strong in every way, O best of sages, the mighty-armed king named Sagara was born. ॥37॥
5.38.38: Aurva performed the birth ceremony and other rites for that great soul, taught him the Vedas and śāstras, and then bestowed the missile on him. ॥38॥
5.38.39: That fiery missile, hard to withstand even for the immortals, the greatly fortunate Sagara, best of kings, received with joy according to due rite. ॥39॥
5.38.40: Endowed with the power of that missile and with his own strength, he, enraged, swiftly slew the Haihayas by the might of the missile. ॥40॥
5.38.41: And that Sagara, the foremost of the famous, won fame throughout the worlds and established dharma on the surface of the earth. ॥41॥
5.38.42: Then the Śakas, together with the Yavanas, the Kāmbojas and likewise the Pāhlavas, being slain at that time, went to Vasiṣṭha for refuge. ॥42॥
5.38.43: The greatly radiant Vasiṣṭha, having made a stratagem by means of an agreement and having given them assurance of safety, restrained King Sagara. ॥43॥
5.38.44: Sagara, mindful of his own vow and having heard his preceptor's word, destroyed their dharma and made them alter the style of their hair. ॥44॥
5.38.45: Having shaved half the head of the Śakas, he let them go; he shaved the whole head of the Yavanas, and likewise of the Kāmbojas. ॥45॥
5.38.46: The Pāradas were made shaven-haired and the Pāhnavas bearers of beards; all of them were made by that great-souled one devoid of Vedic recitation and the vaṣaṭ-call. ॥46॥
5.38.47: And the whole earth was conquered righteously by that king; all those kṣatriyas, dear one, were thus made devoid of dharma in former times. ॥47॥
5.38.48: That king, victorious through dharma, having conquered this earth, the ruler had a horse consecrated for the horse-sacrifice. ॥48॥
5.38.49: While he was letting it roam, that horse went to the south-eastern ocean, accompanied by his sixty thousand sons, O sage. ॥49॥
5.38.50: That horse was stolen near the seashore by Śakra, king of the gods, who was pursuing his own interest, and was made to enter the earth. ॥50॥
5.38.51: Then the great king Sagara, to search for that horse, had that region dug up on all sides by his sons. ॥51॥
5.38.52: Then, as the great ocean was being dug there, they came upon that primeval Person, the god Kapila, whose form is the universe. ॥52॥
5.38.53: By the fire that arose from his eyes as he awoke, the sixty thousand were burnt; only four were left. ॥53॥
5.38.54: Harṣaketu, Suketu, likewise another, Dharmaratha, and the valiant Pañcajana — these were the kings who continued his lineage. ॥54॥
5.38.55: And the blessed Hari himself gave him five boons: lineage, intelligence, fame, the ocean as a son, and wealth. ॥55॥
5.38.56: And through that deed of his, the ocean obtained the status of Sāgara; and he recovered that sacrificial horse from the ocean. ॥56॥
5.38.57: That greatly renowned one performed a hundred horse-sacrifices; and there he worshipped the manifestations of Śambhu and the deities, he and the priests being of good vows. ॥57॥
5.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of the lineage from Satyavrata to Sagara, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥38॥
5.39.1: Śaunaka said: How were the sons of Sagara born, heroic, mighty, valourous, sixty thousand in number? Or by what means? Tell me. ॥1॥
5.39.2: Sūta said: Sagara had two wives whose sins had been burnt away by austerity. Aurva, the best of sages, being pleased, granted the two of them a boon. ॥2॥
5.39.3: One chose sixty thousand sons of great vigour; the other, endowed with the boon, chose as she wished a single son to perpetuate the line. ॥3॥
5.39.4: Having come there, and having then obtained those many brave sons, she gave birth to a gourd full of seeds, which was divided apart. ॥4॥
5.39.5: All those boys, increasers of delight, grew up in due order in pots filled with ghee, tended by their own nurses. ॥5॥
5.39.6: Of those great-souled ones, who were burnt there by the fire of Kapila, one son named Pañcajana became king. ॥6॥
5.39.7: Then Pañcajana had a son named Aṃśumān, full of valour. His son was Dilīpa, whose son was Bhagīratha, ॥7॥
5.39.8: the lord who brought down Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, led her to the ocean, and regarded her as his daughter. ॥8॥
5.39.9: Bhagīratha's son was the king known as Śrutasena; his son was Nābhāga, a son supremely righteous. ॥9॥
5.39.10: Ambarīṣa was the son of Nābhāga; from him came Sindhudvīpa. The valourous Ayutājit was the heir of Sindhudvīpa. ॥10॥
5.39.11: Ayutājit's son was Ṛtuparṇa of great fame. He knew the secret of divine dice, and that king became the friend of Nala. ॥11॥
5.39.12: Ṛtuparṇa's son was Anuparṇa of great splendour; his son was Kalmāṣapāda, also called by name Mitrasaha. ॥12॥
5.39.13: Kalmāṣapāda's son was renowned as Sarvakarman; and the renowned Anaraṇya was the son of Sarvaśarman. ॥13॥
5.39.14: Anaraṇya's son was the learned king Muṇḍidruha; his son was Niṣadha, and then Rati, also called Khaṭvāṅga, ॥14॥
5.39.15: by whom, having come here from heaven and obtained life for only a muhūrta, all three worlds were won through wisdom and truth, O sinless one. ॥15॥
5.39.16: His son was Dīrghabāhu; Raghu was his son. Aja was his son, and from him came Daśaratha. ॥16॥
5.39.17: From Daśaratha was born Rāma, righteous-souled and of great fame — he, a portion of Viṣṇu and a great devotee of Śiva, by whom the descendant of Pulastya Rāvaṇa was slain. ॥17॥
5.39.18: His story has been described in many ways in the Purāṇas and is well known in the Rāmāyaṇa; therefore it is not told here in detail. ॥18॥
5.39.19: To Rāma was born a son, renowned as Kuśa. From Kuśa was born Atithi, and his son was Niṣadha. ॥19॥
5.39.20: Niṣadha's son was Nala, and Nala's son was Nabha. From Nabha came Puṇḍarīka, and after him Kṣemadhanvā is remembered. ॥20॥
5.39.21: Kṣemadhanvā's son was the powerful Devānīka; Devānīka's son was the lord named Ahīnagu. ॥21॥
5.39.22: Ahīnagu's heir was the valourous one named Sahasvān; his son was Vīrasena, who was born in the Ikṣvāku lineage. ॥22॥
5.39.23: Vīrasena's heir was Pāriyātra; then came a son named Bala, and from him was born a son, Sthala. ॥23॥
5.39.24: From him came a son, the powerful Yakṣa, born of a portion of the Sun. His son was Aguṇa, and from him came a son, Vidhṛti. ॥24॥
5.39.25: His son Hiraṇyanābha became a teacher of yoga; he was a disciple of the sage Jaimini, skilled in the knowledge of the Self. ॥25॥
5.39.26: From that best of kings Kauśalya Yājñavalkya then learned the yoga called adhyātma, which cleaves the knot of the heart. ॥26॥
5.39.27: His son was named Puṣya; his son was called Dhruva; his son was Agnivarṇa, and after him a son named Śīghra. ॥27॥
5.39.28: His son, named Maru, became perfected in yoga; that lord dwells even today in the place called Kalāpa village. ॥28॥
5.39.29: At the end of the Kali age, together with the sages dwelling there, he himself will restore the vanished Solar dynasty in particular. ॥29॥
5.39.30: His son was Pṛthuśruta; his son is remembered as Sandhi; his son was Amarṣaṇa, and his son was Marutvān. ॥30॥
5.39.31: His son was Viśvasāhva; his son was Prasenajit; his son was Takṣaka, and his son was Bṛhadbala. ॥31॥
5.39.32: These past kings of the Ikṣvāku dynasty have been fully recounted. Now hear of the future kings of that line, most knowing in dharma. ॥32॥
5.39.33: Bṛhadbala's son will be Bṛhadraṇa; the son of Bṛhadraṇa will be Urukriya. ॥33॥
5.39.34: His son will be Vatsavṛddha; after him the son Prativyomā; his son will be Bhānu, then Divāka, a commander of armies. ॥34॥
5.39.35: His son will be Sahadeva, a great hero; his son Bṛhadaśva; and his son the mighty Bhānumān. ॥35॥
5.39.36: Bhānumān's son will be the valourous Pratīkāśva; his son will be Supratīka, the best of kings. ॥36॥
5.39.37: His son will be Marudeva; then Sunakṣatra will be; his son Puṣkara; and his son Antarikṣa, O brāhmaṇas. ॥37॥
5.39.38: His son will be the heroic Sutapas; and after him the son of Mitracitta, Bṛhadbhāja; and his son is named Barhi. ॥38॥
5.39.39: His son will be Kṛtañjaya, and his son Raṇañjaya; then Sañjaya, and his son Maya; and his son Śākya. ॥39॥
5.39.40: His son will be Śuddhoda; his son Lāṅgala; his son Prasenajit; and his son the one called Śūdraka. ॥40॥
5.39.41: Ruṇaka will be his son; Suratha is remembered as his son. Sumitra will be his son, who is indeed the very end of the lineage's continuance. ॥41॥
5.39.42: This lineage of the Ikṣvākus — of kings of wondrous valour, most righteous and of good deeds — will indeed end with Sumitra. ॥42॥
5.39.43: Having reached Sumitra as its king, that auspicious lineage will come to its end in the Kali age; then, in the Kṛta age of the brāhma order, it will flourish again. ॥43॥
5.39.44: Thus, in the Vaivasvata lineage, the kings born of the Ikṣvāku line, givers of abundant sacrificial gifts, have been proclaimed according to their prominence. ॥44॥
5.39.45: This supremely meritorious creation line is that of Āditya Vivasvat and of the god Śrāddhadeva, the bestower of prosperity on creatures. ॥45॥
5.39.46: A man who reads or hears this creation line of Āditya, blessed with offspring and having enjoyed supreme happiness here, attains union (sāyujya) with the deity. ॥46॥
5.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the kings born in the lineage of Vaivasvata, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥39॥
5.40.1: Vyāsa said: Having heard thus the unsurpassed account of the lineage of the Sun, Śrāddhadeva, Śaunaka, the best of sages, respectfully questioned Sūta. ॥1॥
5.40.2: Śaunaka said: O Sūta, O Sūta, may you live long, disciple of Vyāsa; salutation to you. You have made us hear a supreme, divine and supremely purifying story. ॥2॥
5.40.3: You have spoken of the Sun as Śrāddhadeva, the increaser of the noble lineage. A doubt has arisen in me about that; I state it before you. ॥3॥
5.40.4: From what cause indeed does Vivasvat, the Āditya, have the status of Śrāddhadeva? I wish to hear that with delight; cut away this doubt of mine. ॥4॥
5.40.5: And tell me also, O lord, the greatness of the śrāddha and its fruit, by which the ancestors, being pleased, join him the performer with welfare. ॥5॥
5.40.6: And I wish to hear this too: the excellent creation of the Pitṛs. Narrate it in detail; show compassion, O greatly wise one. ॥6॥
5.40.7: Sūta said: I shall gladly tell you all of it, the creation of the Pitṛs, O Śaunaka, as it was narrated by Mārkaṇḍeya to Bhīṣma when he inquired. ॥7॥
5.40.8: It was sung by Sanatkumāra to the wise Mārkaṇḍeya; I shall declare it to you, a teaching that bestows the fruit of all desires. ॥8॥
5.40.9: Questioned by Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma, the best of upholders of dharma, lying on the bed of arrows, spoke; hear that, I tell it to you. ॥9॥
5.40.10: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How indeed is prosperity obtained among men by one who desires prosperity? I wish to hear this: doing what does one not come to grief? ॥10॥
5.40.11: Sūta said: Having heard the question put by Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma, the knower of dharma, spoke these words with great delight while all were listening. ॥11॥
5.40.12: Bhīṣma said: O Yudhiṣṭhira, those men who perform śrāddhas with devotion — through the śrāddhas each gratifies all of that, by the grace of the Pitṛs. ॥12॥
5.40.13: Men desiring fruits always perform śrāddhas, intending them for the father and likewise for the father's father, ॥13॥
5.40.14: and the father's grandfather, always in the three piṇḍas. The Pitṛs grant dharma to one desiring dharma, and progeny to one desiring progeny, ॥14॥
5.40.15: and prosperity to one desiring prosperity they grant, O Yudhiṣṭhira. ॥15॥
5.40.16: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The ancestors of some dwell in heaven, of others again in hell; and the fruit born of action is said to be fixed for living beings. ॥16॥
5.40.17: How do those śrāddhas, once offered, reach the ancestors? And how are those who dwell in hell able to obtain that fruit? ॥17॥
5.40.18: I have heard that even the gods in heaven worship the Pitṛs. I wish to hear this; tell me in detail. ॥18॥
5.40.19: Bhīṣma said: Here I shall recount to you, as I heard it, O subduer of foes, what was sung long ago by my father after he had gone to the other world. ॥19॥
5.40.20: At the time of my father's śrāddha, I held up the piṇḍa; my father, breaking through the ground, asked to receive it from my hand. ॥20॥
5.40.21: But I, concluding, this is not the rule seen in the ritual code, then gave the piṇḍa on the kuśa grass itself, without wavering. ॥21॥
5.40.22: Then my father, satisfied and pleased with me, spoke in a sweet voice, O best of the Bharatas, O sinless one: ॥22॥
5.40.23: Through you, a wise knower of dharma, I truly have an heir; I have been saved. The test was made by me, O best of men. ॥23॥
5.40.24: Whatever standard a king sets by his righteous conduct, the subjects always follow that, the conduct set as a standard. ॥24॥
5.40.25: Hear, O best of the Bharatas, the eternal Vedic duties. The standard of Vedic dharma has been upheld by you, my son. ॥25॥
5.40.26: Therefore, greatly pleased with you, I lovingly give you an unsurpassed boon, hard to obtain in the three worlds; accept it. ॥26॥
5.40.27: Death shall have no power over you as long as you wish to live; only after receiving permission from you will death prevail. ॥27॥
5.40.28: Or what other excellent boon that you desire shall I give you further? Tell me, O best of the Bharatas, what is in your mind. ॥28॥
5.40.29: When he had spoken thus, I saluted him with joined palms and said: I am fulfilled, since you are pleased, O giver of honour. I ask a certain question; let it be answered by you yourself. ॥29॥
5.40.30: He said to me: Speak it; if you wish, I shall tell you. Thus addressed, I asked him there, and the king, being asked, explained it. ॥30॥
5.40.31: Śantanu said: Hear, dear son; I shall answer your question truly, and tell the whole Pitṛkalpa, which I heard from Mārkaṇḍeya. ॥31॥
5.40.32: What you ask me, dear one, that very thing I asked the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya, and he, the knower of dharma, told me. ॥32॥
5.40.33: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Hear, O king: once, as I was gazing at the sky, I saw a great aerial chariot coming then near the mountain. ॥33॥
5.40.34: In that aerial chariot I saw a couch with the lustre of blazing embers, of great radiance, glowing, uniform and charming. ॥34॥
5.40.35: And there I saw, lying, a person of blazing splendour, the size of a thumb, like fire placed within fire. ॥35॥
5.40.36: I, having offered salutation to him and bowed my head to the lord, asked him: How may we know you, O mighty one? ॥36॥
5.40.37: That righteous one said to me: You do not possess that austerity by which you could know me, O sage, the son of Brahmā. ॥37॥
5.40.38: Know me as Sanatkumāra; what shall I do for you? The other sons of Brahmā are younger than I, ॥38॥
5.40.39: seven invincible brothers whose lineages are established. But we follow the ascetic's dharma, having restrained the self within the self. ॥39॥
5.40.40: As I was born, so I have remained; I am known as Kumāra. Therefore this name of mine, Sanatkumāra, has been declared, O sage. ॥40॥
5.40.41: Because, with devotion, you have performed austerities out of a longing to see me, here I am, seen by you. May good befall you. What wish of yours shall I fulfil? ॥41॥
5.40.42: To him who had spoken thus I said: Listen, O Lord, and narrate to me exactly as it happened the original creation of the Pitṛs. ॥42॥
5.40.43: Thus addressed, he said to me: Listen to all of it as it truly is. I shall tell you faithfully, dear child, the auspicious creation of the Pitṛs. ॥43॥
5.40.44: Sanatkumāra said: Long ago Brahmā created the gods and said to them: Worship me. But, setting him aside, they, eager for rewards, worshipped their own selves. ॥44॥
5.40.45: They were cursed by Brahmā: Fools, you shall become bereft of understanding. Therefore, knowing nothing and deprived of understanding, they approached the Grandfather; ॥45॥
5.40.46: bowing down, they all said to him: Please grant us your favour. Thus addressed, he spoke this to them, solely for the sake of expiation: ॥46॥
5.40.47: Ask your own sons; then you will regain knowledge. Thus told, they, bereft of understanding, earnestly questioned their sons. ॥47॥
5.40.48: Solely for the sake of expiation, the heaven-dwellers regained their understanding. Go, little sons — thus were they addressed by their sons, O sinless one. ॥48॥
5.40.49: Then those gods, under the curse, having been told by their sons, go, little sons, went and questioned the Creator about the meaning of being called sons. ॥49॥
5.40.50: Then the god Brahmā said to those doubting gods: Listen, all you immortals: you are not knowers of Brahman. ॥50॥
5.40.51: Therefore, what was told to you by those sons of yours, the best of the wise, should be accepted, casting aside doubt, just so and not otherwise. ॥51॥
5.40.52: You gods and you Pitṛs, dwellers of heaven, worship one another with great love, granting the fruits of all desires. ॥52॥
5.40.53: Sanatkumāra said: Then, by Brahmā's word, their doubts dispelled, they became loving towards one another and bestowers of happiness, O tiger among sages. ॥53॥
5.40.54: Then the gods said to them: Since we were called little sons by you, therefore you shall be our fathers — there is no doubt. ॥54॥
5.40.55: Whoever performs the rite in the śrāddha for the ancestors — no doubt — will be blessed; Soma, nourished by śrāddhas, will nourish the worlds: ॥55॥
5.40.56: the ocean, the mountains and forests, filled with moving and unmoving beings. And those men who, desiring prosperity, perform śrāddhas — ॥56॥
5.40.57: to them the ancestors, ever pleased, will grant prosperity. And those who in the śrāddha offer three rice-balls (piṇḍa), with name and lineage (gotra) — ॥57॥
5.40.58: the fathers and great-grandfathers, present everywhere and satisfied by the offerings of śrāddha, will continually prosper them. ॥58॥
5.40.59: So let that statement be true, O heaven-dwellers: we are all sons and fathers of one another. ॥59॥
5.40.60: Thus those Pitṛs and the gods, in accordance with dharma, became sons of each other; they are renowned on the face of the earth as fathers of one another. ॥60॥
5.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The description of the power of the Pitṛs, in the section on śrāddha, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥40॥
5.41.1: Sanatkumāra said: O best of ascetics, seven groups of Pitṛs (ancestors) are declared to dwell in heaven: four are embodied, and three are without form. ॥1॥
5.41.2: The hosts of gods worship them, and likewise the foremost classes, the brahmins and the rest. They, in turn, first nourish Soma by the power of yoga. ॥2॥
5.41.3: Therefore śrāddha offerings should be given, and especially to yogins. For all, the vessel should be of silver, or else adorned with silver. ॥3॥
5.41.4: A śrāddha given with the svadhā call placed first truly pleases the Pitṛs — having first made the nourishing offering to Fire, to Soma and to Yama, ॥4॥
5.41.5: and making the offering facing north into the fire, or, if there is no fire, into water. Whoever pleases the Pitṛs with devotion, the Pitṛs please him in return. ॥5॥
5.41.6: The Pitṛs bestow nourishment and abundant offspring, heaven, increase of health, and whatever else is desired. ॥6॥
5.41.7: O sage, the rite for the Pitṛs surpasses even the rite for the gods. You are devoted to the Pitṛs, O brahmin seer; through that you are free from old age and death. ॥7॥
5.41.8: The state that belongs to one devoted to the Pitṛs, O sage, is not reached through yoga. Therefore devotion to the Pitṛs should be practised especially, O great sage. ॥8॥
5.41.9: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having spoken thus, the lord of the gods, after quickly granting him an eye endowed with discernment, hard to obtain even for the gods, went to his yogic state. ॥9॥
5.41.10: Listen further, O Bhīṣma: long ago the brahmin sons of Bhāradvāja, having attained the discipline of yoga, fell from it through misconduct. ॥10॥
5.41.11: Vāgduṣṭa, Krodhana, Hiṃsra, Piśuna, Kavi, Khasṛṣa and Pitṛvartī — so they were by names and likewise by deeds. ॥11॥
5.41.12: They were sons of Kauśika, dear one, and became disciples of Garga. When their father died, they all were then living away from home. ॥12॥
5.41.13: At the command of their teacher they were tending a milch cow, a tawny one with a calf of like colour; and then they all went astray. ॥13॥
5.41.14: On the way, as they were tormented by hunger, through childishness and delusion, O Bhārata, a cruel thought arose in them then to kill that cow. ॥14॥
5.41.15: Kavi and Khasṛpa pleaded for her, but the intent did not go away then; nor were those two able then to restrain their own brothers. ॥15॥
5.41.16: But Pitṛvartī, the brahmin among them who daily performed śrāddha as his regular rite, endowed with devotion to the Pitṛs, spoke to them all in anger: ॥16॥
5.41.17: If it must be done, let it be carried out as an offering to the Pitṛs, all of you performing the śrāddha with collected minds. ॥17॥
5.41.18: In this way this cow too will attain merit, there is no doubt; having worshipped the Pitṛs according to dharma, no unrighteousness will befall us. ॥18॥
5.41.19: Thus addressed, they all then sprinkled the cow, dedicated her to the Pitṛs, and consumed her, O Bhārata. ॥19॥
5.41.20: Having consumed the cow, they all reported to their teacher: The cow was killed by a tiger; please take the calf. ॥20॥
5.41.21: Out of guilelessness that brahmin accepted the calf. But through their false conduct the sin of cow-killing fell upon them. ॥21॥
5.41.22: Then, after some time, those seven brothers, dear one, met death when their lifespan came to an end. ॥22॥
5.41.23: Because of their cruelty, their violence, and their ignoble conduct toward the teacher, the seven brothers were born as those who delighted in fierce violence. ॥23॥
5.41.24: Thus the seven were born as hunters among the Daśārṇas, sons of a hunter, strong and high-minded, yet discerning in dharma. ॥24॥
5.41.25: Next they were all deer on the lovely mountain Kālañjara, devoted to their own duty, free from delusion, yet trembling with anxiety. ॥25॥
5.41.26: Reflecting on that very matter, which arose from remembrance of their former birth, they lived as forest-dwellers, patient, free from the pairs of opposites, and without possessions. ॥26॥
5.41.27: All those forest-dwellers were of good deeds and true dharma, free from unrighteous conduct, having attained the memory of their past births. ॥27॥
5.41.28: The dharma they had heard in former births in the houses of their teachers — just so their minds remained fixed, even within saṃsāra, upon turning back from the world. ॥28॥
5.41.29: Those ascetics, living on whatever food they obtained, gave up their lives in the midst of the mountain; and the places where they fell, O Bhārata, ॥29॥
5.41.30: are seen just so even today on the mountain Kālañjara, O king. Through that deed they were born as ones who had left behind both good and evil. ॥30॥
5.41.31: From an auspicious birth they passed to a more auspicious one, becoming cakravāka birds; in the auspicious land of Śaradvīpa the seven lived as water-dwellers. ॥31॥
5.41.32: Renouncing the life of mates, these sages upholding dharma were named Niḥsaṅga, Nirmama, Śānta, Nirdvandva, Niṣparigraha, ॥32॥
5.41.33: Nivṛtti and Nirvṛta — so were the birds known by name. All those birds were celibate and lived according to dharma. ॥33॥
5.41.34: Remembering their births, well matured, the seven celibates dwelt together, of true dharma, ever free from change. ॥34॥
5.41.35: Because of the false conduct toward their teacher committed through delusion in their brahmin birth, they received birth in animal wombs; and through the śrāddha they obtained knowledge. ॥35॥
5.41.36: Likewise, because the śrāddha was performed by them, steadfast, for the sake of the rite of the Pitṛs, knowledge and birth were then obtained in succession, each higher in quality. ॥36॥
5.41.37: The sacred knowledge (brahman) heard in former births in the houses of teachers remained established just so; therefore one should diligently cultivate knowledge. ॥37॥
5.41.38: Sumanas, Suvāk, Śuddha, the fifth Chidradarśaka, Svatantra and Suyajña — these are known by name as the Kulīṅgas. ॥38॥
5.41.39: While those birds wandered there, following dharma, a noteworthy event took place; hear of it, O great sage. ॥39॥
5.41.40: The king, lord of the Nīpas, endowed with majesty, glorious, surrounded by his women of the inner palace, entered that forest there. ॥40॥
5.41.41: That cakravāka bird named Svatantra, having seen that king going along, endowed with happiness and furnished with royal splendour, longed to be like him. ॥41॥
5.41.42: If there is any merit of mine, or austerity, or even religious observance — I am worn out by fasting and by unwavering austerity — ॥42॥
5.41.43: then by the full fruit of all that I have done, may I become such a king, a vessel of every good fortune. ॥43॥
5.41.44: Then the two cakravākas, his companions, said: Let us two be your ministers, wishing for what is dear and beneficial to you. ॥44॥
5.41.45: Saying, so be it, the boon was granted; then that was the destiny of him whose self was in yoga. And thus those two cakravākas spoke their own words in reply. ॥45॥
5.41.46: Sumanas said: Since you, speaking for worldly action even after attaining that discipline of yoga, ask for such a boon, therefore hear my words. ॥46॥
5.41.47: You will be a king, dear one, in Kāmpilya, the best of cities; and these two will be your ministers, overcome by their deviation from yoga. ॥47॥
5.41.48: The other three did not speak of kingship to those four companions. Again he showed favour: among them Sumanas spoke. ॥48॥
5.41.49: The curse will have an end; you will attain yoga again. And this Svatantra will know the cries of all creatures. ॥49॥
5.41.50: Through the grace of the ancestors, merit has been obtained by you, since, having sprinkled the cow according to dharma, its parts were offered to the ancestors. ॥50॥
5.41.51: Union with knowledge is, for all of us, the means to yoga. And this earnest statement, a single verse that has been uttered — ॥51॥
5.41.52: having heard it conveyed through another person, you will then attain yoga. Having said this, that bird, the wise Sumanas, fell silent. ॥52॥
5.41.53: Mārkaṇḍeya said: For the welfare of the worlds, dear one, O eminent son of Śantanu, I have thus told their story. What more do you wish to hear? ॥53॥
5.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The description of the creation of the Pitṛs and of the destiny of the seven hunters, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥41॥
5.42.1: Bhīṣma said: O Mārkaṇḍeya, greatly wise one, best among those who bear devotion to the Pitṛs, kindly tell me what happened after that, O best of sages. ॥1॥
5.42.2: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Those seven, who moved about the Mānasa lake, intent on the dharma of yoga, living on air and water, continually wasted away their bodies. ॥2॥
5.42.3: That king, surrounded by the women of his inner palace like Maghavan (Indra) in Nandana, having sported there for a very long time, went with his wife to his own city. ॥3॥
5.42.4: He had a son named Anūha, supremely righteous. Having installed that son in the kingdom, Vibhrāja went to the forest. ॥4॥
5.42.5: He began to perform austerities where those companions dwelt; there he, of great austerity, was without food, living on air. ॥5॥
5.42.6: Then, because it was illumined by him, that forest became well known by the name Vaibhrāja, bestowing success in yoga. ॥6॥
5.42.7: There indeed those birds—four steadfast in the dharma of yoga and three fallen from yoga—gave up their bodies. ॥7॥
5.42.8: In the city of Kāmpilya those seven great souls, headed by Brahmadatta, were born, all free from taint. ॥8॥
5.42.9: Here four retained memory of their former births, while three were deluded. Brahmadatta, independent and of great vigour, was born of Aṇuha. ॥9॥
5.42.10: Chidradarśin and Sunetra, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, who had dwelt together in their former birth, were born as heirs of a learned Vedic brahmin (śrotriya). ॥10॥
5.42.11: Pañcāla was a Bahvṛca (Ṛgvedin) and held the office of teacher; Puṇḍarīka, knower of two Vedas, was a Chandoga (Sāmavedin) and also an Adhvaryu. ॥11॥
5.42.12: Then the king, seeing his son Brahmadatta free of taint, consecrated him in his own kingdom and attained the supreme state. ॥12॥
5.42.13: Pañcāla and Puṇḍarīka, having established their sons in the house, entered the forest, and there they reached the highest state. ॥13॥
5.42.14: Brahmadatta's wife was named Sannati, O Bhārata; united with him in single-minded devotion, she delighted together with her husband. ॥14॥
5.42.15: The remaining companions, the cakravāka birds, were born in Kāmpilya as heirs of a śrotriya, in the family of a poor man, O king. ॥15॥
5.42.16: Dhṛtimān, Sumahātmā, Tattvadarśī and Nirutsuka—these four, accomplished in Vedic study, discerning the flaws of worldly life. ॥16॥
5.42.17: They, devoted to yoga and perfected, all set forth, having taken leave of one another and bowed to the lotus feet of Śambhu. ॥17॥
5.42.18: All those brahmins spoke again to their father: We shall make a provision for you by which you will maintain yourself. ॥18॥
5.42.19: Going to the taintless king Brahmadatta together with his ministers, you should make him hear this verse of great meaning. ॥19॥
5.42.20: Pleased at heart, he will give you villages and abundant enjoyments. Having said this much and having honoured that elder, they all attained the dharma of yoga and reached supreme bliss. ॥20॥
5.42.21: The father of those four great-souled brahmins, having learned the verse from his sons, felt as though he had accomplished his purpose. ॥21॥
5.42.22: He made the king and those two ministers hear that verse: Seven hunters in Daśārṇa, deer on Mount Kālañjara, ॥22॥
5.42.23: cakravākas on Śaradvīpa, swans on Lake Mānasa—they were born in Kurukṣetra as brahmins, masters of the Veda. ॥23॥
5.42.24: They have set out on the long road; why do you still languish? Hearing that, Brahmadatta, lord of men, fell into a swoon. ॥24॥
5.42.25: So too did his minister Pāñcāla and Puṇḍarīka, O Bhārata. Then, remembering that lake and regaining that yoga, ॥25॥
5.42.26: they endowed the brahmin with ample wealth and enjoyments. Having consecrated Viṣvaksena, subduer of foes, in his own kingdom, ॥26॥
5.42.27: Brahmadatta went to the forest with his wife; attaining yoga by sheer strength, he reached the state that is very hard to attain. ॥27॥
5.42.28: Puṇḍarīka too, righteous-souled, attained the unsurpassed Sāṅkhya-yoga; reaching the goal of yoga, he became perfected, purified by that deed. ॥28॥
5.42.29: Pāñcālya, of great austerity, having composed the Krama recitation of the Veda and produced the complete Śikṣā, attained the status of a teacher of yoga and foremost fame. ॥29॥
5.42.30: The valiant who, longing for freedom from rebirth, resort to this reach that supreme abode of Śambhu; may they destroy their sin today. ॥30॥
5.42.31: When a bodily, mental or verbal sin has been committed, O great sage, one should recite this properly with devotion, endowed with faith. ॥31॥
5.42.32: One is freed from all sins through repeatedly chanting Śiva's name. When this name of that God of gods is uttered, ॥32॥
5.42.33: sin dissolves like an unbaked pot in water. Therefore, when sin has been accumulated, immediately afterwards, ॥33॥
5.42.34: this should be recited for the allaying of sin, O great sage, and repeatedly by faithful men for obtaining the fruit of all desires. ॥34॥
5.42.35: Whoever reads this chapter or hears it for the sake of prosperity is freed from all sins and attains liberation; there is no doubt. ॥35॥
5.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The description of the power of the ancestors, in the section on the ancestors, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥42॥
5.43.1: Śaunaka said: O Sūta, O preceptor who is a disciple of Vyāsa, tell us now about the worship of the teacher, and also what is to be done at the end of hearing the text. ॥1॥
5.43.2: Sūta said: Having heard the supreme narrative, one should worship the teacher with devotion according to the rule; at the end of the text, with a gladdened mind, one should give gifts to the teacher according to the rule. ॥2॥
5.43.3: Then the wise man, having bowed to the speaker and having duly honoured him with ornaments for the hands and ears and with fine garments of soft cloth and the like, ॥3॥
5.43.4: and at the completion of the worship of Śiva, he should give a cow with her calf; having made a seat of gold weighing one pala, covered with cloth, ॥4॥
5.43.5: and having placed on it the auspicious text written in elegant letters, the wise man should give it to the teacher; thereby he becomes freed from the bonds of worldly existence. ॥5॥
5.43.6: A village, an elephant, a horse, and other things too according to one's capacity — all these, O sage, should be given to the great-souled reciter. ॥6॥
5.43.7: The Purāṇa heard properly, together with the prescribed procedure, is declared to be fruitful indeed; O sage Śaunaka, I have spoken only the truth. ॥7॥
