5.43.8: Therefore, O sage, one should listen with devotion, in accordance with the prescribed procedure, to the Purāṇa, which is rich in the meaning of the Vedas, bestows merit, and is the heart of revelation (śruti). ॥8॥
5.43.iti: Thus ends the forty-third adhyāya, named The manner of worshipping Vyāsa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥43॥
5.44.1: The sages said: O greatly wise Sūta, treasury of compassion, tell us of the birth of Vyāsa. O master, O lord, by your supreme grace make us fulfilled. ॥1॥
5.44.2: The mother of Vyāsa is said to be the auspicious woman named Satyavatī; and that lady, it is said, was married by King Śantanu. ॥2॥
5.44.3: How was the great yogin Vyāsa born in her from Parāśara? A great doubt has arisen here; you should dispel it. ॥3॥
5.44.4: Sūta said: Once, while travelling on a pilgrimage, the yogin Parāśara by chance came to the lovely, auspicious bank of the Yamunā. ॥4॥
5.44.5: The righteous one then said to a Niṣāda fisherman who was having his meal: Take me quickly across the Yamunā by boat. ॥5॥
5.44.6: Thus addressed by that sage, the Niṣāda spoke to his own daughter Matsyagandhā: Girl, take him across quickly by boat. ॥6॥
5.44.7: O fortunate one, this ascetic, born from the womb of Adṛśyantī, an ocean of dharma, master of the four Vedas, wishes to cross. ॥7॥
5.44.8: Thus instructed by her father, Matsyagandhā ferried the great sage, radiant as the sun, seated in the boat. ॥8॥
5.44.9: Through the force of destiny, the great yogin—who had never been infatuated even on seeing the beauty of the Apsarases—became stricken with desire for her. ॥9॥
5.44.10: Wishing to take the charming fisherman's daughter, the sage touched her right hand with his right hand. ॥10॥
5.44.11: The large-eyed one said to him with a smile: What is this deed being done, condemned by those who restrain their speech (sages)? ॥11॥
5.44.12: You were born in the lovely lineage of Vasiṣṭha, O great-minded one, while I, O brāhmaṇa, am born of a Niṣāda; how could union between us two be fitting? ॥12॥
5.44.13: Human birth is hard to obtain, brāhmaṇhood especially; and even there, asceticism is hard to attain, O best of sages. ॥13॥
5.44.14: Endowed with learning, form, speech, lineage and character, you have fallen under the power of Kāma's arrows—this indeed is a great wonder. ॥14॥
5.44.15: Though he has set about an improper act, no one on earth is able to stop him from doing it, out of fear of this yogin's curse. ॥15॥
5.44.16: Having thus reflected in her heart, she said to the great sage: Have patience, master, until I have taken you across. ॥16॥
5.44.17: Sūta said: Hearing her words, Parāśara, king of yogins, swiftly let go of her hand, and then reached the other side of the river. ॥17॥
5.44.18: The sage, tormented by desire, again seized that girl; but the girl, trembling, said to that treasury of compassion: ॥18॥
5.44.19: O best of sages, I am foul-smelling, dark-complexioned, born of a Niṣāda; whereas you are of supremely noble thought, the best of yogins. ॥19॥
5.44.20: Union between us two is not fitting, like that of glass and gold; union between those alike in birth and form would bring happiness. ॥20॥
5.44.21: Being so addressed by her, he in a mere moment made the maiden Yojanagandhā ('fragrant for a league'), lovely in form and charming. ॥21॥
5.44.22: Again that sage, afflicted by desire, seized the girl; seeing him wishing to take her, Vāsavī spoke again: ॥22॥
5.44.23: Intercourse should be performed at night, not by day—so the scripture has declared. In union by day there is great fault, and also censure hard to bear. ॥23॥
5.44.24: Therefore wait until night comes. People are watching here, and my father is standing on the bank. ॥24॥
5.44.25: Hearing these words spoken by her, the bull among sages at once created a mist by the power of his merit. ॥25॥
5.44.26: When the mist had arisen, resembling night in its darkness, the girl, anxious about intercourse, again spoke to that sage: ॥26॥
5.44.27: O yogin, your seed is unfailing; if, having enjoyed me, you go away, I would be pregnant—then, master, what would become of me? ॥27॥
5.44.28: O greatly wise one, my vow of maidenhood will be destroyed; then people will laugh. What shall I say to my father? ॥28॥
5.44.29: Parāśara said: Delight with me freely, girl, in the pleasures born of love. Tell me your own wish; I will fulfil it now, beloved. ॥29॥
5.44.30: Because you make my command true, be Satyavatī by name, worthy of reverence by all yogins and even by the gods. ॥30॥
5.44.31: Satyavatī said: If neither my father nor my mother nor other people on earth come to know, and if my maidenhood is not destroyed, then accept me. ॥31॥
5.44.32: And, lord, may there be a son equal to you, possessed of wondrous power; may there be fragrance in my body always, and youth ever new. ॥32॥
5.44.33: Parāśara said: Listen, beloved: all you desire will be fulfilled. A son born of a portion of Viṣṇu, of great fame, will be yours. ॥33॥
5.44.34: Know that there is indeed some reason why I am afflicted by desire; for even on seeing the beauty of the Apsarases my mind was never deluded. ॥34॥
5.44.35: Having beheld you, fish-smelling one, I fell under the sway of delusion. Girl, what Brahmā has written on the forehead cannot turn out otherwise. ॥35॥
5.44.36: Your son, O fair-hipped one, will be the composer of the Purāṇas and the divider of the branches of the Veda, of renowned fame in the three worlds. ॥36॥
5.44.37: Having said this and enjoyed that lovely-limbed one, the master of yoga bathed in the water of the Yamunā and departed swiftly, O great sage. ॥37॥
5.44.38: She too quickly conceived an embryo radiant as the sun, and on an island of the Yamunā (daughter of the Sun) gave birth to a son like Kāmadeva. ॥38॥
5.44.39: Holding a water-pot in his left hand and an excellent staff in his right, adorned with tawny matted locks, he was a mass of splendour. ॥39॥
5.44.40: As soon as he was born, the radiant one said to his mother: Go, mother, as you wish; I too shall go hence. ॥40॥
5.44.41: Mother, whenever you have some task that your heart desires, I will come as soon as you remember me, in order to fulfil your wish. ॥41॥
5.44.42: Having said this and saluted his mother's feet, he who was a treasure of austerity went to a sacred ford that cleanses sin, to perform austerities. ॥42॥
5.44.43: She too, the virtuous one, went to her father's side, agitated by love for her son, recalling her son's deeds and describing her own good fortune. ॥43॥
5.44.44: Because the boy was born on an island (dvīpa), he became known as Dvaipāyana; and because he divided the branches of the Veda, he is celebrated as Vedavyāsa. ॥44॥
5.44.45: First he went to the king of tīrthas, Prayāga, which grants dharma, desire, wealth and liberation; then Naimiṣa, Kurukṣetra, Gaṅgādvāra, Avantikā, ॥45॥
5.44.46: Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Dvārakā, Amarāvatī, the Sarasvatī, the confluence of the Sindhu, and the meeting of the Gaṅgā with the ocean, ॥46॥
5.44.47: Kāñcī, Tryambaka, the bank of the Seven Godāvarīs, Kālañjara, Prabhāsa, and likewise the hermitage of Badarikā, ॥47॥
5.44.48: Mahālaya, likewise the Oṅkāra-kṣetra, Puruṣottama, Gokarṇa, Bhṛgukaccha, Bhṛgutuṅga and Puṣkara, ॥48॥
5.44.49: and the tīrthas beginning with Śrīparvata, and likewise Dhārātīrtha — having gone to these and bathed according to rule, he performed supreme austerity. ॥49॥
5.44.50: Thus, wandering through many tīrthas situated in various lands, the son of Kālikā Satyavatī reached the city of Vārāṇasī, ॥50॥
5.44.51: where Viśveśvara himself and the great goddess Annapūrṇā, the two treasures of compassion, shine forth to grant nectar to their devotees. ॥51॥
5.44.52: Having reached the tīrtha of Vārāṇasī and then seen Maṇikarṇikā, that lord of sages cast off the sin accumulated over ten million births. ॥52॥
5.44.53: Having seen all the liṅgas headed by Viśveśa, and bathed in all the pools, step-wells, wells and lakes, ॥53॥
5.44.54: having bowed to all the Vināyakas and saluted all the Gaurīs, and having worshipped Kālarāja Bhairava, the devourer of sin, ॥54॥
5.44.55: having diligently praised the gaṇas headed by Daṇḍanāyaka, and having pleased the Keśavas headed by Ādikeśava, ॥55॥
5.44.56: and having bowed again and again to the Suns headed by Lolārka, and tirelessly made offerings of piṇḍas at all the tīrthas, ॥56॥
5.44.57: the pure-souled one installed a liṅga named Vyāseśvara, by the sight of which, O brahmins, a man becomes a master of speech in the branches of learning. ॥57॥
5.44.58: Having worshipped with great devotion the liṅgas headed by Viśveśa, he pondered repeatedly: Which liṅga grants success quickly, ॥58॥
5.44.59: by worshipping which Mahādeva we may obtain all the branches of knowledge, and by whose grace I may gain the power to compose the Purāṇas? ॥59॥
5.44.60: Is it the glorious Oṅkāranātha, or perhaps Kṛttivāseśvara? Or Kedāreśa, Kāmeśa, Candreśa, or Trilocana? ॥60॥
5.44.61: Kāleśa, Vṛddhakāleśa, or Kalaśeśvara; Jyeṣṭheśa, Jambukeśa, or Jaigīṣavyeśvara? ॥61॥
5.44.62: Daśāśvamedha, Īśāna, or Drumacaṇḍeśa; Dṛkkeśa, Garuḍeśa, Gokarṇeśa, or Gaṇeśvara? ॥62॥
5.44.63: Or Prasannavadaneśa, Dharmeśa, Tārakeśvara, Nandikeśa, Nivāseśa, Patrīśa, or Prītikeśvara? ॥63॥
5.44.64: Parvateśa, Paśupati, or Hāṭakeśvara; or else Bṛhaspatīśvara, or Tilabhāṇḍeśa? ॥64॥
5.44.65: Is it Bhārabhūteśvara, or Mahālakṣmīśvara? Or Maruteśa, Mokṣeśa, Gaṅgeśa, or Narmadeśvara? ॥65॥
5.44.66: Kṛṣṇeśa, Parameśāna, or else Ratneśvara; Yāmuneśa, Lāṅgalīśa, or the all-pervading glorious Viśveśvara? ॥66॥
5.44.67: Or else Avimukteśvara, or Viśālākṣīśa; Vyāghreśvara, Varāheśa, or Vidyeśvara? ॥67॥
5.44.68: Varuṇeśa, Vidhīśa, or Harikeśeśvara; Bhavānīśa, Kapardīśa, Kandukeśa, or Ajeśvara? ॥68॥
5.44.69: Or else Viśvakarmeśvara, or Vīreśvara; Nādeśa, Kapileśa, or Bhuvaneśvara? ॥69॥
5.44.70: Vāṣkulīśa, Mahādeva, or else Siddhīśvara; Viśvedeveśvara, Vīrabhadreśa, or Bhairaveśvara? ॥70॥
5.44.71: Amṛteśa, Satīśa, or Pārvatīśvara; Siddheśvara, Mataṅgeśa, or else Bhūtīśvara? ॥71॥
5.44.72: Āṣāḍhīśa, Prakāśeśa, likewise Koṭirudreśvara, and Madālaseśvara — or perhaps Tilaparṇeśvara? ॥72॥
5.44.73: Or is it Hiraṇyagarbheśa, or the glorious Madhyameśvara? Among these and ten million other liṅgas, in which shall I take refuge? ॥73॥
5.44.74: Thus troubled by anxious thought, Vyāsa, whose self delighted in devotion to Śiva, reflected for a moment with a mind made steady by meditation. ॥74॥
5.44.75: Ah, I know. It had slipped my mind until now; my wish is accomplished: the liṅga worshipped by the Siddhas, which grants dharma, desire, wealth and liberation, ॥75॥
5.44.76: by the sight and touch of which the mind attains purity, and where indeed the door of heaven always stands open — ॥76॥
5.44.77: that supreme place in the great field of Avimukta, the field of the Siddhas, where abides the supreme liṅga called Madhyameśvara. ॥77॥
5.44.78: Indeed there is no other liṅga in Kāśī equal to Madhyameśvara, to see which the gods come at every festival day. ॥78॥
5.44.79: Therefore Mahādeva named Madhyameśvara is to be served; through worship of him many brahmins have attained perfection. ॥79॥
5.44.80: Since Śaṅkara, as the chief deity, stands in the middle of Kāśī for the happiness of the people of his own city, he is therefore called Madhyameśvara. ॥80॥
5.44.81: The Gandharva named Tumburu, and likewise the divine sage Nārada, by worshipping this Liṅga became masters of the science of music. ॥81॥
5.44.82: By worshipping this very one, Viṣṇu became the bestower of liberation; and so Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra became the creator, preserver and destroyer. ॥82॥
5.44.83: Kubera too became the lord of wealth, and Vāmadeva indeed the king among Śaivas; the king named Khaṭvāṅga, who was childless, came to have offspring. ॥83॥
5.44.84: The Apsaras named Candrabhāmā, sweet-voiced as a cuckoo, dancing out of her own devotion, merged bodily into the midst of the Liṅga. ॥84॥
5.44.85: Śrīkara, the son of a cowherd woman, by serving Madhyameśvara obtained the rank of a gaṇa-leader of the compassionate Śiva. ॥85॥
5.44.86: Bhārgava and Gīṣpati, both gods worshipped by the Daityas and the Suras respectively, became masters of learning through the grace of the Lord Madhyameśa. ॥86॥
5.44.87: I too, worshipping here the Lord Madhyameśvara, shall surely and swiftly obtain the power to compose the Purāṇas. ॥87॥
5.44.88: Having thus made up his mind, the steadfast Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, bathed in the waters of the Bhāgīrathī and, as a votary, took up a course of observance. ॥88॥
5.44.89: At times he lived on leaves, at times on fruits and vegetables; somewhere he lived on air, on water, and at times kept a vow of total fasting. ॥89॥
5.44.90: With such observances the righteous yogin worshipped Madhyameśvara at the three times of day with fruits from various trees. ॥90॥
5.44.91: When much time had thus passed, as the son of Kālikā, having bathed in the waters of the Tripathagā, was coming at dawn — ॥91॥
5.44.92: — just then the pure-souled one saw Maheśvara in the midst of the Liṅga: Madhyameśvara, the Lord, granter of the boons desired by devotees, ॥92॥
5.44.93: his left side adorned by Umā, with a tiger skin as upper garment, his form beautiful with the waves of the Gaṅgā moving in his mass of matted hair, ॥93॥
5.44.94: his locks moonlit by the radiance of the shining young autumn moon, all his limbs smeared with ash, his form white as camphor, ॥94॥
5.44.95: with eyes long, reaching to the ears, and lips red as coral, a boy with the form of a five-year-old, wearing ornaments fit for a child, ॥95॥
5.44.96: bearing a bodily radiance that humbles the pride of millions of Kandarpas, naked, his lotus-face smiling, playfully singing the Sāman, ॥96॥
5.44.97: an ocean of boundless compassion, bearing the name Bhaktavatsala (loving to devotees), quickly pleased, beloved of Umā, his face gracious with favour — Hara. ॥97॥
5.44.98: Having beheld him, with a voice choked with love he composed a hymn to him who is unreachable even by yogins, the friend of the afflicted, whose nature is consciousness. ॥98॥
5.44.99: Vedavyāsa said: O God of gods, O greatly blessed one, loving to those who seek refuge, hard to attain by speech, mind and action, beyond the range even of yogins. ॥99॥
5.44.100: The Vedas did not know your greatness, O Lord of Umā. You alone are the creator, sustainer and likewise destroyer of the world. ॥100॥
5.44.101: You are the first of all the gods, the Lord who is being, consciousness and bliss. You have neither name nor lineage; you are omniscient, O Sadāśiva. ॥101॥
5.44.102: You alone are the supreme Brahman, the remover of the noose of Māyā; you are not stained by the three guṇas, as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water. ॥102॥
5.44.103: You have no birth, no conduct, no country and no family; yet though such, you as Lord fulfil the desires of the three worlds. ॥103॥
5.44.104: Neither Brahmā, nor the Lord of Lakṣmī, nor the gods with Indra, nor the chief yogins know your true nature — you, such as you are, we worship. ॥104॥
5.44.105: From you is everything, and you indeed are everything; you are the Lord of Gaurī, the destroyer of the three cities; you are the child, the youth, the old man — you I fix in my heart. ॥105॥
5.44.106: Salutation to that Maheśa, meditated upon by devotees, to Śambhu, truly the Primeval Person, to Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self. ॥106॥
5.44.107: Having praised thus, as soon as he fell prostrate on the ground like a staff, that boy, delighted, spoke to Vedavyāsa. ॥107॥
5.44.108: Choose a boon, O yogin, whatever is in your mind; there is nothing that cannot be given, since I am subject to my devotees. ॥108॥
5.44.109: Then, rising up, delighted, the sage Vyāsa of great austerity replied: What is unknown to you who are omniscient, O Lord? ॥109॥
5.44.110: You are the inner Self of all, the blessed Śarva, the giver of everything; why does the Lord set me to begging, which brings abasement? ॥110॥
5.44.111: Hearing these words of Vyāsa of spotless mind, Mahādeva, bearing the form of a boy, smiled purely and said: ॥111॥
5.44.112: The boy said: O best of the knowers of Brahman, the wish you have formed in your heart will come true in a very short time, without doubt. ॥112॥
5.44.113: Abiding in your throat, O Brahmin, I, the Lord, the Inner Controller, shall properly bring forth the Purāṇas together with the Itihāsas. ॥113॥
5.44.114: This holy hymn uttered by you, the Abhilāṣāṣṭaka, grants desires when recited three times daily for a year in a shrine of Śambhu. ॥114॥
5.44.115: Recitation of this hymn is declared to increase learning and intelligence, to bring all prosperity, and to grant dharma and liberation to men. ॥115॥
5.44.116: Rising at dawn, well bathed, worshipping Śaṅkara's Liṅga and reciting this hymn for a year, even a fool would become a Bṛhaspati. ॥116॥
5.44.117: Whether by a woman or by a man, this hymn, recited with discipline for a year near the Liṅga, would increase intelligence and learning. ॥117॥
5.44.118: Having said this, that Mahādeva in the form of a boy merged into the Liṅga; and Vyāsa, shedding tears, was overwhelmed with love for Śiva. ॥118॥
5.44.119: Thus having obtained the boon from the great Lord Madhyameśvara, Vyāsa composed the eighteen Purāṇas with ease of his own. ॥119॥
5.44.120: The Brāhma, the Pādma, the Vaiṣṇava, the Śaiva, and likewise the Bhāgavata; the Bhaviṣya and the Nāradīya, and after that the Mārkaṇḍeya; ॥120॥
5.44.121: Then the Āgneya, the Brahmavaivarta, the Laiṅga and the Vārāha; then the one called Vāmana, the Kaurma, the Mātsya and the Gāruḍa; ॥121॥
5.44.122: likewise the Skānda, and the Purāṇa called Brahmāṇḍa, are proclaimed. They are bringers of fame and merit to the men who hear them, and their theme is the glory of Śaṅkara. ॥122॥
5.44.123: Sūta said: You earlier stated the names of the eighteen Purāṇas. Now, O best of Veda-knowers, give the explanation of those names. ॥123॥
5.44.124: Vyāsa said: This very question was put by Taṇḍi, born of Brahmā, addressing Nandikeśvara; what he said, I now tell. ॥124॥
5.44.125: Nandīśvara said: O Taṇḍi, since the speaker in it is the four-faced Brahmā himself, in person, that first Purāṇa is called the Brāhma, O sage. ॥125॥
5.44.126: That collection in which the greatness of the Padma Kalpa is related is therefore called the Pādma, the second Purāṇa. ॥126॥
5.44.127: The Purāṇa composed by Parāśara, which makes Viṣṇu known, is itself regarded as narrated by Vyāsa, because of the non-difference between son and father. ॥127॥
5.44.128: That in which, in the earlier and later sections, the deeds of Śiva are narrated abundantly — this is the Śaiva Purāṇa, as the knowers of the Purāṇas declare. ॥128॥
5.44.129: That in which the story of the Goddess Durgā is found is called the Bhāgavata — indeed, the Devī Purāṇa. ॥129॥
5.44.130: The Purāṇa spoken by Nārada they call the Nāradīya. That in which, O Taṇḍi, the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya was the speaker — ॥130॥
5.44.131: that is called the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, the seventh. From its connection with Agni it is the Āgneya; from its telling of the future, the Bhaviṣya. ॥131॥
5.44.132: From the transformation (vivartana) of Brahman it is called the Brahmavaivarta; because it tells the story of the Liṅga, the Purāṇa is called the Liṅga. ॥132॥
5.44.133: The Purāṇa of the Boar is the Vārāha, the twelfth, O sage. That in which Skanda himself is the listener and Maheśvara in person the speaker — ॥133॥
5.44.134: that is called the Skānda. The story of Vāmana is the Vāmana; the Kaurma is the story of the Tortoise; the Mātsya is that proclaimed by the Fish. ॥134॥
5.44.135: That of which Garuḍa himself is the speaker is named the Gāruḍa; because it tells the story of the cosmic egg, it is proclaimed the Brahmāṇḍa. ॥135॥
5.44.136: Sūta said: This very question was put by me to the wise Vyāsa; then I heard from him the explanation of all the Purāṇas. ॥136॥
5.44.137: Thus Vyāsa was born from Parāśara in Satyavatī. He composed the Purāṇa collections and the excellent Mahābhārata. ॥137॥
5.44.138: Regarding Satyavatī's union with Parāśara and then again with Śantanu, O brahmin, you should not entertain doubt here. ॥138॥
5.44.139: This wondrous birth, which had its proper cause, has been narrated. In the conduct of the great, the discerning should take up only the virtues. ॥139॥
5.44.140: Whoever hears or even recites this supreme secret is freed from all sins and is honoured in the world of the sages. ॥140॥
5.44.iti: Thus ends the forty-fourth adhyāya, named The description of the birth of Vyāsa, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥44॥
5.45.1: The sages said: We have heard the delightful story of Śambhu, filled with various narratives and joined with various incarnations, which grants enjoyment and liberation to men. ॥1॥
5.45.2: Now, O best of the knowers of Brahman, we wish to hear from you the charming story of the Mother of the world, the Blessed Goddess. ॥2॥
5.45.3: She who is the primordial, eternal Śakti of Maheśa, the Supreme Brahman, renowned as Umā, the supreme mother of the three worlds — ॥3॥
5.45.4: Two of her incarnations, Satī and Haimavatī, we have heard. O Sūta of great intellect, tell us of her other incarnations. ॥4॥
5.45.5: What intelligent person would grow weary of the act of hearing the virtues of the Holy Mother, which the wise never abandon? ॥5॥
5.45.6: Sūta said: Blessed are you, great souls; you are ever fulfilled, since you ask about the great story of Umā, the Supreme Mother. ॥6॥
5.45.7: The sages know that the dust of the lotus-feet of those who hear, ask about, and recite it is itself as sacred as the holy places. ॥7॥
5.45.8: Blessed and fulfilled are they, and blessed are their mother and family, whose mind is absorbed in the Holy Goddess, the supreme consciousness. ॥8॥
5.45.9: Those who do not praise the Queen of the gods, the cause of all causes, are deluded by the qualities of Māyā and are unfortunate; there is no doubt. ॥9॥
5.45.10: Those who do not worship the Great Goddess, an ocean of the essence of compassion, fall into the terrible blind well that is saṃsāra. ॥10॥
5.45.11: Just as one might abandon the Gaṅgā and go to desert water to quench one's thirst, so does one who abandons the Goddess go to another god distinct from her. ॥11॥
5.45.12: By the mere remembrance of her one effortlessly obtains the four aims of human life; what excellent man would abandon her? ॥12॥
5.45.13: Long ago the sage Medhas was asked this by the great-souled Suratha. What Medhas then said, listen to it; I shall tell you. ॥13॥
5.45.14: Formerly, in the Svārociṣa Manvantara, there was a king named Viratha. Suratha was his son, of great strength and valour. ॥14॥
5.45.15: He was generous in giving, truthful, skilled in his own dharma, accomplished, a devotee of the Goddess, an ocean of compassion, and protector of his subjects. ॥15॥
5.45.16: While he, with splendour like Indra's, was ruling the earth, there arose nine kings intent on seizing the land. ॥16॥
5.45.17: They besieged that king's capital named Kolā, and a tumultuous, dreadful battle took place with them. ॥17॥
5.45.18: In the battle that king was defeated by those powerful hosts of enemies, and, his kingdom wholly seized, he was driven out of Kolā. ॥18॥
5.45.19: That king came to his own city and ruled with his ministers; but there too he was defeated by powerful adversaries. ॥19॥
5.45.20: By fate, his own groups led by his ministers turned hostile, and they appropriated all the wealth that lay in the treasury. ॥20॥
5.45.21: Then the king left the city under the pretext of hunting; alone, mounting a horse, he went into a dense forest. ॥21॥
5.45.22: Wandering here and there, the king saw there the hermitage of an eminent sage, resplendent on every side with flower gardens, ॥22॥
5.45.23: filled with the sound of the Vedas, inhabited by peaceful creatures, surrounded on all sides by disciples, their disciples, and their disciples' disciples. ॥23॥
5.45.24: O wise ones, in that hermitage tigers and other mighty beasts did not harm the weak, owing to the power of that best of brahmins. ॥24॥
5.45.25: There the wise and very compassionate king dwelt, honoured by the lord of sages with kind words, food, and a seat. ॥25॥
5.45.26: One day that great king fell into an inescapable anxiety: Alas, for me, unfortunate, foolish, and bereft of power! ॥26॥
5.45.27: My kingdom has been taken entirely by hosts of enemies puffed up with pride. The kingdom protected by my forefathers is now enjoyed by enemies. ॥27॥
5.45.28: In this Caitra lineage there was no king like me. What shall I do? Where shall I go? How indeed may I regain the kingdom? ॥28॥
5.45.29: My long-standing officials and ministers — I do not know which king they have now approached and serve. ॥29॥
5.45.30: Having ruined the kingdom, I do not know what state they have now reached — those who were full of zeal on the battlefield and cutters-down of hosts of foes. ॥30॥
5.45.31: My great heroes serve another king. My mountain-like elephants and horses that ran swift as the wind — ॥31॥
5.45.32: and the treasury amassed by my forefathers — are they now being cared for by them or not? Thus the supremely righteous king fell under the sway of delusion. ॥32॥
5.45.33: Meanwhile a certain vaiśya arrived there. The king asked: Who are you, sir, and why have you come here? ॥33॥
5.45.34: Why do you appear dejected? Tell me this now. Hearing these pleasant words spoken by the king, ॥34॥
5.45.35: Samādhi, the best of vaiśyas, shedding tears from his eyes, replied to the king in words bowed with affection. ॥35॥
5.45.36: The merchant said: I am a vaiśya named Samādhi, born in a wealthy family. O lord of the earth, I was cast out by my sons, wife, and others out of greed for wealth. ॥36॥
5.45.37: O king, grieved by my own karma, I have come to the forest. I do not know the welfare of my sons, grandsons, and wives, ॥37॥
5.45.38: of my brothers, nephews, other kin, and friends; I do not rightly know their welfare, O lord, ocean of compassion. ॥38॥
5.45.39: The king said: Why do you, like a foolish creature, cherish love for those wicked sons and others, greedy for wealth, by whom you were driven out? ॥39॥
5.45.40: The merchant said: O king, you have spoken rightly, words rich in essential meaning; yet my mind is greatly deluded by the noose of affection. ॥40॥
5.45.41: Thus, O best of sages, the merchant and the king, both troubled by delusion, then went into the presence of Medhas, the foremost of sages. ॥41॥
5.45.42: That valiant king of men, very steadfast, accompanied by the chief of merchants, bowed with his head to the best of yogins. ॥42॥
5.45.43: Joining his palms, the king spoke these words to the sage: O blessed one, you should now cut away the delusion of us two. ॥43॥
5.45.44: I, abandoned by royal fortune, have taken refuge in a dense forest; yet, though my kingdom has been taken away, contentment does not arise in me at all. ॥44॥
5.45.45: And this merchant has been driven out of his home by his own people, his wife and others; yet his attachment does not come to an end. ॥45॥
5.45.46: Tell us what the cause is here: though we both have knowledge, our mind has become agitated by delusion. This is indeed a great foolishness. ॥46॥
5.45.47: The sage said: Mahāmāyā, the sustainer of the world, eternal, whose form is Power — she, drawing away the minds of all, deludes them. ॥47॥
5.45.48: O lord, all the gods beginning with Brahmā, deluded by her māyā, do not know the supreme reality — what then to speak of humans? ॥48॥
5.45.49: She creates the whole universe, she alone protects it, and she alone withdraws it in time — the supreme Goddess possessing the three guṇas. ॥49॥
5.45.50: He alone with whom she, the boon-giver who takes forms at will, is pleased passes beyond delusion — not otherwise, O best of kings. ॥50॥
5.45.51: The king said: Who is that goddess Mahāmāyā who deludes all? And how was that goddess born? Kindly tell me, O sage. ॥51॥
5.45.52: The sage said: When the world had become a single ocean and Keśava, king of yogins, spreading Śeṣa as his bed, resorted to yogic sleep and slept, ॥52॥
5.45.53: then two asuras were born from the ear-wax of Viṣṇu, named Madhu and Kaiṭabha, renowned on the face of the earth. ॥53॥
5.45.54: Radiant like the sun at the dissolution, terrible, huge-bodied, with great jaws, their faces dreadful with fangs, as if devouring the worlds, ॥54॥
5.45.55: seeing the lotus-seated Brahmā on the lotus of the Lord's navel, they became ready to kill him, saying, Hey, who are you? ॥55॥
5.45.56: Seeing those two daityas, and Janārdana lying asleep in the ocean of milk, the eldest of the gods praised the supreme Goddess. ॥56॥
5.45.57: Brahmā said: Protect, protect me, O Mahāmāyā, loving to those who seek refuge, O Mother of the world, from these two terrible-looking daityas. ॥57॥
5.45.58: I bow to Mahāmāyā, Yoganidrā, Umā, Satī, Kālarātri, Mahārātri, Moharātri, higher than the highest; ॥58॥
5.45.59: mother of the three gods, eternal, granting the desired fruits to devotees, protectress of all the gods, an ocean of compassion. ॥59॥
5.45.60: Through your power I, Brahmā, Mādhava, and the Lord of Girijā create, protect, and in due time destroy the world. ॥60॥
5.45.61: You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā, you are modesty (hrī); you are considered pure intelligence. You alone, O Mother, are contentment, nourishment, peace, forbearance, hunger, and compassion. ॥61॥
5.45.62: You alone, O Mother, are Viṣṇumāyā; you alone are regarded as consciousness. You are declared the supreme Power; you too are shame and thirst. ॥62॥
5.45.63: You are error; you are in the form of memory; you abide in the form of the mother. You are Lakṣmī in the homes of men who practise virtuous conduct. ॥63॥
5.45.64: You are birth (jāti); you are considered livelihood; you alone are in the form of pervasion. You alone, in the form of consciousness, pervade all and stand established. ॥64॥
5.45.65: Such as you are, O Ambikā, delude these two invincible asuras; O source of the world, awaken Nārāyaṇa, the unborn, all-pervading Lord. ॥65॥
5.45.66: The sage said: Entreated by Brahmā for the destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, she — Mahāvidyā, sustainer of the world, presiding deity of all knowledge — ॥66॥
5.45.67: appeared, O king, on the bright twelfth day of Phālguna, the Power renowned as Mahākālī, enchantress of the three worlds. ॥67॥
5.45.68: Then a voice arose from the sky: Do not fear, O lotus-seated one. Today, having slain Madhu and Kaiṭabha in battle, I shall destroy this thorn. ॥68॥
5.45.69: Having said this, Mahāmāyā came forth from the eyes, mouth and other parts of Hari and stood in view of Brahmā, whose birth is from the Unmanifest. ॥69॥
5.45.70: And Hṛṣīkeśa, Janārdana, god of gods, arose. He saw before him the two daityas named Madhu and Kaiṭabha. ॥70॥
5.45.71: A fight began between them and Viṣṇu of incomparable splendour; then for five thousand years there was a hand-to-hand combat. ॥71॥
5.45.72: Deluded by the power of Mahāmāyā, the two foremost dānavas said to Ramā's beloved: Choose the boon you desire. ॥72॥
5.45.73: Nārāyaṇa said: If you two are pleased with me, let this boon be given to me: may you both be slain by me. I ask no other boon of you. ॥73॥
5.45.74: The sage said: Seeing the earth become one ocean, they said to Keśava: Slay us where this earth is not flooded with water. ॥74॥
5.45.75: Saying, so be it, the Lord raised his brilliantly blazing discus and, placing their heads on his own thigh, cut them off. ॥75॥
5.45.76: Thus, O king, the origin of Kālikā has been told to you. Now hear likewise the birth of Mahālakṣmī, O wise one. ॥76॥
5.45.77: Though changeless, she takes form; though formless, the goddess Umā manifests age after age to destroy the suffering of the gods. ॥77॥
5.45.78: All this is the splendour of her will; her assuming a body is said to be in play, for the sake of her devotees' describing her qualities. ॥78॥
5.45.iti: Thus ends the forty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of the incarnation of Mahākālikā, in the section on the slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥45॥
5.46.1: The sage said: There was an asura named Rambhāsura, the crest-jewel of the Daitya race. From him was born a Dānava of great might named Mahiṣa. ॥1॥
5.46.2: That lord of the Danujas, having conquered all the gods in battle, ruled the kingdom in heaven, seated on great Indra's throne. ॥2॥
5.46.3: Then the defeated gods went to Brahmā for refuge. Brahmā too, taking them along, went to where Viṣṇu and Śiva (Vṛṣākapī) were. ॥3॥
5.46.4: Having gone there, all the gods bowed to Śaṅkara and Keśava and narrated their own story accurately and in due order. ॥4॥
5.46.5: O two Lords, all of us have been driven out of heaven by the wicked Mahiṣa, having been defeated on the battlefield. ॥5॥
5.46.6: We wander in this mortal world and find peace nowhere. To what misery after misery have the gods led by Indra not been brought? ॥6॥
5.46.7: The Sun and Moon, the noose-bearer Varuṇa, Kubera and Yama, Indra, Agni, Vāyu, the Gandharvas, Vidyādharas and noble Cāraṇas — ॥7॥
5.46.8: — the duties proper to these and to others, that sinful asura, who makes the Daitya side fearless, performs himself. ॥8॥
5.46.9: Therefore you ought to protect us gods who have come for refuge; and may you two lords quickly devise a means of slaying him. ॥9॥
5.46.10: Hearing these words of the gods, Dāmodara and the Lord of Satī became extremely angry, their eyes rolling with rage. ॥10॥
5.46.11: Then from the mouths of Viṣṇu and Śambhu, filled with intense anger, and likewise from the bodies of the other gods, a radiance came forth. ॥11॥
5.46.12: All the gods, intent on meditating on Durgā, saw a mass of exceedingly great radiance blazing in the ten directions. ॥12॥
5.46.13: That most terrifying splendour, arisen from the bodies of all the gods, coalesced and became a woman — Mahiṣamardinī herself. ॥13॥
5.46.14: Her brilliant face arose from Śambhu's splendour; from Yama's came her hair, and from Viṣṇu's her arms. ॥14॥
5.46.15: From the Moon's splendour her pair of breasts was born; from Indra's her waist; from Varuṇa's her shanks and thighs. ॥15॥
5.46.16: From the Earth's splendour came her hips; from Brahmā's her two feet; from the Sun's her toes, and from the Vasus' her fingers. ॥16॥
5.46.17: From Kubera's splendour her nose, from Prajāpati's her teeth, from Agni's her three eyes, and from the Twilight's her two eyebrows. ॥17॥
5.46.18: From Vāyu's her two ears; and likewise from the splendour of the other heaven-dwellers arose that Supreme Goddess, the lotus-dweller Lakṣmī. ॥18॥
5.46.19: Then, beholding her who had arisen from the mass of splendour of all the gods, all the gods attained supreme joy. ॥19॥
5.46.20: Seeing her without weapons, the gods, lords of heaven headed by Brahmā, resolved to make that auspicious one armed. ॥20॥
5.46.21: Then Maheśa presented a trident to the Great Goddess; Lord Kṛṣṇa a discus; and the noose-bearer Varuṇa a conch and a noose. ॥21॥
5.46.22: Agni gave a spear, and Vāyu a bow and two quivers full of arrows; the Lord of Śacī gave the thunderbolt and a bell. ॥22॥
5.46.23: Yama gave the staff of Death, Prajāpati a rosary; Brahmā gave a water-pot, and the Sun placed his rays in her hair-pores. ॥23॥
5.46.24: Kāla gave her a sword and a gleaming shield; the Ocean of Milk a lovely necklace and likewise a pair of unaging garments. ॥24॥
5.46.25: It also gave a crest-jewel, a pair of earrings, and bracelets as well, a half-moon ornament, armlets, and a pair of charming anklets, ॥25॥
5.46.26: a neck ornament, and rings for all her fingers. And Viśvakarman gave her a beautiful axe, ॥26॥
5.46.27: many missiles, and likewise impenetrable armour. The Ocean gave a lovely fresh garland and a lotus. ॥27॥
5.46.28: Himavat gave a lion and various gems; Kubera presented her with a cup filled with wine. ॥28॥
5.46.29: And Śeṣa, leader of the serpents, gave her a serpent-necklace adorned with wondrous workmanship and strung with many fine gems. ॥29॥
5.46.30: Honoured by these and other gods with ornaments and weapons, the Goddess roared aloud again and again with peals of laughter. ॥30॥
5.46.31: The expanse of the sky was filled with her terrifying roar; there was a great echo, and the three worlds shook. ॥31॥
5.46.32: The four oceans surged and the earth trembled. Then the gods, afflicted by Mahiṣa, raised the cry of Victory! ॥32॥
5.46.33: Then all those gods praised Ambikā, the supreme Śakti in the form of Mahālakṣmī, with voices choked with devotion. ॥33॥
5.46.34: Seeing the world in turmoil, those enemies of the gods, with their soldiers in armour, rose up with weapons raised. ॥34॥
5.46.35: Mahiṣa too, filled with rage, rushed toward that sound. Then he saw the Goddess, who pervaded the three worlds with her radiance. ॥35॥
5.46.36: Meanwhile, the great heroes protected by Mahiṣāsura arrived there by the crore, bearing weapons. ॥36॥
5.46.37: Cikṣura, Cāmara and Udagra, Karāla, Uddhata and Bāṣkala, Tāmra, Ugrāsya and Ugravīrya, Biḍāla and Andhaka, ॥37॥
5.46.38: Durdhara and Durmukha, Trinetra and Mahāhanu — these and many other heroes skilled in war, ॥38॥
5.46.39: masters of weapons and missiles, fought in battle with the Goddess. Thus passed a terrible time as the two sides fought. ॥39॥
5.46.40: The masses of various weapons and missiles hurled by the hands of the enemy host became fruitless in an instant through the power of Mahāmāyā. ॥40॥
5.46.41: Then that Goddess struck down the enemies headed by Cikṣura, together with their troops, with her mace, arrows, trident, spear and axe. ॥41॥
5.46.42: When his own armies had thus been slain, Mahiṣāsura turned his attention to those troops born from the Goddess's breath. ॥42॥
5.46.43: He struck some with his hooves and some with his two horns, and again and again he tore others apart with his tail and his snout. ॥43॥
5.46.44: Having thus slain the Goddess's troops, that lord of the asuras rushed forward to kill the Goddess's lion; then she became enraged. ॥44॥
5.46.45: He too, of great might, in anger pounding the ground with his hooves, uprooted a mountain with his two horns, hurled it, and roared. ॥45॥
5.46.46: Heavy mountains, flung by him as he whirled about swiftly in every direction, fell from the sky onto the earth, O best of kings. ॥46॥
5.46.47: Clouds pierced by his horns broke apart into pieces, and the ocean, lashed by his tail, surged over its shores on every side. ॥47॥
5.46.48: Seeing Mahiṣāsura thus enraged, Ambikā, who grants fearlessness to the gods, devised the means of slaying him. ॥48॥
5.46.49: Then the Sovereign Goddess raised her noose, cast it over him and bound the buffalo; he too abandoned his buffalo form. ॥49॥
5.46.50: Then the deceiver quickly became a lion; just as Ambikā was about to cleave its head, he became a man with sword in hand. ॥50॥
5.46.51: The Goddess struck him, shield and sword in hand, with arrows; then, taking the body of an elephant, he tore at the lion with his trunk. ॥51॥
5.46.52: Then the Goddess cut off his trunk with her great sword, and the demon once again assumed his own form. ॥52॥
5.46.53: At that very moment he shook the three worlds with all their moving and unmoving beings. Then Caṇḍikā, the Great Māyā, of proud valour, became enraged. ॥53॥
5.46.54: She drank the drink again and again and laughed, her eyes rolling; and that asura too roared, puffed up with the intoxication of his strength and might. ॥54॥
5.46.55: That asura uprooted mountains and hurled them at her, and she swiftly pulverised them with the blows of volleys of arrows. ॥55॥
5.46.56: The Supreme Sovereign Goddess, her senses stirred, her face flushed from the intoxication of the wine, spoke in a voice deep as thunder-clouds. ॥56॥
5.46.57: The Goddess said: Ho, fool, ho, witless one, why do you persist in vain obstinacy? No asuras whatsoever in the three worlds can stand before me. ॥57॥
5.46.58: The sage said: Having spoken thus, the Goddess who embodies all the arts leapt up, pressed down the asura with her foot, and pierced him in the throat with her fierce trident. ॥58॥
5.46.59: Then, pinned under her foot, he came only half-way out of his own mouth, held fast by the Goddess's power. ॥59॥
5.46.60: That great wretch, still fighting though only half emerged, had his head cut off by her great sword and was felled to the ground. ॥60॥
5.46.61: Then his troops, crying out Alas! Alas! with faces downcast, fled from the battlefield in terror, calling, Save us, save us. ॥61॥
5.46.62: Then all the gods headed by Indra praised the Goddess; the gandharvas sang loudly and the troupes of dancers danced. ॥62॥
5.46.63: Thus, O king, the manifestation of Mahālakṣmī has been told to you; now hear, with a composed mind, the origin of Sarasvatī. ॥63॥
5.46.iti: Thus ends the forty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the incarnation of Mahālakṣmī, in the account of the slaying of Mahiṣāsura, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥46॥
5.47.1: The sage said: There was a demon, the Daitya Śumbha, and his brother the mighty Niśumbha. By these two brothers the three worlds, with all that moves and does not move, were overrun through their power. ॥1॥
5.47.2: Sorely oppressed by those two, the gods went to the Himālaya and bowed to the Mother of all beings, the giver of desires. ॥2॥
5.47.3: The gods said: Victory to you, O Durgā, O Great Ruler! Victory, O you who love your own people! Salutations again and again to you, Śivā, who protect the three worlds. ॥3॥
5.47.4: Salutation to the giver of liberation; salutations again and again to the Supreme Mother. Salutation to you who bring about the origin, maintenance and end of the whole of worldly existence. ॥4॥
5.47.5: Salutation to you who take the form of Kālikā; salutation to you of the form of Tārā. Salutation be to you, who have the nature of Chinnamastā, to Śrīvidyā. ॥5॥
5.47.6: O Bhuvaneśī, salutation to you; salutation to you of the form of Bhairavī. Salutation be to Bagalāmukhī; salutations again and again to Dhūmāvatī. ॥6॥
5.47.7: Salutation to Tripurasundarī; salutations again and again to you, Mātaṅgī. Salutation to you, the Unconquered; salutations again and again to Vijayā. ॥7॥
5.47.8: Salutations again and again to you, Jayā, Maṅgalā, Vilāsinī. Salutation to you whose form is the milch-cow granting all; salutation be to you of terrible form. ॥8॥
5.47.9: Salutation to you of invincible form; salutations again and again to you of eternal form. Salutations again and again to you, Rudrāṇī, protector of those who come for refuge. ॥9॥
5.47.10: Salutation to her who is known through Vedānta; salutation to you, the Supreme Self. Salutations again and again to the sovereign of endless crores of cosmic eggs. ॥10॥
5.47.11: Thus praised by the gods, Gaurī, the auspicious Śivā, pleased and granting boons, said to all the gods: Who is being praised here by you? ॥11॥
5.47.12: Then from Gaurī's body a maiden appeared, and while they looked on she spoke with great reverence to Śiva's Śakti: ॥12॥
5.47.13: O Mother, this hymn to me is being offered by all the dwellers of heaven, who are oppressed by the mighty Daityas Niśumbha and Śumbha. ॥13॥
5.47.14: Because she came forth from the sheath (kośa) of her body, she is therefore celebrated by the name Kauśikī—she who is in person the slayer of the demon Śumbha. ॥14॥
5.47.15: She is also called Ugratārikā and Mahogratārikā; and because she manifested thus, she is called Mātaṅgī on earth. ॥15॥
5.47.16: She said to all the gods: Remain free of fear. I shall accomplish your task—I am independent and need no support. ॥16॥
5.47.17: Having said this, the Goddess quickly vanished. But Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the two servants of those demon brothers, saw that Goddess. ॥17॥
5.47.18: Seeing her enchanting form, a delight to the eyes, the two fell to the ground, senseless and infatuated. ॥18॥
5.47.19: Going back, they told the king the whole story from the beginning: O king, I have seen a captivating woman such as never was before. ॥19॥
5.47.20: She is seated on a lovely peak of the Himālaya, riding a lion, attended on all sides by divine maidens with folded hands. ॥20॥
5.47.21: One massages her feet, another dresses her hair; one massages her hands, another has applied collyrium to her eyes. ॥21॥
5.47.22: One, taking a mirror in her hand, shows her her face; another offers betel leaf mixed with cloves, cardamom and the like. ॥22॥
5.47.23: One companion stands before her holding a spittoon in her hand; another adorns all her limbs with ornaments, garments and the like. ॥23॥
5.47.24: Her shanks and thighs are like plantain stems, her nose like a parrot's, her creeper-like arms like serpents; her feet bear tinkling anklets, and she wears a lovely girdle. ॥24॥
5.47.25: Her breasts sway with a pearl necklace fragrant with gleaming musk; her neck shines with a collar; she is graceful and adorned with garlands. ॥25॥
5.47.26: The goddess bears the half-moon and wears jewelled earrings; she has a lovely braid, large eyes, and is adorned with three eyes. ॥26॥
5.47.27: She holds a rosary of letters; bracelets shine on her wrists; her fingers bear golden rings, and her hands gleam with bright armlets. ॥27॥
5.47.28: Fair Gaurī is clad in white garments, resplendent in the lotus posture, with a tilaka dot of saffron and her head adorned with the moon. ॥28॥
5.47.29: She has the radiance of lightning; her breasts rise high under a bodice of priceless cloth; with eight lofty arms she holds excellent weapons. ॥29॥
5.47.30: No Asura woman, no Nāga woman, no Gandharva woman, no Dānava woman exists in the three worlds such as that charming one is. ॥30॥
5.47.31: Therefore her fitness for enjoyment befits you alone, for she is the jewel among women and you, lord, are the jewel among men. ॥31॥
5.47.32: Hearing what Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa said, that great demon sent a messenger named Sugrīva to her. ॥32॥
5.47.33: Go, messenger, to the snowy mountain; some beautiful woman dwells there. Tell her my words and bring her with all effort. ॥33॥
5.47.34: Thus instructed by him, Sugrīva, foremost of Dānavas, went to the Himālaya and spoke to Maheśvarī, the Mother of the world. ॥34॥
5.47.35: The messenger said: O Goddess, the demon Śumbha is a Daitya, and Niśumbha is his younger brother; he is famed in the three worlds, of great strength and valour. ॥35॥
5.47.36: I am a messenger sent by him; I have come into your presence. O Sovereign of the gods, hear now what he has said. ॥36॥
5.47.37: Having conquered Indra and the others in battle, I carried off their jewels. I myself enjoy the gods' share given in sacrifice by the gods and others. ॥37॥
5.47.38: I regard you as the jewel among women, standing above all jewels. Let you, such as you are, enjoy me or my younger brother with the delights born of love. ॥38॥
5.47.39: Hearing these words spoken by Śumbha and conveyed by the messenger, she, the Great Māyā, beloved as life to the Lord of beings, replied: ॥39॥
5.47.40: The Goddess said: You speak the truth, O messenger; nothing false is being said. But I made a certain vow long ago—learn it from me. ॥40॥
5.47.41: He who shakes off my pride, he who conquers me in battle, him alone am I willing to make my husband, and no other; this is certain. ॥41॥
5.47.42: So you tell Śumbha and Niśumbha my words; let him then do here whatever is fitting. ॥42॥
5.47.43: Having heard these words of the Goddess, the dānava named Sugrīva went there and reported them to the king in full detail. ॥43॥
5.47.44: Then, having heard what the messenger said, Śumbha of terrible command, full of anger, spoke to Dhūmrākṣa, his general, the foremost of the mighty. ॥44॥
5.47.45: O Dhūmrākṣa, on the snowy mountain there is a certain beautiful woman. Go quickly and bring her, so that she will indeed come here. ॥45॥
5.47.46: In bringing her you need have no fear, O best of asuras; if she wishes to fight, battle must be waged with effort. ॥46॥
5.47.47: Thus instructed, the daitya called Dhūmralocana went to the Himālaya and spoke to the Ruler of the worlds, born of a portion of Umā. ॥47॥
5.47.48: Go to my master's presence; otherwise I, accompanied by a force of thousands of asuras, will kill you, O fair-hipped one. ॥48॥
5.47.49: The Goddess said: You have been sent by the king of the daityas, O hero; if you kill me, what can I do to you? But I consider going with you impossible without a battle. ॥49॥
5.47.50: Addressed thus, the dānava Dhūmralocana ran at her; with the mere utterance of huṃ Maheśvarī burned him up. ॥50॥
5.47.51: From then on that Goddess is called Dhūmāvatī on earth; when worshipped, she cuts down the host of enemies of her devotees. ॥51॥
5.47.52: When Dhūmrākṣa had been slain by the Goddess, his troops were chewed up by her furious mount; those who remained all fled. ॥52॥
5.47.53: Hearing that the daitya had thus been slain by the Goddess, the mighty Śumbha became greatly enraged, biting both his lips. ॥53॥
5.47.54: He dispatched in succession the asuras Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa and Raktabīja; and those daityas, so commanded, went to where Ambikā stood. ॥54॥
5.47.55: Seeing the Blessed Goddess mounted on the lion, attended by the powers Aṇimā and the rest, illuminating the directions with her radiance, the chief dānavas spoke. ॥55॥
5.47.56: O Goddess, go quickly into the presence of Śumbha and Niśumbha; otherwise we shall kill you together with your attendants and your mount. ॥56॥
5.47.57: Choose as husband him who is praised by the world-guardians and others, O lovely one; you will attain great bliss, hard to obtain even for the gods. ॥57॥
5.47.58: Having heard what was said, the Mother, the Supreme Goddess, smiled, and that Goddess uttered true and gracious words. ॥58॥
5.47.59: The Goddess said: Maheśāna is without a second, the supreme Brahman, Sadāśiva, whose true nature even the Vedas do not know; what then to speak of Viṣṇu and the others? ॥59॥
5.47.60: I am his subtle Prakṛti; how could I choose another husband? A lioness, even when tormented by desire, never chooses a jackal. ॥60॥
5.47.61: Nor does a she-elephant choose a donkey, nor a leopardess a hare. You speak falsely, O daityas, bound by the serpent of death. ॥61॥
5.47.62: Go to Pātāla, or fight, if you have the power. Hearing these anger-provoking words, they said to one another: ॥62॥
5.47.63: Considering you in our minds a weak woman, we do not kill you. But if there is desire for battle in your mind, then come, firm upon your lion. ॥63॥
5.47.64: As they quarreled thus, the strife grew; sharp arrows rained down in the battle from both sides. ॥64॥
5.47.65: Having thus fought with them in sport, the Supreme Goddess slew the great asura Raktabīja together with Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa. ॥65॥
5.47.66: Even though they had harboured hostile minds, these enemies of the gods in the end attained the supreme world, the world to which her own people go. ॥66॥
5.47.iti: Thus ends the forty-seventh adhyāya, named The slaying of Dhūmralocana, Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa and Raktabīja, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥47॥
5.48.1: The king said: O lord, having heard that Dhūmrākṣa, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, and likewise the demon Raktabīja had been slain by the Goddess, Śumbha, the tormentor of the gods, ॥1॥
5.48.2: what did he do then, O brahmin? Tell me this now, to me who am eager to hear the sin-destroying story of the Source of the world. ॥2॥
5.48.3: The sage said: O king, having heard that these foremost Daityas were slain, the great demon of formidable valour commanded his own hosts, hard to withstand, in whom delight arose at the mere utterance of the word battle. ॥3॥
5.48.4: Let those born of the Kālaka lineage, endowed with strength, assembled at my command in hope of victory, together with the Kālakeya, Maurya and Daurhṛda asuras, and others too, quickly march forth. ॥4॥
5.48.5: Having instructed those Daityas, Niśumbha and Śumbha, mounted on chariots, went forth. The armies following those two mighty ones rose up from the earth like moths bound for destruction. ॥5॥
5.48.6: The army had the mṛdaṅga and mardala drums sounded, together with bherī, ḍiṇḍima, jharjhara and ānaka drums. On the battlefield the lovers of battle rejoiced, while those who loved their lives fled from the fight. ॥6॥
5.48.7: Then those warriors, clad in battle-garments, of flawless bodies, reached the battlefield, bearing masses of weapons and missiles, fiercely contending with one another out of desire for victory. ॥7॥
5.48.8: Some asuras mounted on elephants, some riding horses, and others mounted on chariots, not distinguishing their own people from the enemy, joyfully threw themselves into the battle in the company of the lord of the asuras. ॥8॥
5.48.9: The roar produced by the śataghnīs arose again and again, and by it the gods were shaken. A great darkness spread across the sky; the disc of the sun's chariot could not be seen. ॥9॥
5.48.10: Foot-soldiers marched forth by crores, full of pride and eager for victory; and other asuras, riding chariots, horses and elephants, went out joyfully — how many crores of them. ॥10॥
5.48.11: Rutting elephants, like dark mountains, spread their trumpeting cries over the battle; and camels too, resembling small hills, sent forth gurgling sounds from their throats. ॥11॥
5.48.12: And the horses neighed — bred in lofty lands, wearing large neck-ornaments, skilled in their paces; planting their hooves on the heads of elephants, they flew along the path of the sky like birds. ॥12॥
5.48.13: Seeing the enemy's army thus rushing upon her, Ambikā then strung her bow; she rang the bell that brings dismay to foes, and the lion too roared, shaking its mane. ॥13॥
5.48.14: Then Niśumbha, seeing Śivā standing on the snowy mountain with lovely ornaments and weapons, spoke words full of sentiment, like one well versed in the moods of amorous women. ॥14॥
5.48.15: For ladies like you, even a jasmine petal strewn upon your lovely body surely causes pain. How then, O great Goddess, will you wage a terrible battle with that very charming body? ॥15॥
5.48.16: Having uttered these words the great demon fell silent. Caṇḍikā said to him: Why do you prattle in vain, foolish asura? Give battle — or else go to the abode of the Nāgas. ॥16॥
5.48.17: Then the great chariot-warrior, exceedingly enraged, poured a wondrous rain of volleys of arrows in battle, as dense clouds rain water — as if the rainy season had then come to the battlefield. ॥17॥
5.48.18: He fought with sharp arrows, with tridents and axes, with bhindipālas, iron bars and bows, with the weapons called bhuśuṇḍī, prāsa and kṣurapra, and with great swords, alongside warriors arrogant with pride. ॥18॥
5.48.19: In that battle great elephants, like dark mountains, with their frontal globes split, staggered about; and the standards of Śumbha and Niśumbha, white as moving cranes, were left without flags and without supports. ॥19॥
5.48.20: Daityas with bodies split open like fish, and terrifying horses with severed necks, were made lifeless by Kālikā in battle; other asuras were turned into flesh for food by the lion. ॥20॥
5.48.21: Meanwhile streams carrying blood flowed forth; the river there overflowed with heaps of the slain. The warriors' hair was like water-moss, and their upper garments resembled white foam. ॥21॥
5.48.22: Horseman fell upon horseman, elephant-riders upon those on elephants, chariot-warrior upon chariot-lord, foot-soldier upon foot-soldiers: a great fight between evenly matched opponents took place. ॥22॥
5.48.23: Then Niśumbha reflected in his heart: This terrible time has now arrived. Through adverse time even a poor man may become very rich, and a very rich man poor. ॥23॥
5.48.24: A dullard may become of broad intellect, and a great intellect a dullard; a cruel man laden with faults may be praised. The very mighty meet defeat in battle, and the weak win at the front of combat. ॥24॥
5.48.25: Victory or defeat comes to embodied beings effortlessly, by the will of the Supreme Lord alone. Not even Maheśvara, the Lotus-born or the Lord of Ramā could live by overstepping Time. ॥25॥
5.48.26: Having come to the front of battle, heroes do not in their hearts regard flight as right. But how can there be victory in battle against her, by whom my entire army has been destroyed? ॥26॥
5.48.27: Surely she has come to accomplish the gods' purpose and to crush the Daitya army — she is the primeval form, the supreme Prakṛti, Śivā; she is by no means an ordinary worldly woman. ॥27॥
5.48.28: Even death dealt by a woman is proclaimed dishonourable by those eager to taste the relish of battle. Yet, without fighting, how shall we show our face in the presence of the asura king? ॥28॥
5.48.29: Having reflected thus, the great warrior mounted a mighty chariot urged on by its charioteer and went swiftly to where the consort of Maheśvara stood, whose blossoming youth is coveted by celestial women. ॥29॥
5.48.30: He said to her: O great Goddess, what is gained by slaying these warriors who live on wages? If you wish to fight, then let there be battle with us two, clad in fine battle-garments. ॥30॥
5.48.31: Then Kauśikī said to Kālī: Behold the obstinacy of these two. When calamity approaches, Time, the impeller of good and evil, gives the mind a perverse turn. ॥31॥
5.48.32: Then Niśumbha struck Caṇḍikā with thousands of arrows, and Kālikā likewise. Śivā shattered the arrows shot by the asura into a thousand pieces with volleys of her own arrows. ॥32॥
5.48.33: Then, raising a gleaming sword along with a shield, he struck the lion on the head. Ambikā split that sword with her great sword, as woodcutters split a tree with an axe. ॥33॥
5.48.34: His sword broken, he drove an arrow into the breast of the supreme Ambikā; that too was cut down. Again he hurled a trident at her heart; that too she pulverized with a blow of her fist. ॥34॥
5.48.35: Taking up a mace, the great warrior asura, facing death, again rushed at Ambā. She crushed that too with the edge of her trident; and again the trident he raised was split by another stroke. ॥35॥
5.48.36: Then Ambikā, with her own sharp arrows, like terrible serpents, fit for sucking the blood of the gods' enemies and smeared with poison, struck Niśumbha down and brought him to the ground. ॥36॥
5.48.37: When his younger brother of immeasurable strength had been felled, the lord of the asuras, filled with fury, standing in his chariot and equipped with eight arms, went to where the beloved of Maheśa was. ॥37॥
5.48.38: Then the Goddess blew her foe-subduing conch and made the unbearable twang of her bow; the lion too roared, shaking its mane, and the sky resounded with the three sounds. ॥38॥
5.48.39: Then the Mother of the world let out a loud laugh, and by it all the enemies of the gods were terrified. The gods then cried out Victory! when Ambikā said: Stand firm in battle. ॥39॥
5.48.40: That Daitya king hurled a great spear with blazing flames, and it was struck down by her meteor-like missile. Śivā split the arrows sent by Śumbha, and he too split a thousandfold the arrows shot by Śivā. ॥40॥
5.48.41: Caṇḍikā raised her trident and struck that great asura; he fell unconscious, like a mountain whose wings have been severed by Hari (Indra), shaking the sky and the earth together with the ocean. ॥41॥
5.48.42: Then, having endured the pain caused by the trident, the mighty one, creating ten thousand arms, struck Kālikā, the great Goddess mounted on her lion, with discuses that bring destruction to the immortals. ॥42॥
5.48.43: Then, playfully shattering his discuses, Śivā raised her trident and struck him; and the two brothers, having met death from the world-purifying lotus-hand of Śivā, attained the supreme state. ॥43॥
5.48.44: When that greatly valiant Niśumbha of terrible prowess, and Śumbha, were slain, all the daityas entered the abode of Bali (the netherworld). ॥44॥
5.48.45: Others among the enemies of the gods were devoured by Kālī, the lion and the rest; and still others fled in the ten directions, stricken with fear. ॥45॥
5.48.46: The rivers flowed along their courses with clear water; pleasant-touching breezes blew; the sky became spotless. ॥46॥
5.48.47: The sacrifice was begun again by the gods and the brahmarṣis, and all the dwellers of heaven, headed by the great Indra, became happy. ॥47॥
5.48.48: O lord, whoever with faith repeatedly studies this supremely pure and meritorious account of Umā, containing the slaying of the daitya kings— ॥48॥
5.48.49: he, having enjoyed here all pleasures, hard to obtain even for the gods, would go hereafter to Umā's abode through the grace of Mahāmāyā. ॥49॥
5.48.50: The sage said: Thus arose the Goddess, slayer of the asura Śumbha; she is called Sarasvatī, manifested directly from a portion of Umā, O king. ॥50॥
5.48.iti: Thus ends the forty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of the appearance of Sarasvatī, in the account of the slaying of Niśumbha and Śumbha, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥48॥
5.49.1: The sages said: O Sūta, best knower of all matters, narrate the incarnation of Umā, the sovereign of the worlds, from whom Sarasvatī was born, ॥1॥
5.49.2: she who is celebrated as the supreme Brahman, the root Prakṛti, the sovereign Goddess; formless yet possessing form, eternal, full of bliss, the true one. ॥2॥
5.49.3: Sūta said: O ascetics, listen with love to this supreme and great account, by merely understanding which a man attains the highest goal. ॥3॥
5.49.4: Once there was a war between the gods and the demons against each other; through the power of Mahāmāyā, victory came to the immortals. ॥4॥
5.49.5: Then the immortals, puffed up with pride, spread their own praise: We are blessed, we are blessed! What can the demons do to us? ॥5॥
5.49.6: They, having seen our utterly unbearable might, went in fear to the abode of the Nāgas, crying, Flee, flee. ॥6॥
5.49.7: Ah, what strength! Ah, what splendour, destroying the race of the Daityas! Ah, the good fortune of the gods! Thus they all extolled themselves. ॥7॥
5.49.8: Then, at that very moment, a radiance appeared in the form of a towering mass; seeing that never-before-seen thing, the gods were astonished. ॥8॥
5.49.9: With choked throats they said, What is this? What is this? — not knowing the supreme power of Śyāmā, the breaker of pride. ॥9॥
5.49.10: Then the overlord of the gods commanded the gods: Go, you, and examine truly what this is. ॥10॥
5.49.11: Urged by the lord of the gods, Vāyu went near the radiance; and that radiance, addressing him, said to him, Who are you, sir? ॥11॥
5.49.12: Thus questioned then by that exceedingly mighty radiance, Vāyu, full of pride, said this: I am Vāyu, the life-breath of the world. ॥12॥
5.49.13: This whole world, moving and unmoving, is woven warp and woof in me alone, the support of all; I set the entire world in motion. ॥13॥
5.49.14: Then the great radiance said: If you are capable of moving things, O Vāyu, move this blade of grass placed here, by your own will. ॥14॥
5.49.15: Then the ever-moving one (Vāyu) strove with all his effort; when it did not move from its place, he became ashamed. ॥15॥
5.49.16: Falling silent, Vāyu then went to Indra's assembly and related what had happened, including his own defeat: ॥16॥
5.49.17: We all falsely imagine lordship over everything in ourselves; we are unable to do anything even to a trifling object. ॥17॥
5.49.18: Then Indra (Marutvān) sent all the gods; when they could not know it, Indra himself went. ॥18॥
5.49.19: Then, seeing Maghavan (Indra) approaching, the utterly unbearable radiance at once vanished, and Vāsava was astonished. ॥19॥
5.49.20: I take refuge in him alone whose deeds are such: thus the thousand-eyed Indra reflected again and again. ॥20॥
5.49.21: Meanwhile, there, Śiva's consort, whose very body is guileless compassion, in order to bestow grace on them and to take away their pride, ॥21॥
5.49.22: on the ninth day of the bright half of Caitra, when the sun stood at midday, the goddess Umā, whose form is being-consciousness-bliss, manifested. ॥22॥
5.49.23: Shining in the midst of the radiance, illuminating the directions with her lustre, clearly making all the gods understand: I alone am Brahman. ॥23॥
5.49.24: Holding in her four hands the gesture of granting boons, the noose, the goad and the gesture of fearlessness, served by the Vedas, lovely, proud in fresh youth; ॥24॥
5.49.25: clad in red garments, with red garlands and unguents, resembling ten million Kandarpas, with radiance equal to ten million moons, ॥25॥
5.49.26: Mahāmāyā, the inner controller of all, the witness of all beings, whose own nature is the supreme Brahman, spoke: ॥26॥
5.49.27: Umā said: Neither Brahmā, nor the foe of Mura (Viṣṇu), nor the Lord, the foe of the Cities (Śiva), can be proud in the least before me — what then to speak of the other gods? ॥27॥
5.49.28: I am the supreme Brahman, the supreme light, having the form of the twofold praṇava; I alone am everything; there is no one other than me. ॥28॥
5.49.29: Though formless, I have form; I am the essence of all principles, of unfathomable qualities, eternal, the form of both effect and cause. ॥29॥
5.49.30: Sometimes in the form of a beloved woman, sometimes in male form, sometimes in the form of both — I, the sovereign, am of all forms. ॥30॥
5.49.31: I am Viriñci (Brahmā), the creator; I am Acyuta, the protector of the world; I am Rudra, the destroyer; I am the enchantress of the whole universe. ॥31॥
5.49.32: All the powers headed by Kālikā, Kamalā and Vāṇī are indeed born from a portion of me alone, and so are all these digits. ॥32॥
5.49.33: By my power you conquered all the sons of Diti; not knowing me as such, you vainly consider yourselves lords of all. ॥33॥
5.49.34: Just as a conjurer makes a wooden doll dance, so I, the sovereign, make all beings dance. ॥34॥
5.49.35: From fear of me the wind blows, the oblation-eater (Agni) burns everything, and the guardians of the worlds ceaselessly perform their respective duties. ॥35॥
5.49.36: Sometimes for the hosts of gods, sometimes for the sons of Diti, I, independent, bring about victory fully, by my own play. ॥36॥
5.49.37: The imperishable supreme abode, beyond Māyā, higher than the highest, which the Vedas describe — that form is mine alone. ॥37॥
5.49.38: My form is held to be twofold, with qualities and without qualities: the one is mingled with Māyā, the second is not dependent on it. ॥38॥
5.49.39: Knowing me thus, O gods, abandon each your own pride and, filled with love, worship me, the eternal Prakṛti. ॥39॥
5.49.40: Hearing these words of the Goddess, pregnant with compassion, the gods, their necks bowed in devotion, praised the supreme Goddess: ॥40॥
5.49.41: Forgive us, O Mistress of the world; be gracious, O supreme Goddess. May such pride never again be ours, O Mother; show us mercy. ॥41॥
5.49.42: From then on, those gods, having abandoned their pride and with collected minds, worshipped Umā as before, according to the prescribed rites. ॥42॥
5.49.43: Thus, O brahmins, I have narrated to you the manifestation of Umā, by merely hearing which one attains the supreme state. ॥43॥
5.49.iti: Thus ends the forty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the appearance of Umā, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥49॥
5.50.1: The sages said: We all wish to hear the deeds of Durgā day after day. O most wise one, describe to us yet another wonderful truth about her. ॥1॥
5.50.2: As we listen to the many nectar-like stories from your lotus mouth, our mind is not satisfied, O Sūta, best of the knowers of all matters. ॥2॥
5.50.3: Sūta said: The mighty son of Ruru, known by the name Durgama, obtained the four Vedas through a boon granted by Brahmā. ॥3॥
5.50.4: Having also obtained a strength unconquerable by the gods, he wrought many calamities on the surface of the earth, and in heaven the gods trembled. ॥4॥
5.50.5: When the Vedas were lost, all rites were indeed lost; and the brāhmaṇas, along with the gods, then became of evil conduct. ॥5॥
5.50.6: There was no giving of gifts, no fierce austerity, no sacrifice, no oblation at all. Then a drought lasting a hundred years arose on the earth. ॥6॥
5.50.7: There was a great cry of distress in the three worlds; all people became miserable, sorely afflicted by hunger and thirst. ॥7॥
5.50.8: Rivers and oceans, step-wells, wells and lakes all became waterless; trees and creepers withered completely. ॥8॥
5.50.9: Then, seeing the great suffering of the dejected creatures, the gods went for refuge to Yogamāyā, the great Goddess. ॥9॥
5.50.10: The gods said: Protect, protect all your own creatures, O Mahāmāyā. Surely withdraw your anger, otherwise the worlds will perish. ॥10॥
5.50.11: Just as the demon Śumbha was slain, and mighty Niśumbha, Dhūmrākṣa, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, and the mighty Raktabīja, ॥11॥
5.50.12: the demon Kaiṭabha together with Madhu, and Mahiṣāsura too—in the same way, O ocean of compassion, friend of the afflicted, slay this one quickly. ॥12॥
5.50.13: Children commit faults at every step; who in the world bears with them except the mother alone? ॥13॥
5.50.14: Whenever suffering has come upon the gods and likewise the brāhmaṇas, then you swiftly descend and make the people happy. ॥14॥
5.50.15: Hearing their lament thus, the compassionate one then revealed a form made of endless eyes. ॥15॥
5.50.16: She held in her four hands a bow and arrow, a lotus, and various roots and fruits, her lotus face serene. ॥16॥
5.50.17: Then, seeing the creatures tormented, her eyes filled with compassion, she wept, deeply moved, for nine days and nine nights. ॥17॥
5.50.18: From her eyes she released streams of water by the thousands; by them the worlds and all the plants were refreshed. ॥18॥
5.50.19: The rivers and the oceans too became full of fathomless water; and vegetables, roots and fruits sprang up on the surface of the earth. ॥19॥
5.50.20: She distributed the fruits held in her hands to the gods, lovely grasses to the cows, and likewise to others according to what befitted them. ॥20॥
5.50.21: All became content—gods, twice-born and humans. Then the Goddess said: What else shall I do for you? ॥21॥
5.50.22: Then the gods, gathering together, said: The people have been gladdened by you. Show compassion and give back the Vedas that were seized by Durgama. ॥22॥
5.50.23: Saying, so be it, she said: Go, go to your own abodes; I shall give you back the Vedas before long. ॥23॥
5.50.24: Then the delighted gods, having bowed deeply to the source of the world whose eyes were like full-blown blue lotuses, went each to his own abode. ॥24॥
5.50.25: Then a tumult arose in heaven, on earth and in the sky. Hearing it, Raurava (the son of Ruru) at once besieged the city on all sides. ॥25॥
5.50.26: Then Śivā, having set up a fiery circle all around for the protection of the gods, herself went out from it. ॥26॥
5.50.27: Then a battle took place between the two, the Goddess and the demon; in the fight they rained sharp arrows that pierced armour. ॥27॥
5.50.28: Meanwhile, from her body there came forth beautiful forms: Kālī, Tārā, Chinnamastā, Śrīvidyā, Bhuvaneśvarī, ॥28॥
5.50.29: Bhairavī, Bagalā, Dhūmrā, the glorious Tripurasundarī, and Mātaṅgī—these ten Mahāvidyās came forth bearing weapons. ॥29॥
5.50.30: Then countless Mothers of divine form arose, all bearing the crescent moon, all with a radiance like lightning. ॥30॥
5.50.31: Then a terrifying battle began with the hosts of Mothers; by them the army of Raurava, a hundred akṣauhiṇīs, was slain. ॥31॥
5.50.32: Then she struck the demon Durgama with the edge of her trident; he fell upon the earth like a tree whose roots have been dug out. ॥32॥
5.50.33: Having thus slain the demon named Durgāsura, the Goddess took the four Vedas and gave them to the gods. ॥33॥
5.50.34: The gods said: For our sake you assumed a form made of endless eyes; therefore, O Ambikā, the sages will celebrate you as Śatākṣī ('Hundred-eyed'). ॥34॥
5.50.35: Since the worlds were sustained by vegetables born from your own body, your name will be renowned as Śākambharī. ॥35॥
5.50.36: Since the great demon named Durgama was slain by you, O Śivā, people will therefore call you Durgā, the blessed and auspicious one. ॥36॥
5.50.37: O Yoganidrā, salutation to you; salutation be to you, O mighty one; salutation to you, giver of knowledge; to the Mother of the universe, salutation again and again. ॥37॥
5.50.38: To the Supreme Goddess who is made known through sayings such as Tat tvam asi (That thou art), the sovereign of endless crores of cosmic eggs, salutation again and again. ॥38॥
5.50.39: O Mother, we who are ignorant of your power are unable to praise you, who are hard to reach by speech, mind and body, and whose eyes are the sun, moon and fire. ॥39॥
5.50.40: Seeing gods such as us, who would show such compassion, apart from the sovereign of the gods, Mother Śatākṣī? ॥40॥
5.50.41: Act so that the three worlds are not continually overwhelmed by afflictions. In this way you should make an effort toward the destruction of our enemies. ॥41॥
5.50.42: The Goddess said: Just as cows, on seeing their calves, run eagerly and swiftly to them, so too I, on seeing you, run to you, being deeply stirred. ॥42॥
5.50.43: For me, who regard you as my children and would give even my life for you, a single moment of not seeing you passes like an age. ॥43॥
5.50.44: You who are rich in devotion should have no anxiety at all, while I remain present for you, removing your calamities. ॥44॥
5.50.45: Just as the Daityas were slain before, so shall I slay the Asuras. No doubt should be entertained about this; I speak the truth, the truth. ॥45॥
5.50.46: When Śumbha and Niśumbha, two other Daityas, come into being, then I, full of glory, shall be born of Yaśodā, the wife of Nanda, ॥46॥
5.50.47: assuming a womb-born form, I shall be born in the cowherds' settlement (Gokula). I shall slay those two Asuras; therefore they will call me Nandajā (born of Nanda). ॥47॥
5.50.48: Since I shall slay Aruṇa having assumed the form of a bee, people in the world will celebrate me as Bhrāmarī. ॥48॥
5.50.49: When, again taking on a terrible form, I devour the Rākṣasas, then my name will become renowned as Bhīmā Devī. ॥49॥
5.50.50: Whenever affliction arising from the Asuras thus occurs on earth, then each time I shall descend and bring about welfare, without doubt. ॥50॥
5.50.51: The goddess who is remembered as Śatākṣī is likewise regarded as Śākambharī; she alone is proclaimed as Durgā. The person is one and the same in all three. ॥51॥
5.50.52: There is no deity on earth as compassionate as Śatākṣī — the Great Goddess who, seeing the creatures in distress, wept for nine days. ॥52॥
5.50.iti: Thus ends the fiftieth adhyāya, named The description of the incarnations of Śatākṣī and others, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥50॥
5.51.1: The sages said: O disciple of Vyāsa, O greatly fortunate Sūta, best of the Purāṇa-reciters, we wish to hear some further narrative concerning the Ruler (īśitṛ), ॥1॥
5.51.2: namely the unsurpassed kriyāyoga of Umā, the Mother of the world, which was told by Sanatkumāra to the great-souled Vyāsa. ॥2॥
5.51.3: Sūta said: Blessed are you, great souls, firm in your vow of devotion to the Goddess. Hear with reverence the supreme, hidden secret of the Parāśakti. ॥3॥
5.51.4: Vyāsa said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing son of Brahmā, of great intellect, I wish to hear the most wondrous kriyāyoga of Umā. ॥4॥
5.51.5: What is its characteristic, and what fruit arises when it is performed? And what is dear to the Supreme Mother—tell me all of that completely. ॥5॥
5.51.6: Sanatkumāra said: O Dvaipāyana, this secret about which you inquire—hear it all, O greatly wise one, from me as I describe it. ॥6॥
5.51.7: Jñānayoga, kriyāyoga and likewise bhaktiyoga—these three paths of the revered Mother are declared, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation. ॥7॥
5.51.8: Jñānayoga is the union of the mind with the Self; but the union with external objects is called kriyāyoga. ॥8॥
5.51.9: Bhaktiyoga is held to be the contemplation of the oneness of the Goddess and oneself. Among all three yogas, that foundational one is called kriyāyoga. ॥9॥
5.51.10: From action devotion arises; from devotion knowledge arises; from knowledge liberation arises—this is the settled conclusion in the scriptures. ॥10॥
5.51.11: Yoga is the principal cause of liberation, O best of sages; and kriyāyoga is the supreme means of attaining the object of yogic meditation. ॥11॥
5.51.12: One should know Māyā to be Prakṛti and the possessor of Māyā to be the eternal Brahman; knowing their form as non-different, one is released from the bondage of worldly existence. ॥12॥
5.51.13: Whoever builds a temple of the Goddess, of stone or likewise of wood, or of clay, O son of Kālī, hear the meritorious fruit of that. The great fruit accruing to one who worships with yoga day after day— ॥13॥
5.51.14: —that fruit he obtains who has a temple of the Goddess built. A thousand generations of his family yet to come and a thousand past—that righteous one saves, causing an abode of the revered Mother to be built. ॥14॥
5.51.15: Sin committed over ten million births, whether small or great, perishes from the very moment of beginning a temple of the revered Mother. ॥15॥
5.51.16: As the Gaṅgā is foremost among rivers and the Śoṇa among all male rivers, as the earth in forbearance and as the ocean in depth, ॥16॥
5.51.17: and as the sun excels among all the planets, so the revered Supreme Mother excels among all the gods. ॥17॥
5.51.18: She is the chief among all deities; he who has a house built for her attains eminence birth after birth. ॥18॥
5.51.19: In Vārāṇasī, in Kurukṣetra, in Prayāga and likewise Puṣkara, on the shore where the Gaṅgā meets the sea, in Naimiṣa, at Amarakaṇṭaka, ॥19॥
5.51.20: on the most holy Śrīparvata, at Gokarṇa, on Jñānaparvata, in Mathurā, in Ayodhyā and likewise in Dvārāvatī— ॥20॥
5.51.21: in these and other holy regions, or in any place whatsoever, one who has a dwelling of the Mother built is freed from bondage. ॥21॥
5.51.22: For as many years as the arrangement of bricks endures, for so many thousands of years he is honoured in Maṇidvīpa. ॥22॥
5.51.23: Whoever has images made, marked with all the proper characteristics, surely goes without fear to the supreme world of Umā. ॥23॥
5.51.24: Having installed an image of the Goddess at an auspicious season, planetary position and asterism, a mortal becomes fulfilled through the grace of Yogamāyā. ॥24॥
5.51.25: Those men of the family who will be and who have passed, up to the end of the kalpa—all of them he carries across, having installed a beautiful image of the Goddess. ॥25॥
5.51.26: Whatever merit would come from establishing the three worlds, O bull among sages, ten million times that merit comes from installing the revered Goddess. ॥26॥
5.51.27: Whoever, having installed the Goddess in the centre, installs the pañcāyatana deities in the four directions—his merit cannot be counted. ॥27॥
5.51.28: The fruit gained from ten million repetitions of Viṣṇu's names during an eclipse of the moon or sun—a hundred million times greater than that ॥28॥
5.51.29: comes from merely repeating Śiva's name; ten million times greater than that from repeating the name of the revered Goddess; and ten million times greater than that ॥29॥
5.51.30: is the merit obtained from building a temple of the Goddess. He by whom that Goddess, Mother of the world, embodiment of the three Vedas, has been installed— ॥30॥
5.51.31: for him nothing is hard to obtain, by the compassion of the revered Mother. Sons, grandsons and the rest flourish, and all impurity perishes. ॥31॥
5.51.32: Those who even in mind wish to perform the excellent installation of an image, they too go to Umā's supreme world, hard for sages to attain. ॥32॥
5.51.33: Whoever, seeing a temple being built, reflects in his mind, I will have one built when wealth comes to me— ॥33॥
