5.51.34: —thus his family goes at once to heaven, there is no doubt. By the power of Mahāmāyā, what is hard to obtain in the three worlds? ॥34॥
5.51.35: Those who have taken refuge solely in the revered Supreme Mother, source of the world, should not be considered human beings; they are verily the Goddess's own attendants. ॥35॥
5.51.36: Those who, walking, sleeping or standing, day and night utter the two-syllabled name Umā—they are attendants of Śivā. ॥36॥
5.51.37: Those who, in regular and occasional rites, worship the Goddess, the supreme Śivā, with flowers, incense and lamps, will go to the abode of Umā. ॥37॥
5.51.38: Those who daily smear the Goddess's pavilion with cow dung or clay and sweep it will go to the abode of Umā. ॥38॥
5.51.39: Those by whom a charming, unsurpassed temple of the Goddess has been built—to the people of their family the Mother grants blessings. ॥39॥
5.51.40: May my own, the objects of my love, live a hundred years; may no paths of calamity befall them—thus the revered Mother speaks day and night. ॥40॥
5.51.41: He by whom an auspicious image of the great goddess Umā is caused to be made: ten thousand men born in his family are honoured in Maṇidvīpa. ॥41॥
5.51.42: Having installed an image of Mahāmāyā and worshipped it properly, whatever desire the practitioner prays for, that he obtains. ॥42॥
5.51.43: Who could count the fruit of one who bathes the excellent installed image of the holy Mother with ghee mixed with honey? ॥43॥
5.51.44: One should bathe the Supreme Goddess with waters containing sandal, aguru, camphor, spikenard, musta-grass and the like, and with the milk of cows of a single colour. ॥44॥
5.51.45: One should offer an excellent oblation with incense of eighteen ingredients, and perform the waving of lights (nīrājana) for the Goddess with wicks of camphor and ghee. ॥45॥
5.51.46: On the eighth of the dark fortnight, on the ninth, or on the new-moon day, or on the fifteenth lunar day, one should worship the Nurse of the worlds, especially with fragrances and flowers. ॥46॥
5.51.47: Reciting the Jananī-sūkta, or reciting the Śrī-sūkta, or else the Devī-sūkta, or even the root mantra. ॥47॥
5.51.48: Excepting viṣṇukrāntā and tulasī, every flower should be known as pleasing to the Goddess, and the lotus especially. ॥48॥
5.51.49: He who offers a golden flower, or even a silver one, to the Goddess goes to the supreme abode, attended by crores of siddhas. ॥49॥
5.51.50: At the end of worship, the servants of the Goddess must always ask pardon for faults: Be gracious, O Supreme Ruler, giver of joy to the world. ॥50॥
5.51.51: Praising her with such words, the mantra-practitioner, wholly devoted to the Goddess, should meditate on her as mounted on a lion, her hands showing the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures. ॥51॥
5.51.52: Having thus meditated on Maheśānī, who grants devotees the fruits they desire, one should arrange various ripe fruits as the food-offering. ॥52॥
5.51.53: But whoever eats the food-offering of Śambhu's Śakti, the Supreme Self, that man shakes off all impurity and becomes pure. ॥53॥
5.51.54: He who performs the Bhavānī vow on the third day of the bright half of Caitra, freed from the bonds of worldly existence, attains the supreme state. ॥54॥
5.51.55: On this very third day the wise one should hold the swing festival and worship Umā, the Nurse of the worlds, together with Śaṅkara, ॥55॥
5.51.56: with flowers, saffron, garments, camphor, aguru and sandal, incense, lamps, food-offerings, garlands, perfumes and other things too. ॥56॥
5.51.57: Then he should swing the Goddess Mahāmāyā, Maheśvarī, the holy Gaurī united with Śiva, who brings about all welfare. ॥57॥
5.51.58: He who every year on this day performs the vow and likewise the swinging, with discipline—to him Śivā grants everything he wishes. ॥58॥
5.51.59: The third day in the bright half of Mādhava (Vaiśākha) is called Akṣayā. Whoever on it diligently performs the vow of the World-Mother, ॥59॥
5.51.60: and worships Gaurī together with Śaṅkara with flowers of mallikā, mālatī, campā, japā, bandhūka and lotus, ॥60॥
5.51.61: shaking off the sin committed over a crore of births, arising from mind, speech and body, he enjoys here the four imperishable goals of life. ॥61॥
5.51.62: He who on the bright third of Jyeṣṭha performs the vow and worships Maheśvarī with supreme love—for him nothing is unattainable. ॥62॥
5.51.63: On the third day of the bright half of Āṣāḍha one should hold the chariot festival, most dear to the Goddess, according to one's means. ॥63॥
5.51.64: One should regard the chariot as the earth, its wheels as the moon and sun, the horses as the Vedas, and the charioteer as the lotus-born Brahmā. ॥64॥
5.51.65: Having fashioned the chariot thus, studded with clusters of various gems and resplendent with flower garlands, he should install Śivā in it. ॥65॥
5.51.66: The wise man should contemplate: The Supreme Mother is seated in the chariot to protect the world and to behold the world. ॥66॥
5.51.67: As the chariot moves slowly, one should raise the cry of victory: Protect us people who have taken refuge in you, O Goddess, loving to the afflicted. ॥67॥
5.51.68: With such words and the sounds of various instruments he should please her; and having taken the chariot to the boundary, he should worship her there in the chariot. ॥68॥
5.51.69: Then, having praised her with various hymns, he should bring her back to his own house and, making a hundred prostrations, pray to the World-Mother. ॥69॥
5.51.70: The learned one who thus performs the worship, vow and chariot festival, having enjoyed all pleasures here, goes in the end to the Goddess's abode. ॥70॥
5.51.71: Likewise, he who on the bright third of Śrāvaṇa and Bhādrapada performs the vow and worship of the Mother according to rule ॥71॥
5.51.72: rejoices constantly here with sons, grandsons and the like, and with wealth and the like; in the end he goes to Umā's world, which lies above all worlds. ॥72॥
5.51.73: In the bright half of Āśvina one should perform the Navarātra vow, by doing which all desires are fulfilled—there is no doubt. ॥73॥
5.51.74: Neither the four-faced Brahmā, nor the five-faced Śiva, nor the six-faced Skanda, nor anyone else is able to describe the power of this Navarātra vow. ॥74॥
5.51.75: O best of sages, by performing the Navarātra vow, King Suratha, son of Viratha, regained his own kingdom that had been taken away. ॥75॥
5.51.76: The wise King Sudarśana, son of Dhruvasandhi and lord of Ayodhyā, recovered his seized kingdom by its power. ॥76॥
5.51.77: Having performed this king of vows and worshipped Maheśvarī, Samādhi was freed from the bondage of saṃsāra and became a partaker of liberation. ॥77॥
5.51.78: The man who worships the Goddess on the third, fifth, seventh, eighth, ninth or fourteenth lunar day, ॥78॥
5.51.79: having performed the vow according to rule in the bright half of Āśvina—Śivā ceaselessly fulfils all his heart's desires. ॥79॥
5.51.80: He who performs the vow on the third day of the bright half of Kārttika, Mārgaśīrṣa, Pauṣa, Tapas (Māgha) and likewise Tapasya (Phālguna), ॥80॥
5.51.81: One who worships the goddess Maṅgalā with red flowers such as karavīra (oleander) and with fragrant incense obtains every auspicious thing. ॥81॥
5.51.82: Women should always perform this great vow for marital good fortune; men too should undertake it to obtain learning, wealth and sons. ॥82॥
5.51.83: Likewise, the Umā-Maheśvara vow and whatever other vows are dear to the Goddess should be performed with one's own devotion by those seeking liberation. ॥83॥
5.51.84: This Saṃhitā is supremely meritorious, increasing devotion to Śiva, filled with many narratives, auspicious, and bestowing both enjoyment and liberation. ॥84॥
5.51.85: Whoever listens to it with devotion, or attentively causes it to be heard, or reads it, or has it read, attains the supreme goal. ॥85॥
5.51.86: He in whose house this Saṃhitā rests, written in elegant letters and duly worshipped according to rule, would obtain all his desires. ॥86॥
5.51.87: He never has fear from evil beings such as bhūtas, pretas and piśācas; he surely obtains the wealth of sons, grandsons and the like—there is no doubt. ॥87॥
5.51.88: Therefore this delightful, supremely meritorious Umā Saṃhitā should always be heard and recited by those who desire devotion to Śiva. ॥88॥
5.51.iti: Thus ends the fifty-first adhyāya, named The exposition of kriyāyoga, in the fifth saṃhitā, the Umā-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥51॥
